title: [BugFix][Engram] Skip HOST_UVA page migration during CPU binding
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17286.

With Engram HOST_UVA offload, post-warmup CPU binding runs `migratepages` after the large host tables have already been registered and pinned. Migrating the whole worker can stall startup for many minutes, and DP replicas sharing a backing can request different NUMA destinations.

Keep CPU thread and IRQ affinity at the existing post-warmup/post-capture point, but skip process-wide page migration when `engram_config.cpu_offload` is enabled. Move the migration call out of the thread-binding methods so it can be skipped independently. Other configurations retain the existing migration behavior and ordering.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Engram HOST_UVA workloads can keep CPU binding enabled without the process-wide `migratepages` startup stall. No new configuration is required. Shared-table placement and selective page migration are outside this fix.

### How was this patch tested?

- The complete existing CPU-binding and V1 worker unit-test files passed (151 tests). Only existing CPU-binding expectations were updated for the migration call location and argument forwarding. No new test cases were added; mock-only tests cannot reproduce the pinned HOST_UVA page-migration stall, which was validated on hardware as described below.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Standalone validation, Ascend `2cd0042f1`: A3, CANN 9.1, 16 NPUs, TP2/DP8, shared Engram HOST_UVA, async scheduling, DSpark5 with eager draft, and FULL_DECODE_ONLY. All 16 workers completed post-capture affinity binding in 4-7 seconds; 1,257 measured requests succeeded. Two fixed 128-token probes matched the no-binding control exactly in tokens and logprobs. This ran under UID 1000, so IRQ writes were skipped due to permissions.
- Full P/D (1P1D) rerun on this PR head, external DP, Engram HOST_UVA with `{"cpu_offload": true, "dp_shared_memory": true}` and `enable_cpu_binding: true`, single-node TP4/DP4 prefill plus TP2/DP8 decode on 16 NPUs each, V1 runner, DSpark5, decode side on async scheduling with FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Every worker logged `CPU affinity applied without process-wide NUMA page migration.` and no `migratepages` process appeared on either node. Both halves reached ready: prefill in 353.5 s, decode in 475-513 s. Twelve measured `vllm bench serve` runs (128/4096 input, 256 output, concurrency 1/8/32, temperature 0) completed with mean ITL 37.4-50.2 ms and 66-643 output tok/s.
- Control on the PR merge base without this patch, same deployment: the decode half never reached ready. Up to 16 `migratepages` helpers appeared right after graph capture, EngineCore repeatedly reported `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds`, and the helpers were still running more than 45 minutes later, with their target worker stuck in state `D` and `kill -9` having no effect.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Performance] Speed up startup for DeepSeek V4
body:
ISSUE: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/16552
PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16548
Branch: `coldstart` (fork `yanganYNU/vllm-ascend`)
Base: `main` (rebuilt on latest `upstream/main`)

Related:
- 0.27 backport: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17130
- 拉起时间分析 https://gitcode.com/mindie_yangan/Scripts-LLM/blob/main/lep_speed/startup_timing.md
- 冷启动优化方案 https://gitcode.com/mindie_yangan/Scripts-LLM/blob/main/lep_speed/coldstart_plan.md

No Motor-side change is needed for this PR.

## **1. 背景**

Fixes #16552

Large-EP PD (Flash / Pro / GLM and similar). Construct used to scan
~820k quant keys per RMSNorm; warmup JIT'd 16 RMS `BLOCK_M` values;
first NZ format-cast and Triton compile sat after I/O.

## **2. 设计**

Same Flash-best optimizations as the 0.26 PR, ported to the main package
layout. `is_layer_skipped_ascend` is already O(1) on main (#16051), so that
index is not in this PR. Main already maps a missing
`quant_description[prefix + ".weight"]` to unquantized, so the Pro MTP
`mtp.0.head.weight` KeyError on 0.26 does not apply here.

Dropped the old CPU-then-NPU expert path (it hit `Expected NPU tensor` on
Prefill dummy_run). Kept main's current hash-router `tid2eid` table.

Two opt-in prewarm threads, switched in `additional_config.ascend_warmup_config`
and both default to false (review feedback from @yiz-liu and @kunpengW-code):
- `enable_early_nz_warmup`: pays the first NZ format-cast lazy init during I/O.
  It is independent of the quantization scheme, so it lives in
  `model_executor/warmup/nz_warmup.py` with the other startup warmups, not in
  a quant method
- `enable_early_kernel_warmup`: compiles the Triton warmup kernels during I/O

```json
"additional_config": {
    "ascend_warmup_config": {
        "enable_early_kernel_warmup": true,
        "enable_early_nz_warmup": true
    }
}
```

`NPUModelRunner.load_model` starts both threads before `get_model()` and
joins them before it returns, so every model can use them and neither
overlaps memory profiling or KV cache allocation.

The MTP embed-table skip from the 0.26 PR is not included. DeepSeek V4 always
has `compress_ratios`, so that branch never ran (review feedback from
@Angazenn).

No loader default is changed. The netloader disk fallback used to drop the
whole `model_loader_extra_config`, which silently disabled the user's
multithread load; it now carries the keys `DefaultModelLoader` accepts and
drops only the netloader-only ones. Thread-count defaults stay with vLLM
(review feedback from @nu11ptr7).

## **3. 修改内容**

### 3.1 修改清单

业务代码:

- `vllm_ascend/ops/layernorm.py`
- `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/rms_norm.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/rms_triton_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/rejection_sampler_triton_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/early_kernel_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/nz_warmup.py`
- `vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v4/model.py`
- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`
- `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py`

Docs:

- `docs/source/user_guide/configuration/additional_config.md`
- `vllm_ascend/eplb/core/eplb_utils.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_loader/netloader/utils.py`
- `vllm_ascend/model_loader/netloader/netloader.py`

DT:

- `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_early_kernel_warmup.py` (new)
- `tests/ut/ops/test_rms_block_sizing.py` (new)
- `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_rms_triton_warmup.py`
- `tests/ut/model_executor/test_deepseek_v4.py`
- `tests/ut/model_loader/netloader/test_netloader_utils.py`
- `tests/ut/eplb/core/test_eplb_utils.py`
- `tests/ut/ops/test_layernorm.py`
- `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_nz_warmup.py` (new)
- `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py`
- `tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py`

### 3.2 DT

| 用例 | 覆盖 |
| --- | --- |
| `test_early_kernel_warmup.py` | `ascend_warmup_config` gating (default off, uninitialized config counts as off), thread is daemon and started once, `get_current_vllm_config() is None` does not latch the state, failures never propagate, `join` waits for a live thread and warns if it outlives the timeout |
| `test_rms_block_sizing.py` | `_rms_block_m` floors to `{1,2,4,8,16}`, is capped at 16, never returns 0 |
| `test_rms_triton_warmup.py` | warmup compiles exactly the five power-of-two keys, `assume_used=True` skips the `attn_groups` probe, the early thread is joined first |
| `test_deepseek_v4.py` | routed MoE receives the configured swiglu limit |
| `test_netloader_utils.py` | disk fallback keeps `DefaultModelLoader` keys, drops `SOURCE`/`LISTEN_PORT`, adds no defaults, preserves an explicit opt-out |
| `test_eplb_utils.py` | linear expert map is built once per `(ep_size, ep_rank, n_experts)`, each layer gets its own copy, a `None` map is passed through |
| `test_layernorm.py` | `quant_description` is scanned once, not once per RMSNorm |
| `test_nz_warmup.py` | NZ warmup runs once, stays off unless `enable_early_nz_warmup` is set, starts at most one daemon thread, `join_nz_warm_thread` waits for it |
| `test_ascend_config.py` | `AscendWarmupConfig` coerces string bools and rejects unknown keys |
| `test_worker_v1.py` | `NPUWorker.load_model` does not join the prewarm threads |

### 3.3 pre-commit

No config change. `ruff` / `codespell` / `markdownlint` / `gitleaks` / mypy
clean, `cpu-ut` green (5713 passed).

One unrelated line is included because it blocks the gate:
`vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite.py:663` fails mypy on current `main`
(`"XModelConfig" has no attribute "index_full_mask"`, from #16669). Switched to
the `getattr` form already used a few lines above.

## **4. 自验证**

Ran on the 0.27.1rc image
`mindie-motor:3.2.0b3-vllm_ascendnightly-releases-0.27.1rc-a2-openeuler24.03-py3.12-aarch64`,
image Motor 3.2.0b3, no wheel. Overlay is the 0.27 layout of this change set
plus `modelslim_config.py` (that file is not in this PR: main no longer has
`is_layer_skipped_ascend`). Same Motor both sides. Triton cache hot both
sides. HTTP 200. That overlay still read the two prewarm switches from env
vars; the prewarm logic is the same. The join before profiling should not
add wall time on these scenes: the NZ lazy init is 15~19 s and the Triton JIT
hits the hot cache, against 42 s (Flash) / 98 s (Pro) of weight I/O.

A = first `Available plugins` to the last `Model runner load_model total
time`; B = `init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model)`. A+B is
taken on the slowest decode pod.

Flash W8A8, A2 4-node, one P and one D instance of two pods each, dp16
(`17-17-06` vs `18-29-36`):

| | baseline | this change set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| slowest decode A+B | 318 s | **206 s** |
| `load_model total` | 151~161 s | **58~68 s** |
| construct | 77 s | **3~4 s** |

Pro W4A8, A2 8-node, one P and one D instance of four pods each
(`18-58-22` vs `19-26-10`):

| | baseline | this change set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| slowest decode A+B | 811 s | **461 s** |
| `load_model total` | 463~529 s | **135~161 s** |
| construct | 308~318 s | **4~5 s** |

Weight I/O is unchanged (Pro 83~98 s both sides). Warmup did not move: both
runs reuse a hot Triton cache, the only B-stage item in this change set is
the Triton kernel warmup and it was already 0.33~0.47 s on the baseline, and
the bulk of B is `torch.compile` plus graph capture (Pro 43 s + 59 s, equal on
both sides), which this PR does not touch. Construct on 0.27.1rc still needs
the `modelslim_config.py` index; that lands in the 0.27 backport, not here.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Misc]feat: adapt to vLLM main (903285fb)
body:

Adapt vllm-ascend to vLLM main commits up to September 16. ### Changes | Files | Upstream vLLM change | vllm-ascend adaptation | |-------|---------------------|------------------------| | — | [5392fbca](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/5392fbca2a45d0224f5653e01885d271518d2dfd) — Upstream reworked YaRN rope construction (extrapolation_factor/attn_factor/apply_yarn_scaling -> mscale/mscale_all_dim/attention_factor, yarn_get_mscale gains mscale), dropped `req_states` from the MRV2 PCPManager and taught its partition_batch to handle spec decode natively, and added an `allow_partial_hash_hits` switch to get_kv_cache_coordinator/HybridKVCacheCoordinator. | Gave AscendYaRNRotaryEmbedding two version-selected __init__ signatures forwarding the tree-appropriate kwargs; made AscendPCPManager accept req_states but forward it only on the release base; added allow_partial_hash_hits to the patched get_kv_cache_coordinator and AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator (release-guarded forward to the original); made the patched test's removed-symbol patches release-only and typed the pre-existing sentinel lines so the file passes mypy; gave copy_kv_cache_blocks_inplace a CPU fallback, moved the mooncake group mocks into setUpModule so the shared-process batch stops dropping them, and typed the mooncake file's latent mock lines so it passes mypy. E2E was then blocked by a contaminated vllm install (a stale newer `vllm/multimodal/cache/` package shadowed the target's `cache.py`, breaking `import vllm` in conftest before the plugin loads); removed that orphan from the installed tree and the stale `build/` copy. Finally, the lint venv lost its numpy==1.26.4 pin and inherited the system numpy 2.3.5 (upgraded by the e2e's unconstrained scipy), so the ~70 spurious `[var-annotated]`/cascade mypy errors were fixed per-error-code with targeted `# type: ignore[...]` comments across the reported lines. | | — | [485421b1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/485421b1c3572597a4cfaece04836a843537435a) — The 0.29 deprecation removed `CommonAttentionMetadata._seq_lens_cpu`/`_num_computed_tokens_cpu` and their properties, and the dflash DP-padding fix replaced `Speculator._build_draft_attn_metadata` with `_build_attn_metadata`/`_build_uniform_attn_metadata`. | Made `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` own the two removed fields as `field(default=None, kw_only=True)` so its `unpadded()` and all Ascend attention/proposer readers keep working; gave `AscendDFlashSpeculator`/`AscendDSparkSpeculator`/`AscendAutoRegressiveSpeculator` a lane-gated `_build_draft_attn_metadata` shim that calls the old super method on the release tree and `_build_uniform_attn_metadata`/`_build_attn_metadata` (with a synthesised `BatchExecutionDescriptor`) on main, and made the dspark/dspark-metadata UT patch the method that actually exists on the running lane. Fix round: widened the dspark bridge's `num_reqs_padded` to optional, routed `build_draft_attn_metadatas` through the non-updating bridge (was double-updating), and updated the minimax-m3 / eagle-proposer UTs to stop building the base `CommonAttentionMetadata` with the removed fields. E2E then exposed an Ascend FIA tiling failure in the draft MTP graph, so the shims now reproduce vLLM's removed `_build_draft_attn_metadata` body via `build_draft_attn_metadata_legacy()` on main (release still calls the pinned super method), and the dspark UTs patch the method each lane calls. Second E2E round pinned the real cause: capture drives `_multi_step_decode`, which #56181 reroutes to `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` (an entry point Ascend did not override), so the captured draft graph lost the forced `DecodeOnly`/TND layout while replay still fed cumulative `actual_seq_lengths_q`. Added an `AscendAutoRegressiveSpeculator._build_uniform_attn_metadata` override that reproduces #56181's batch-descriptor token semantics and re-enters `_build_draft_attn_metadata`, plus a `dcp_local_seq_lens` passthrough on that method. | | `docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.md` | [120ec4eb](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/120ec4ebd2803c3cc63729e18fcfd42b5ba47447) | — | | `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_cache.py`
`tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py` | [d43bb2f3](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d43bb2f37f87a63d3a9a299c97050443cf6a2520) — HiSparse host-resident sparse-MLA (#53781) threads a CUDA `SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder` through `DeepseekV2DecoderLayer`/`DeepseekV2MLAAttention`/`MLAModules`/`MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper`, so the decoder layer now always passes `index_group_builder=` to `DeepseekV2MLAAttention`, and `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper.forward` calls `self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` for sparse MLA. The same commit refactors `MLAAttention`'s KV-cache update into `update_kv_cache`/`prepare_kv_cache_update`, replaces `init_kv_cache`'s `runner_kv_caches` with `bind_kv_cache_to_layers`, and adds defaulted interface surface (`AttentionImplBase.prepare_for_batch`, `MLAAttentionImpl.hisparse_cache`, `KVCacheSpec.host_resident`/role properties, `KVCacheConfig.hisparse_host_num_blocks`, KV-connector `get_transfer_results`/`finish_forward`/`reset_capture_state`). | Added `index_group_builder: Any = None` to the Ascend-patched `DeepseekV2MLAAttention.__init__` (`_deepseek_v2_mla_attention_init`) and dropped it, so the upstream decoder layer's new keyword no longer raises `TypeError` (Ascend builds no sparse index group). Added a no-op `record_logical_topk_ready()` to `AscendMLAImpl` and `AscendSFAImpl` so the new sparse-wrapper hook resolves on the Ascend impls. The remaining changes are additive with defaults and need no Ascend edit: HiSparse is CUDA-only, the KV-cache-update refactor still reaches `impl.do_kv_cache_update(...)` with the same args, and `init_kv_cache` now calls `bind_kv_cache_to_layers`, whose default `AttentionLayerBase.bind_kv_cache` already matches the Ascend binding (`self.kv_cache = kv_cache`), leaving the existing `bind_kv_cache` patch as a harmless MRV1 path. Fix round (UT): the 7 pre_ci failures were all test-mock drift from the same upstream contracts — mocks lacked `attention_config.hisparse_config` (`test_deepseek_v41_cache.py`, `test_mooncake_connector.py`), called `init_kv_cache(runner_kv_caches=...)`/patched `bind_kv_cache` (`test_attn_utils_v2.py`), or built `OffloadingGroupConfig` without the new required `group_id` (`test_native_cpu_offload.py`). Made each lane-aware with `vllm_version_is("0.29.0")`: mocks gained `hisparse_config=None`, the kv-cache test patches `bind_kv_cache_to_layers` (main) vs `bind_kv_cache` (release) and passes `runner_kv_caches` only on release, and the offloading test adds `group_id` only on main. Fix round (mypy): touching `tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py` and `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_cache.py` pulled their pre-existing latent type errors into the per-file mypy scope (16 issues). Added targeted `# type: ignore[arg-type/assignment/union-attr/method-assign]` on the exact reported lines and annotated the bare `results`/`tasks` list literals, wrapping the over-long `_adjust_kv_layout` calls so every line stays within the limit. Fix round (mypy 2/2): mypy attributes the `_adjust_kv_layout(None, ...)` arg-type error to the argument line, not the call-opening line, so the two `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments were moved onto the `None, raw, ...` continuation lines. Fix round (mypy 2/2, retry): after the formatter exploded the call, mypy still reports the arg-type on the first-argument line (`None,`), so both `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments now sit on that argument line, where the formatter cannot move them. Fix round (E2E family): upstream #53781 changed `GPUModelRunner.initialize_kv_cache` to call the new `bind_kv_cache_to_layers` and to filter `init_kv_cache`'s result with `cache.device`. Ascend's `_reshape_kv_cache_v2` stores each layer as a `(k_cache, v_cache)` tuple, so `MLAAttention.bind_kv_cache`'s `kv_cache.squeeze(1)` and the `.device` filter both raised `AttributeError` on tuple/list for every MRV2 model (MTP, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen3, DFlash, DSpark). Added an Ascend `bind_kv_cache_to_layers` (`patch_bind_kv_cache.py`) that assigns `.kv_cache` directly, patched it into `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils` on main, and wrapped `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner.init_kv_cache` so component tuples expose a `device` proxy (`_KVCacheComponents`) while keeping the tuple layout the Ascend impls index into. | | — | [72d4d831](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/72d4d8315749c146cf19f047fecfec491911770d) — The step range drops the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor-alignment pad from the vision path: `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/common/mm_preprocess.py` removes `COMPRESS_PAD_TO`, `IMAGE_PAD_ID`, `IMAGE_PAD_TOKEN_NAME`, the processor's pad-splicing (`_apply_token_matches_with_placeholders`) and the `embed_input_ids` pad remap, and `DeepseekV41Config` stops setting `mm_prefix_span_leading_pad_modulus` (base sentinel id is now 129264 with no pad slot). The rest of the range (ROCm elastic-EP warmup deferral, NixlEP `eep_stage`→`all2all_manager`, `on_commit` removal, DP-coordination skip, EPLB buffers, watermarking) is additive or CUDA/ROCm-only. | Removed the now-deleted `IMAGE_PAD_ID`/`IMAGE_SENTINEL_BASE_ID` imports from the Ascend V4.1 wrapper and dropped the `masked_fill` pad remap in `embed_input_ids` (pass raw ids through, mirroring upstream); set `mm_prefix_span_leading_pad_modulus = 0` so the MRV1 doc-range logic takes the no-pad branch. Updated the two V4.1 UTs to the new contract (no `COMPRESS_PAD_TO`/`IMAGE_PAD_ID`, pad-free engram/sentinel masks, pass-through embedding, config no longer exposes the modulus). | | — | [e19a3e17](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/e19a3e172ecc1d1ece8ecce9dfd91bf811a814a0) — The batch (HiSparse host cache TP sharing #56629 plus PCP+DCP refinements) renames `CommonAttentionMetadata.dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu` to `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` and adds `req_idx`, changes `PCPManager._reorder_segments`/`_get_rank_segments` signatures, adds `MLAAttention.supports_pcp_dcp` guard and `KVCacheConfig.hisparse_host_*` fields. The HiSparse/offload parts are CUDA/ROCm-only. | Made `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` own both `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu` (removed on main) and `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` (absent on release) as `field(default=None, kw_only=True)` and propagate both in `unpadded()`, so the copy works on either tree. Updated `AscendPCPManager.get_num_tokens_for_dispatch`'s 0.28 fallback to the new `_get_rank_segments` signature (dropped `num_computed_tokens`). Dropped the removed base field from the eagle-proposer base-field guard UT. The PCP+DCP `supports_pcp_dcp` guard is not triggered by Ascend's own attention forward (which bypasses the base MLA forward), and Ascend's metadata builders do not set `req_idx`. Fix round (UT): the only failure was `test_pcp_manager_v2.py::test_partition_batch_refreshes_local_ascend_input_batch_metadata` — upstream #53781 replaced the "pure prefills last" PCP segment sort with a canonical `(is_prefilling, req_idx, start)` sort, so on main rank 0's local rows are now head-then-tail (`[5, 3]`, query_start_loc `[0, 5, 8]`). Made the test's four order-dependent expectations lane-aware (release keeps the old tail-then-head values). | | `vllm_ascend/__init__.py`
`vllm_ascend/utils.py` | [aed894c1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/aed894c190aa3db74c502d521b3bc3935ad85de1) — The warmup migration wraps the DFlash input-prepare kernel in a `@triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup(kernel=_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel, ...)` dispatcher, and `GPUModelRunner.__init__`/`GPUModelRunner.__init__` (MRV1) now create `jit_warmup_registry` via a `@JitWarmupRegistry.capture` decorator instead of an explicit assignment. Sampling/Eagle/rejection kernels were similarly wrapped. | `patch_triton.py` retargets the dispatcher on main — `setattr(dflash_speculator.prepare_dflash_inputs, "kernel", _prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel_ascend)` — because the module-attribute `dflash_speculator._prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel = ...` patch can no longer reach the captured kernel; the release lane (plain function) keeps the attribute patch. Verified Ascend's MRV1/MRV2/310p model runners all call `super().__init__`, so the decorator-created `jit_warmup_registry` exists, and `JitWarmupRegistry.register` is a no-op without an active registry (so Ascend's post-super sampler construction and its own `kernel_warmup` are safe). No other Ascend patch targets a dispatcher-wrapped kernel. title: [Performance] Avoid request-count specialization in DSA-CP metadata kernel
[Feature] Add runtime_guard control plane (detect, report, dump_kv)
body:
Hot-reloadable runtime_config plus wave-synced detectors, report, and KV dump on Ascend v1/v2 runners, with docs and unit tests.
---

## [Feature] Add runtime_guard control plane (detect, report, dump_kv)

### 1. 摘要 / Summary

**中文**:为 vllm-ascend 引入 runtime_guard 控制面:一组低开销在线异常检测器 + 事件报告 + 按请求 KV dump + 热更新配置。目标是在"静默输出异常"与"进程崩溃"之间补上运行时可观测与取证能力——NaN/Inf logits、退化复读、禁词子串、投机解码接受率异常均可在服务不中断的情况下被捕获、报告并转储现场。**默认关闭、零侵入**(C1 实测开启代码不加载检测时开销为 0)。

**English**: Adds the runtime_guard control plane to vllm-ascend: a set of low-overhead online anomaly detectors, incident reporting, per-request KV dumps, and hot-reloadable runtime configuration. It closes the observability gap between "silently wrong output" and "process crash" — NaN/Inf logits, degenerate repetition, forbidden substrings, and spec-decode acceptance anomalies are captured, reported, and dumped for post-mortem without interrupting serving. **Off by default, zero intrusion** (C1 verified: no measurable overhead when detectors are disabled).

### 2. 改动内容 / What's in this PR

68 files, +15,846 / −180;61 个新文件;**纯 Python,csrc 零改动**(无需重编 .so)。rebase 后内容一致,diff 数字略有平移。
68 files, +15,846 / −180; 61 new files; **pure Python, zero csrc changes** (no .so rebuild needed). Identical content on the rebased tip; diffstat shifts slightly.

| 模块 / Module | 内容 / Content |
|---|---|
| `vllm_ascend/runtime_guard/`(31 文件 / files) | 4 个在线检测器 / detectors: `logits_finite`(NaN/Inf)、`token_repeat`(退化复读)、`output_substring`(禁词子串)、`spec_acceptance`(投机接受率);processor/manager、rank_gate(TP0 检测收敛 + 全 rank dump)、detector placement(ExecScope/LPT 分摊)、incident report(per-rank 路由 + quota/cooldown)、dump_kv action(逐层异步 D2H,payload 含 tp_rank/num_kv_heads)、io_snapshot、wave_tracker |
| `vllm_ascend/runtime_config/`(9 文件 / files) | JSONC 运行时配置 + 热更新(可配 interval,默认 0=关)、原子校验(未知键拒绝并保留旧配置)、TP/PP/DP 安全广播、input_filters、ascend_log 级联 / hot-reload config with atomic validation (unknown-key rejection keeps last-good), TP/PP/DP-safe broadcast, input filters, ascend_log cascade |
| worker 接线 / wiring | `model_runner_v1.py`(+441)、`worker/v2/model_runner.py`(+119)、`worker.py`:v1/v2 双 runner、async-scheduling 安全(pre/post-sample 两阶段采样全 rank 生效) / both runners, async-scheduling-safe (two-phase sampling materializes on all ranks) |
| `tests/ut/` + `runtime_guard/test/` | 153 个 UT,行覆盖 75%(含 5 个注入双门禁 shipped-safety 测试)/ 153 UTs, 75% line coverage (incl. 5 double-gate shipped-safety tests) |

### 3. 设计要点 / Design highlights

- **默认零开销 / Zero overhead when off**:检测器/热更新全部关断时,热路径仅有一次 inactive 早退判断;C1(T1/T0≥0.999)双 runner 实测通过。
  When all detectors and hot-reload are off, the hot path takes a single inactive early-exit check; gate C1 (T1/T0 ≥ 0.999) passed on both runners.
- **rank 收敛执行 / Rank-converged execution**:检测收敛到 last-PP TP0(消除每步 D2H 同步性能损失),dump 各 rank 独立执行;报告按 `rank_dp*_tp*_pp*` 路由,无跨 rank 通信。
  Detection converges to last-PP TP0 (eliminating per-step D2H sync tax); dumps run per-rank; reports route to `rank_dp*_tp*_pp*` with no cross-rank communication.
- **配置热更新安全 / Hot-reload safety**:通过广播保证各 rank 集合通信参与一致;拒绝不正确的 JSON 文件、未知 key、非法 value,并保留旧配置。
  Broadcast keeps collective participation rank-consistent; malformed JSON, unknown keys, and invalid values are rejected while the last-good config is kept.
- **NPU 数据布局适配 / NPU layout handling**:v2 runner 的 StagedWriteTensor 与 UvaBufferWrapper 在 host 侧无数据,v1/v2 统一走 `.gpu` 按需拷贝兜底(block_ids / io_snapshot 已实测非空)。仅 dump 会走此逻辑。
  On the v2 runner, StagedWriteTensor and UvaBufferWrapper carry no host-side copy, so both runners fall back to copying rows on demand from `.gpu` (block_ids / io_snapshot verified non-empty on live NPU). Only dumps ever take this path.

### 4. 性能 / Performance gates(910B4·A2 本机 + 910C·A3 远端,交叉轮换 / cross-rotation)

**中文**:

| 门槛 | 定义 | 阈值 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | guard 代码加载但全关 vs 无 guard 基线,T1/T0 | ≥0.999 | v1=1.00291 / v2=1.00411;A3:DSV2-Lite 1.0067、Qwen3-30B-A3B 1.0058 — 全过 |
| C2 | 3s 热更新轮询开销,T2/T1 | ≥0.999 | 0.99920~1.00644,过;~0.4% 税仅在 reload 开启时存在,默认 reload_interval=0 无此税 |
| C3 | 检测器开销,T3/T2 | ≥0.990 | v1=1.01120 / v2=0.99980(≤1%),过 |
| C4 | 功能隔离,输出 bit-identical | bit 一致 | 过:双 runner 各 1 轮(4 状态 × 3 prompt = 12 组输出),temp=0/seed=42 全部 bit 一致 |
| C5 | dump 直接计时(无对比基线,纯测量;逐层异步 D2H + save,不在热路径) | — | 每 rank:1k tok 0.15-0.22s + 0.11s(34MiB);16k 0.16-0.72s + 0.33-0.77s;128k 0.64-1.62s + 2.7-5.5s(2-3.9GiB);v1/v2 同量级 |
| C6 | 短压后 RSS/HBM 泄漏回落,guard 组 vs 裸 base 组对照差分 | 差值 <+10MB RSS / <+512MB HBM | guard +0.2MB/−0.7MB vs base +0.0MB/+1.3MB → 差值 +0.1MB/−2.0MB,过,零残留 |

短压定义:1k-128k LongBench 语料持续压测(guard 组 15 请求/244k tok,base 组 17 请求/507k tok;prompt 带序号前缀防 KV 复用),停压后 settle 30s,再连续采样 300s(27 点)。

**English**:

| Gate | Definition | Bar | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | guard loaded but all off vs no-guard baseline, T1/T0 | ≥0.999 | v1=1.00291 / v2=1.00411; A3: DSV2-Lite 1.0067, Qwen3-30B-A3B 1.0058 — all pass |
| C2 | 3s hot-reload polling overhead, T2/T1 | ≥0.999 | 0.99920-1.00644, pass; ~0.4% tax exists only while reload is on, absent at the default reload_interval=0 |
| C3 | detector overhead, T3/T2 | ≥0.990 | v1=1.01120 / v2=0.99980 (≤1%), pass |
| C4 | functional isolation, bit-identical outputs | bit-identical | pass: one full pass per runner (4 states × 3 prompts = 12 outputs), temp=0/seed=42, all bit-identical |
| C5 | dump direct timing (no baseline, measurement only; per-layer async D2H + save, off the hot path) | — | per rank: 1k tok 0.15-0.22s + 0.11s (34MiB); 16k 0.16-0.72s + 0.33-0.77s; 128k 0.64-1.62s + 2.7-5.5s (2-3.9GiB); v1/v2 in the same band |
| C6 | post-short-stress RSS/HBM leakback, guard arm vs bare-base control, differential | diff <10MB RSS / <512MB HBM | guard +0.2MB/−0.7MB vs base +0.0MB/+1.3MB → differential +0.1MB/−2.0MB, pass, zero residue |

Short stress = sustained load with 1k-128k LongBench prompts (guard arm 15 req / 244k tok, base arm 17 req / 507k tok; sequence-numbered prompts defeat KV reuse), settle 30s after load stops, then 300s of sampling (27 points).

### 5. 测试证据 / Test evidence

- **功能 / Functional**:P0 冒烟 12/12;P1 5/5;异常注入 4/4(nan/inf/禁词/复读环);热更新软失败;report/dump quota+cooldown;混部双实例 H-01..06;PD 分离 1P1D 冒烟(P/D 双侧挂 guard,D 侧注入,report schema 与单机一致)。
  P0 smoke 12/12; P1 5/5; fault injection 4/4; hot-reload soft-fail; report/dump quota+cooldown; mixed-instance H-01..06; PD-disaggregation 1P1D smoke (guard on both P and D, injection on D, report schema identical to single node).
- **模型与拓扑 / Models & topologies**:DeepSeek-V2-Lite(MoE)、Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B(MoE)、Qwen2.5-0.5B/7B/8B;runner v1+v2;TP / TP+EP / PP / DP。
- **稳定性 / Stability**:soak 有效 **24.06h**(目标 24h 达标):8 并发持续压测,累计 **4625 轮热更 0 失败**,心跳全程健康,无 hang/crash。
  24.06h effective soak (24h goal met): 8-concurrency sustained load, 4,625 hot-reload cycles with 0 failures, healthy heartbeats throughout, no hang/crash.
- **UT**:`runtime_guard/test` + `tests/ut/runtime_config` = **153 passed / 75%**(含注入双门禁 gate 测试;新 tip 上 135/135 全绿);全量 `tests/ut` 回归 2065 passed / 1 failed(上游既有问题,merge-base 同样失败)。
  153 passed / 75% (incl. double-gate tests; 135/135 green on the rebased tip); full tests/ut regression 2065 passed / 1 pre-existing upstream failure (reproduced on merge-base).
- **注入安全 / Injection safety**:RG_INJECT 双门禁 e2e 实证:shipped 构建 + 环境变量 → 0 注入日志/0 report;翻转源码开关后 → 注入生效 + token_repeat report 落盘。
  Double-gate e2e verified: shipped build + env var → zero injection; armed source build → injection fires, report lands.

### What this PR does / why we need it? Adapt vllm-ascend to vLLM main commits up to September 22. ### Changes | Files | Upstream vLLM change | vllm-ascend adaptation | |-------|---------------------|------------------------| | `mypy.ini`
`vllm_ascend/__init__.py` | [b8733988](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/b87339888d29329c42c42573e34cc2beebdcc48b) — Upstream dropped the deprecated `CommonAttentionMetadata._seq_lens_cpu` / `_num_computed_tokens_cpu` fields and their CPU-shadow properties, renamed YaRN scaling kwargs (`extrapolation_factor`/`attn_factor`/`apply_yarn_scaling` → `mscale`/`mscale_all_dim`/`attention_factor`), and made `PCPManager`/`maybe_build_pcp_manager` stop taking a `RequestState` (and stop importing the `prepare_pos_seq_lens` / `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` helpers). | `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` owns `_seq_lens_cpu`/`_num_computed_tokens_cpu` as kw-only fields so all Ascend builders, proposers and tests keep working on both trees; `AscendPCPManager.__init__` forwards `req_states` only under `vllm_version_is("0.29.0")`; `AscendYaRNRotaryEmbedding.__init__` accepts the old+new YaRN kwargs and forwards the version-appropriate set. Tests adapted: YaRN signature allow-list, Ascend metadata ownership, `create=True` mocks for the removed PCP helpers, fake managers expose `block_size`, mypy narrowing/ignores. E2E blocker fixed by an `sys.meta_path` finder in `vllm_ascend/__init__.py` resolving `vllm.multimodal.cache` to `cache.py` when a stale `cache/` package shadows it. Environment-only mypy noise (system numpy 2.x stubs + unbuilt `vllm_ascend_C`) handled in `mypy.ini` (`disable_error_code = ..., var-annotated`, `[mypy-vllm_ascend.vllm_ascend_C]`) plus 19 targeted per-line ignores. | | `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/draft_attn_compat.py` | [485421b1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/485421b1c3572597a4cfaece04836a843537435a) — The MRV2 spec-decode draft builder was renamed/signature-changed upstream: `_build_draft_attn_metadata(num_reqs, num_reqs_padded, num_tokens_padded, seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound, step, …)` became `_build_attn_metadata(num_reqs, batch_desc, query_start_loc_np, …)` with a new `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` wrapper; `DFlashSpeculator._build_draft_attn_metadata` was deleted and `DraftModelSpeculator.arange` became `arange_np`. | `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/spec_decode/draft_attn_compat.py` re-installs an old-signature `DraftModelSpeculator._build_draft_attn_metadata` on main that forwards to the new API, so the existing Ascend wrappers and the `tests/ut` mocks keep working. `AscendAutoRegressiveSpeculator` and `AscendDSparkSpeculator` add a `vllm_version_is("0.29.0")`-guarded `_build_attn_metadata` override carrying the Ascend context factory / DecodeOnly / `actual_seq_lengths_q` fix; `AscendDFlashSpeculator` reverts to its unconditional `build_draft_attn_metadatas`. No-op changes assessed and documented in `analysis.md`. | | `docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.md` | [120ec4eb](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/120ec4ebd2803c3cc63729e18fcfd42b5ba47447) | — | | — | [d43bb2f3](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d43bb2f37f87a63d3a9a299c97050443cf6a2520) — HiSparse 3/N split `bind_kv_cache` so `init_kv_cache` now binds layers through the new runner-info-free `bind_kv_cache_to_layers(kv_caches, forward_context, num_attn_module, kv_cache_groups)` (the `runner_kv_caches` parameter is gone), and `GPUModelRunner.initialize_kv_cache` now derives `self.kv_caches` by filtering `kv_caches_dict.values()` on `cache.device`. | added an NPU-safe `bind_kv_cache_to_layers` (keeps Ascend's `.kv_cache = ...` binding plus `share_replayssm_ring_trackers`) and bound it to `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils` / `vllm.v1.worker.utils` only under `if not vllm_version_is("0.29.0")`, since main's `init_kv_cache` otherwise bypasses the existing `bind_kv_cache` patch (NPU `Attention.bind_kv_cache` raises `NotImplementedError`). Wrapped Ascend's tuple/list KV-cache entries (SFA indexer, K-pool tail) in `AscendKVCacheView(tuple)` / `AscendKVCacheListView(list)` subclasses exposing `.device` so main's device filter accepts them; the wrapper memoizes by object id so shared-layer aliases stay identical. All other step-4 API surface (connector hooks + `failed_recving`, `KVCacheSpec`/`KVCacheGroupSpec` fields, manager attrs, MLA `update_kv_cache`/`prepare_for_batch`) is defaulted and already matched by Ascend. UT fix round (pre_ci, 8 failures): stale test mocks were synced to main's contract — stub configs gain `attention_config.hisparse_config` (deepseek_v41 runtime, Mooncake `MockVllmConfig`), `test_attn_utils_v2` calls `init_kv_cache` with the runner-list-free signature and patches `bind_kv_cache_to_layers` (release branch keeps `runner_kv_caches`/`bind_kv_cache`), and `test_native_cpu_offload` passes the new `OffloadingGroupConfig.group_id` on main only. mypy fix round (15 latent issues surfaced once the UT files entered the changed-file set): mechanical per-line `# type: ignore[...]` on the stubbed-argument and monkeypatch-method assignments in `test_attn_utils_v2.py` / `test_deepseek_v41_cache.py`. E2E fix round: `_deepseek_v2_mla_attention_init` (vllm-ascend's replacement for `DeepseekV2MLAAttention.__init__`) now accepts the new `index_group_builder` argument (dropped — Ascend impls do not consume the upstream `SparseMLAIndexGroup`), and `AscendDSAImpl` / `AscendSFAImpl` / `AscendMLAImpl` gained a no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` for the new sparse-path hook in `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper.forward`. | | — | [72d4d831](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/72d4d8315749c146cf19f047fecfec491911770d) — This step removed the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor-alignment pad from upstream (`COMPRESS_PAD_TO`, `IMAGE_PAD_ID`, `IMAGE_PAD_TOKEN_NAME`, `_apply_token_matches_with_placeholders`, `DeepseekV41Config.mm_prefix_span_leading_pad_modulus`) and reworked the elastic-EP all2all interface (`All2AllManagerBase.stage_ep_size`/`commit_ep_size`/`mask_remote_ranks`, `get_ep_all2all_manager(ep_group=)`, `maybe_make_prepare_finalize(all2all_manager=)`), which `ElasticEPScalingExecutor` now calls unguarded. | dropped the removed V4.1 pad handling — `vl_model.py` no longer imports `IMAGE_PAD_ID`/`IMAGE_SENTINEL_BASE_ID`, no longer sets `mm_prefix_span_leading_pad_modulus`, and `embed_input_ids` embeds `input_ids` unchanged; `model_runner_v1` defaults `span_pad_modulus` to `0` (V4.0 still carries the attribute, so its path is unchanged). Added `stage_ep_size`/`commit_ep_size`/`mask_remote_ranks` no-op hooks to NPU's `_NpuAll2AllManager`. Updated the V4.1 UT imports/assertions to the pad-free contract. Watermarking / MRV2 draft watermark, the fused-MoE `eep_stage`→`all2all_manager` rename, `EplbModelState` buffers, cohere renderer and the RDNA3 MoE backend were assessed and need no Ascend change. | | — | [e19a3e17](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/e19a3e172ecc1d1ece8ecce9dfd91bf811a814a0) — HiSparse TP-shared host pools plus the PCP+DCP sparse-MLA wiring around it renamed `CommonAttentionMetadata.dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu` to `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound`, added `CommonAttentionMetadata.req_idx`, and threaded the new field through `build_attn_metadata` / `InputBatch` / `model_states/default.py`; `SharedOffloadRegion` also gained optional creator-only population args and `KVCacheConfig` gained HiSparse host fields. | `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` now declares `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound`, the legacy `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu` and `req_idx` as kw-only compat fields (default `None`) and `unpadded()` propagates all three, so the sub-batch view works on both trees (release defines the legacy name, main the `_upper_bound` name). The rest of the step needs no Ascend change: `SharedOffloadRegion`'s new args are optional, Ascend never enables HiSparse (the `KVCacheConfig` fields are defaulted), `AscendPCPManager` uses `super()` for the supported path (the old `_get_rank_segments` call is inside the dead `0.28.0` branch), Ascend has no `MLAAttention` subclass or `DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder` subclass, and Ascend ships its own `build_attn_metadata` / `AscendModelState` / sparse indexer. UT fix round (pre_ci, 1 failed + 19 errors): `test_eagle_proposer.py::check_mock` hardcoded the upstream `CommonAttentionMetadata` field name, so it now selects `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` on main and the legacy `dcp_local_seq_lens_cpu` on 0.29.0; `test_pcp_manager_v2.py` order-dependent assertions were made lane-aware to match main's new canonical local-segment order (head chunk before tail) while keeping the release order. | | `vllm_ascend/__init__.py` | [aed894c1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/aed894c190aa3db74c502d521b3bc3935ad85de1) — The warmup migration converted the sampling and spec-decode Triton kernels (`topk_topp`, `vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/{utils,llm_base_proposer,dflash}.py`, MRV2 dflash/multi_module_mtp) into `triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup` owners that capture their kernel at decoration time, and moved `jit_warmup_registry` construction onto a `@JitWarmupRegistry.capture`-decorated `GPUModelRunner.__init__`. | `patch_triton.py` now installs Ascend's `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel_ascend` on the decorated dispatcher (`dflash_speculator.prepare_dflash_inputs.kernel = ...`) on main and keeps the legacy module-global replacement on 0.29.0 — main's dispatcher captured the original kernel at decoration, so the old assignment was dead and the upstream CUDA kernel would have run on NPU. Everything else is transparent: `JitWarmupRegistry.register` no-ops without an active registry, both NPU runners call `super().__init__()` (so `jit_warmup_registry` is set) and Ascend's own `kernel_warmup` never consumes it, Ascend launches the raw v1 rejection kernels directly and patches the public `apply_top_k_top_p_triton`, and Ascend uses NPU custom ops / its own triton kernels for the eagle/dflash copy-expand paths. UT fix round (pre_ci, 4 collection errors): vLLM's Triton JIT-warmup decorators read `triton.runtime.autotuner.Autotuner` at import time, but when vLLM disables Triton (no active driver, CPU UT) it substitutes `vllm.triton_utils.TritonPlaceholder`, which has no `runtime`, so importing `vllm.v1.spec_decode.utils` crashed; `vllm_ascend/__init__.py` defines an installer that provides `triton.runtime.autotuner.Autotuner` (real `Autotuner` when importable, else a stub) and gives `vllm.triton_utils.importing.TritonPlaceholder` a `runtime` class attribute — but it is **not** called at package import (importing vllm there resolved the platform too early and broke `VllmConfig()` device inference). `adapt_patch()` invokes it before importing the worker patches, which is the first point where the placeholder instance can exist. The stub module is annotated `Any` so mypy does not flag the `autotuner` attribute assignment. | | `vllm_ascend/__init__.py` | [dfa1984e](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/dfa1984e58dc898610a320de26f94b6039fccec3) — This step rolled the step-7 warmup migration back for the runner and spec-decode kernels — `GPUModelRunner.__init__` lost `@JitWarmupRegistry.capture`, MRV2 `DFlashSpeculator.prepare_dflash_inputs` and `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator._shift_input_*` are plain kernels launched by module-global lookup again, and `_is_autotuned` gained `if not HAS_TRITON: return False`. It also added the DSA `sparse_indexer_topk_backend` selector and the composite / R-SWA attention plumbing. | reverted step-7's dflash adaptation to the unconditional `dflash_speculator._prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel = _prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel_ascend` (the `.kernel` dispatcher hook no longer exists) and dropped the now-unused `vllm_version_is` import; removed step-7's `_ensure_triton_runtime_attr` compat stub from `vllm_ascend/__init__.py` and the `adapt_patch()` invocation, since upstream now short-circuits `_is_autotuned` when `HAS_TRITON` is false. Everything else is no-op: Ascend ships its own DSA/kpool indexer, inherits the new attention-backend defaults, keeps `dp_shared_memory=False` (engram patch still relaxes `verify_model_config`), and its `rfork`/`netloader` loaders call `initialize_model` directly. | | `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_vision.py`
`tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dspark_graph_contract.py` | [1d0d1081](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/1d0d1081c409176a0e7c24742f7c60b9943657aa) — The cumulative main patch renames the DeepSeek-V4.1 model package `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/` → `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` (updating every internal import, the model registry entries, the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`/`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` backend paths and the `deepseek_v4_1` → `deepseek_v41` quantization-config import), and adds DBO FULL-graph micro-batch capture to the V2 GPU worker: `CudaGraphManager`/`ModelCudaGraphManager.__init__` take a new `ubatch_runner` and `GPUModelRunner` now constructs the graph manager with `ubatch_runner=self.ubatch_runner`. | repointed the three Ascend references to the renamed package (`vllm.models.deepseek_v4_1.*` → `vllm.models.deepseek_v41.*`) in `models/deepseek_v41/vl_model.py` (`common.mm_preprocess`), `models/deepseek_v41/engram/common.py` (`common.engram`) and `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_vision.py`; since the pinned 0.29.0 tree has neither package, each renamed import carries `# type: ignore[import-not-found]` (same pattern as `worker/v2/spec_decode/dflash/aclgraph.py`). Added a `ubatch_runner: object = None` parameter to the MRV2 `graph_manager_wrapper` factory (which upstream substitutes for `ModelCudaGraphManager`) and dropped it, since DBO is unsupported on Ascend — `platform.py` already resets `enable_dbo=False` and `ubatch_size=0`, so `maybe_build_ubatch_runner` returns `None` and the manager's `ubatch_runner` stays `None`, which keeps `_maybe_ubatch_twin`/`_capture_stream` inactive, and `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dspark_graph_contract.py` sets `manager.ubatch_runner = None` on its `__new__`-built `DFlashCudaGraphManager` so the new `_maybe_ubatch_twin` read in `_init_candidates` works. No new version guards: the extra defaulted factory parameter is harmless on 0.29.0 (upstream there never passes it), and the rename is main-only (0.29.0 has neither `deepseek_v4_1` nor `deepseek_v41`; the vision UT skips via `pytest.importorskip("vllm.transformers_utils.configs.deepseek_v41")` and Ascend's V4.1 model modules are only loaded for the V4.1 model type). Everything else was assessed as no-op: the `gelu_and_mul_sparse` IR op / `kernel_config.ir_op_priority` field, the MLA `k_pe.shape[-1] == 0` NoPE fast path, the sparse-MLA `(64, 512, 256, 0, 256)` GLM-5.3-Flash dims and `FlashAttnPrefillBackend` dim entry, the `cpu_moe` DeepSeekV3 routing type, the MoRI-IO/mooncake/nixl connector changes (Ascend ships its own `MooncakeLayerwiseConnector` and never imports the upstream ones), the multi-node weight-cache daemon, `profiler/wrapper`, `BeamSearchParams.skip_special_tokens`, the tokenizer/config docs and the NVIDIA/Qwen4/GLM5Next model edits. | | `docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.md` | [435c96f9](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/435c96f9dbdd29258cb8e0f433c5b54a00cf6b16) · [03dc26e6](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/03dc26e639e1927cda51d7b62639a11a354e1c0d) · [e85c8826](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/e85c8826ce2a810367e8a70eedb987e31b140800) | — | | — | [f84b0c4b](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/f84b0c4bceee120936030dfb0c90af0a818263ed) — `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils.UvaBuffer.uva` changed from a tensor attribute to a method `uva(n=None)` returning the first `n` rows, and `UvaBufferPool`/`StagedWriteTensor` now choose their class from `is_uva_available()` (new `NonUvaBuffer` fallback) and call `buf.uva(n)`/`.uva()` instead of reading the attribute; the same step also moved the spec-decode adaptive-verification estimator into `DraftModelSpeculator` (with `observe_verification` and a `DraftModelSpeculator` guard in `GPUModelRunner.postprocess_sampled`), and edited the nixl/offloading connectors, deepseek_v41 NVIDIA/AMD kernels, MHC layers, input-processor validation and weight-cache daemon. | made Ascend's `UvaBufferWrapper` expose the upstream-main method interface (new `def uva(self, n=None)` over a shared `_sync_device_view`) and re-wrapped it as a `property` only under `vllm_version_is("0.29.0")`, so the pinned lane keeps reading `buf.uva` as a tensor while main calls it as a method; routed `Ascend310PStagedWriteTensor` through a new lane-aware `_uva_device_view()` helper (method on main, attribute on 0.29.0). No other change: Ascend's v2 speculators subclass the upstream `DraftModelSpeculator`/`DSparkSpeculator` and inherit `observe_verification`/`_maybe_predict_acceptance` (the gumbel UT already stubs `acceptance_estimator`), `NPUPlatform.is_pin_memory_available()` already makes upstream `is_uva_available()` true, and the nixl/offloading connectors, deepseek_v41 AMD/NVIDIA kernels, `MHCPreDelayedOp` (Ascend patches only `MHCPreOp`/`MHCFusedPostPreOp`), input-processor validation, `current_stream` and the GPU-worker pooling hook are unreferenced. | | `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2.py` | [5be911ee](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/5be911ee871604895c5a950ac1a5675c71896fd2) — Upstream dropped the worker `InputBatch` aliases (`vllm.v1.worker.lora_model_runner_mixin` now imports `InputBatch` from `gpu_input_batch`, removing `GPUInputBatch`/`TPUInputBatch`; `tpu_input_batch.py` deleted) and reworked MRV2 PCP CUDA-graph capture: `PCPManager.partition_batch` gained `padded_num_reqs`, `maybe_partition_pcp_batch(manager, input_batch, batch_desc)` replaced its `padded_num_tokens` argument, and new `prepare_inputs_to_capture`/`get_dummy_block_tables`/`_resolve_num_reqs_after_padding` helpers plus `set_dummy_context(input_block_tables=)` and PCP staging in `prepare_dummy_attn`/`_dummy_run` were introduced. | pointed `patch_mamba_utils` at the canonical `vllm.v1.worker.gpu_input_batch` for its worker input-batch annotation (imported as plain `InputBatch`, since the `GPUInputBatch` name no longer exists on the lora mixin); added `padded_num_reqs` to `AscendPCPManager.partition_batch` and forward it to `super()` only on main and only when non-`None` (the `vllm_version_is("0.29.0")` branch keeps the 0.29.0 call shape, so the exact-args assertions in `test_pcp_manager_v2` are unchanged); and branch the V2 runner's `maybe_partition_pcp_batch` call to pass `batch_desc` on main vs `padded_num_tokens=batch_desc.num_tokens` on 0.29.0. Everything else is additive/inherited: `set_dummy_context`, `prepare_inputs_to_capture` internals and the new base PCP helpers are defaulted; Ascend replaces the PCP capture path with `_prepare_pcp_inputs_to_capture` and overrides `prepare_dummy_attn`/`get_dummy_block_tables`; `AscendMambaManager` inherits the new `_cache_partial_tail_block`; and the parser/xgrammar/structured-tag/Kimi-K3/HPC changes are unreferenced. Fix round (pre_ci): dropped the `X as Y` alias from the `gpu_input_batch` import (the `broken_imports` checker does not parse `as`, and the underlying `InputBatch` symbol exists in both trees), and adapted `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2.py` to the two-branch call site (AST count 1 → 2; its `_partition` stub now accepts the new positional `batch_desc`), plus three mechanical `# type: ignore` suppressions for the latent errors the file then surfaced under mypy (`:29`/`:327` `[assignment]`, `:352` `[arg-type]`). | | — | [fdfcbbca](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/fdfcbbcac79b0d8134a3a447f2c33001f5de07c1) — Upstream folded `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils.async_copy_to_gpu` into `vllm.utils.torch_utils.async_tensor_h2d` (which gained a keyword `out=` and an optional `device=`), refactored `StructuredOutputManager` so the scheduler now uses `accept_tokens`/`validate_tokens` (removing `should_advance`) and renamed `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/*` to `common/*`, plus MRV2 config/indexer/kv-cache changes (`VllmConfig.num_prefill_lookahead_tokens`, `MLAAttentionSpec.block_stride_alignment`, `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` tensor rank, mla indexer warmup/`_prefill_split_seq_lens`). | repointed the MRV2 PCP/runner/PP helpers at `async_tensor_h2d` from `vllm.utils.torch_utils` (present on both lanes) and, because the 0.29.0 signature has no `out=`, converted the three `out=` call sites to `buf.copy_(async_tensor_h2d(np, device=...))`; branched the Ascend PP+MTP structured-output path in `patch_pp_mtp.py` to keep `manager.should_advance` on `vllm_version_is("0.29.0")` and use `manager.validate_tokens(request, ids)` on main; and synced the UT patch targets (`test_model_runner_v2` renames the Ascend mock to `async_tensor_h2d`; `test_pcp_manager_v2` renames the Ascend target and patches both the new upstream `pcp_manager.async_tensor_h2d` and the legacy `async_copy_to_gpu` with `create=True`). No other change: the MLAAttentionSpec field is inherited, `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` only widened its rank arg, Ascend does not override the mla indexer builder, the glm5next rename is not imported by Ascend, and the parser/engine/eagle3/`CpuGpuBuffer`/moe-runner/`replayssm` edits are compatible or unreferenced. Fix round (pre_ci, 48 UT failures): (A) `sparse_mqa_logits` calls `tl.constexpr` at import and the Triton placeholder's `constexpr` is `None`, so the whole `vllm.models.deepseek_v41` import chain failed on 39 tests — added `_patch_triton_language_placeholder()` to `utils.py`, invoked from `adapt_patch()` (using `import vllm.triton_utils`, not `from ... import tl`, to satisfy the import gate); (B) upstream's new `CpuGpuBuffer.copy_to_gpu` calls `cpu.pin_memory()`, which fails without the NPU pin backend — added `patch/platform/patch_cpu_gpu_buffer.py` restoring the allocation-free copy (registered in `patch/platform/__init__.py`); (C) the PCP copy used `self.device`, absent on `__new__`-built managers — switched to the destination buffer's device; (D) `test_patch_pp_mtp.py`'s `structured_output_manager` mock only had `should_advance`, so added `validate_tokens` to both mocks (keeping `should_advance` for the 0.29.0 lane); (E) that test file then surfaced 3 latent mypy errors — added `# type: ignore[assignment]` (×2) and `# type: ignore[union-attr]`. | | `docs/source/tutorials/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.md` | [903285fb](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/903285fb) | — | | `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_vision_preprocess.py` | [95f4925c](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/95f4925c3a03df8cfcaa21633ccc9dd5b426c7a4) — The cumulative patch is dominated by a repo-wide docstring/format migration plus the ROCm/MoRI head fix, and it refactors `BaseMultiModalProcessor` (`vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py`): the `_call_hf_processor` hook is (re)introduced with the new two-argument `(hf_data, hf_kwargs)` signature and is now called from `_apply_hf_processor_main`, `_get_hf_processor_text`→`_get_hf_mm_text`, `_get_hf_mm_data`/`_preprocess_hf_mm_data`→`_get_hf_mm_inputs` returning `HFMultiModalInputs`, `MultiModalProcessingInfo`→`MultiModalProcessingResult`, and `_maybe_apply_prompt_updates` takes that result object; title: [Refactor] delete VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1 env
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

FlashComm1 was still enabled by the `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1` environment variable, which was kept only as a compatibility path. This PR removes that path so FlashComm1 is enabled only through `additional_config.enable_flashcomm1` (`--additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true}'`). `enable_dsa_cp` still auto-enables FlashComm1.

- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py` no longer reads `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1`.
- Docs, tutorial templates, translations, and the model-adapter skill are updated to the `additional_config` switch.
- Weekly and nightly e2e configs that set the env var are converted in place: `1` / `true` becomes `"enable_flashcomm1": true`, `0` becomes `false`, and commented-out env lines are deleted without turning the feature on.
- For PD configs, the flag is added only on the nodes that previously set the env var. Prefill-on / decode-off cases stay that way, including the GLM-5.2 Memcache PD case.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1` no longer enables FlashComm1. Use `--additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true}'` instead.

### How was this patch tested?

- Updated the existing FlashComm1 unit tests in `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` so they no longer mock the removed env var.
- Migrated weekly and nightly e2e YAML configs to `additional_config.enable_flashcomm1` and checked that each node's previous on/off state is unchanged.
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][Model] Make MiniMax-M3 prefill KV-gather-Q optional on A5
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow up on #14685: A3 already falls back when the experimental Split-KV package is absent, but A5 currently skips the availability check and unconditionally calls the vendor prefill entry point.

- Select the prefill path by optional Split-KV ACLNN availability before building K2Q, without a separate device allowlist. Remove the unused `MINIMAX_M3_PREFILL_KV_GATHER_Q` capability declaration and registrations; retain `FP8_ATTENTION` for dtype validation and existing precision-mode selection.
- Use the existing Q-gather-KV prefill path when the package is unavailable.
- Extend that fallback to A5 E4M3 KV caches: cast/clamp Q consistently with decode, supply unit dequantization scales, and return BF16 output. Variable per-request query lengths and the original `-1` top-k sentinels are preserved.
- Harden the native availability probe: require both entry points from the same provider and reject the **known metadata-enabled experimental ABI**, which adds `metadataOptional` to the workspace-size signature without renaming the entry point. Inspect the selected provider so a lower-priority incompatible library does not disable a compatible provider.

This does not add support for the metadata-enabled ABI or attempt universal ABI detection. It safely falls back for that known incompatible package. Compatible packages retain the current KV-gather-Q path. Precision modes and decode are unchanged. The dedicated KV-gather-Q hardware capability is removed; other capability definitions, including `FP8_ATTENTION`, are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MiniMax-M3 A5 prefill no longer requires the optional experimental Split-KV package: it can use Q-gather-KV with BF16 or E4M3 KV caches.

Dispatch now depends solely on the ACLNN availability probe, not the former A3/A5 capability allowlist. A device previously excluded by that allowlist will also attempt KV-gather-Q if the probe succeeds. Users must install a package containing kernels for the actual SoC: the probe does not verify device-kernel compatibility, and execution errors are not automatically caught and retried on the fallback path. The mocked A2 dispatch test verifies routing only, not A2 hardware support.

To enable KV-gather-Q, install a **compatible** experimental package, source its environment, and restart the workers. No source-code change or new environment switch is needed. The availability result and loader search paths are cached per process; installing a package into an already running worker is not supported.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python -m pytest tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py -q`: **89 passed** on CPU, using the repository's verified vLLM revision `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`.
- Added regression coverage for A5 with/without Split-KV, BF16/FP8 fallback across tensor/tuple/list caches, variable query lengths, invalid FP8 inputs, and ensuring fallback calls neither K2Q nor Split-KV. Updated dispatch coverage for A2/A3/A5 and the hardware-profile tests after removing the dedicated capability.
- Compiled and exercised the exact C++ availability function against synthetic ELF providers: **8 cases passed**, covering missing/partial entry points, compatible/incompatible providers, mixed providers, and both library-priority orders. An additional null-filename fault-injection case passed, confirming that a successful `dladdr` with `dli_fname == nullptr` returns false without calling `dlopen`.
- Inspected the supplied metadata-enabled A3/A5 package headers and ELF exports to confirm the changed signature and metadata entry-point marker.
- Changed `torch_binding.cpp` passed `-fsyntax-only` using the existing A5 CANN/PyTorch build toolchain. This is not a complete wheel rebuild.
- Ruff check/format and `git diff --check`: passed for the changed files.
- `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but could not bootstrap its GitHub-hosted hooks: this server's connection to GitHub timed out. Full pre-commit validation remains for CI.
- **NPU execution and GPQA were not rerun for this patch** because the available A5 devices are occupied by another service. Hardware/CI validation is still required before merging; prior A5 validation is not presented as a test of this patch.

title: [BugFix][MoE] Guard fused MC2 dispatch against silent capacity truncation
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes silent output corruption in the fused MC2 MoE path (`enable_fused_mc2=1`) for long-context prefill.

**Root cause.** The `dispatch_ffn_combine` op sizes its internal per-rank token buffers from `max_output_size` and **silently discards work** once the per-rank post-dispatch token count reaches it:

```cpp
if (preCurrentmSum >= params.maxOutputSize) { currentM = 0; }
else if (preCurrentmSum + currentM > params.maxOutputSize)
    currentM = params.maxOutputSize - preCurrentmSum;
```

No error is raised — the affected tokens simply receive a corrupted MoE output, which surfaces as repeated/garbage tokens (issue #16941) and destroys the argmax margin.

`additional_config.mega_moe_max_tokens` is documented (`ascend_config.py`) as sizing **both** the op's `max_output_size` **and** the CANN MegaMoe symmetric buffer's `max_recv_token_num`, but only the op side was effectively guarded. The mean post-dispatch count per rank is `num_tokens * num_experts_per_tok`; measured load reaches **~4.9x that mean** on GLM-5.2 w4a8 / A3 / EP16, so the historical `65536` default does not cover long-context prefill chunks.

**Measured** (GLM-5.2-w4a8, A3, EP16, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` with 4-way context parallelism → 2048 tokens per rank per op call, topk 8):

| | per-rank post-dispatch load |
|---|---|
| median | 14,923 |
| p99 | 44,332 |
| max | 70,990 |
| single expert max | 31,711 (4.3x mean, **108% of the 65536 default**) |

Same service, same 67531-token request, greedy, 512 tokens:

| op capacity | peer buffer | truncated calls | clean requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 65536 | 65536 | 9 / 58800 | 0 / 6 |
| **131072** | 65536 | 0 / 58800 | 6 / 6 |
| 131072 | 131072 | — | 6 / 6 |

Reproduced independently with `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192` on a 67531-token prompt: **273/288 op calls truncated and 28/288 produced NaN rows**, while the same request with `65536` answers correctly.

**Changes:**

- `_fused_mc2_required_capacity()` — rank-invariant lower bound derived **only from compile-time configuration** (the symmetric buffer is allocated by a collective handshake, so every EP rank must compute the same value):
  `max(token_dispatcher.max_num_tokens_per_rank, global_bs // ep_world_size, max_num_batched_tokens // tensor_parallel_size) * num_experts_per_tok * 8`. Cached, logged once.
- `_fused_mc2_capacity()` — `max(configured, required)` plus a one-time warning naming both buffers and the `--max-num-batched-tokens` alternative.
- Use it for **both** the op's `max_output_size` and the P / PD-mixed peer buffer (`max_recv_token_num`), instead of the raw configured value.
- `_verify_fused_mc2_no_truncation()` — raise instead of returning silently corrupted tokens. Skipped when truncation is provably impossible (`num_tokens * topk * ep_world_size < max_output_size`), so the decode path stays free of device syncs.
- Pass a **copy** of `topk_ids` as `expert_idx`: the op rewrites non-active entries in place (`ApplyXActiveMask` writes `expertPerRank * EP`), mutating the caller's routing tensor.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

Yes, two ways:

1. **Long-context prefill output changes** — previously silently corrupted under the fused MC2 path, now correct.
2. **Memory cost**: raising the capacity from `65536` to `131072` takes **21632 KV cache tokens** on this model (207744 → 186112, **−10.4%**), because the operator workspace and the peer buffer scale linearly with the value. Lowering `--max-num-batched-tokens` shrinks the requirement by the same factor if the KV cache is needed. A one-time warning states the value in use and how to silence it.

Previously valid configurations keep their exact behaviour when the computed requirement does not exceed the configured value.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Operator capacity A/B** (table above): identical request, capacity switched at runtime — `65536` → 9/58800 truncated, 0/6 clean; `131072` → 0/58800 truncated, 6/6 clean.
- **Minimal repro** with `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192` on a 67531-token prompt: 273/288 calls truncated + 28/288 NaN rows before; correct after.
- **Changing the op capacity alone** is sufficient for this workload, which confirms silent truncation is the root cause of the garbled long-context output. The peer buffer is raised as well so both stay consistent, as the vendor comment requires.

### Remaining (not addressed here, needs the operator side)

The fused MC2 path is **still not bit-reproducible**. Two identical greedy prefills of the same 67531-token prompt disagree on **17–36%** of positions at capacity `65536` and on **1–2%** at `131072` (top-1 agreement 0.64–0.83 per position bin), while `enable_fused_mc2=0` is bit-exact. The truncation fix roughly halves the drift but does not remove it.

### Related

- Issue #16941 — garbled / repeated tokens from silent truncation
- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py` — `mega_moe_max_tokens` documentation

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][SpecDecode] Preserve tensor state when skipping drafts
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up to #16512. When drafting is skipped, the current code stores a Python list of empty drafts. Async scheduling can already have reserved speculative placeholders for the next step. The inherited GPUModelRunner._prepare_input_ids requires a Tensor to scatter those slots and asserts on the list.

- Pass SchedulerOutput into _skip_drafting.
- Publish an int32 zero Tensor on the runner device with shape (num_reqs, configured num_spec_tokens).
- Call the existing _copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu(..., zeros_only=True), refreshing the actual draft stride before its async early return and publishing CPU zeros/request IDs/events only when needed.
- Preserve sampled-token/count updates and DP dummy behavior; clear stale draft probabilities as before.

The full configured width covers all reserved slots, including reduced per-step speculative widths. The zeros are draft candidates/placeholders for normal target verification, not directly emitted output tokens. This follows the representation already used on the 0.26 branch.

Add regression coverage for skip -> next async input preparation with reordered requests and 1/3/5 speculative slots; verify sampled tokens and zeros reach the correct positions. Exercise real CPU publication logic for sync, structured output, penalties, and PP, including event recording and untouched unused buffer rows. Check that stale previous draft width is refreshed even when CPU publication is skipped.

Scope: no max-model-length threshold change, no removal of assertions, and no unrelated n-gram state-handling change. The reported 131072 input + 1024 output with max_model_len=133120 does not by itself prove that overflow occurred. Runtime SHA, actual metadata length and effective drafter limit are still needed to attribute that incident.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Prevents a next-step Tensor assertion after the drafter-length skip path. Normal drafting and configuration remain unchanged. No accuracy or performance improvement is claimed without NPU evaluation.

### How was this patch tested?

- Changed-file Ruff lint/format, Python compileall, and git diff --check: passed.
- CPU AST-isolated diagnostic executed the actual Ascend methods and TestDrafterMaxModelLen class against the inherited upstream _prepare_input_ids from this branch's verified vLLM pin (84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c): 12 tests passed. Tensor operations ran on CPU; NPU stream/event APIs and distributed groups were mocked. This is NOT full pytest or NPU execution.
- The pre-fix 0.27 implementation reproduced the inherited Tensor assertion for 1/3/5 reserved slots in the isolated regression; the fixed implementation passed.
- Full command: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py -k TestDrafterMaxModelLen`. Blocked during conftest import by `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'vllm'` on this Windows host.
- `bash format.sh ci` was attempted with Git Bash, but timed out during actionlint environment setup / pre-commit cache-lock waiting. Only the newly started lint process trees were stopped; full lint is not claimed to pass.
- NPU end-to-end, long-context accuracy, performance and the reported workload reproduction remain pending. Keep as draft pending validation and human review.

AI assistance was used to implement and inspect these changes. The submitter must review the changes and test intent before requesting review.

title: [MRV2][BugFix][Kernel] Fix and optimize sampling mask packing on Ascend
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The sampling-mask kernel can overflow UB on Triton-Ascend when
`logits.stride(1) > 1`. For a batch-32, vocabulary-151936, stride-2
input, the original BLOCK_SIZE=8192 kernel fails compilation with:

`ub overflow, requires 12583424 bits while 1572864 bits available`

The implementation also has two Ascend-specific lowering issues:

- reducing the boolean keep mask does not produce the required finite-logit
  count;
- per-element variable shifts and the `[512, 8]` axis-1 reduction lower to
  scalar-heavy execution.

This PR adds an Ascend implementation for both the three-field bitmask API
and the four-field compact-ID plus bitmask API. Both interfaces launch the
same Ascend packing kernel. It:

- makes only strided vocabulary inputs contiguous, without modifying the
  caller's tensor;
- casts the keep mask to int32 before reduction;
- uses BLOCK_SIZE=4096 to remain within the NPU UB limit;
- transposes the packing layout from `[512, 8]` to `[8, 512]`, multiplies by
  compile-time bit weights, and reduces axis 0;
- routes both sampling-mask APIs through the same Ascend packing kernel;
- returns a zero-width `token_ids` tensor for the four-field API so its existing
  `tolists()` method uses the exact packed-mask fallback;
- logs a warning once per process when the four-field compact token-ID path is
  requested;
- adds operator documentation and registers the NPU regression test in the
  A2 single-card nightly matrix.

The four-field compatibility path preserves sampling results but temporarily
gives up the compact token-ID transfer optimization on Ascend. It avoids the
`tl.cumsum`-based dynamic scatter that hangs with Triton-Ascend 3.2.2.

The following msprof results use an Ascend 910, `npu:0`, 10 profiling
rounds, and `MemoryDetail,Occupancy,PipeUtilization,Roofline`. Values are
selected kernel task durations and exclude Python wrapper time and the
preceding contiguous copy.

| Case | Baseline | Optimized | Speedup | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `b1_v17_active1_colstride1` | 123.330 us | 5.640 us | 21.87x | 95.43% |
| `b8_v8191_active1_colstride1` | 244.573 us | 6.960 us | 35.14x | 97.15% |
| `b8_v8192_active1_colstride1` | 244.327 us | 6.680 us | 36.58x | 97.27% |
| `b8_v8193_active1_colstride1` | 365.349 us | 8.940 us | 40.87x | 97.55% |
| `b8_v8193_active0_colstride1` | 365.357 us | 8.780 us | 41.61x | 97.60% |
| `b32_v151936_active1_colstride2` | 4604.258 us | 84.758 us | 54.32x | 98.16% |
| `b128_v151936_active1_colstride1` | 18403.968 us | 327.093 us | 56.27x | 98.22% |

The original stride-2 BLOCK_SIZE=8192 implementation has no runtime
duration because it fails compilation with UB overflow. The table uses
the first compilable correctness-fixed implementation with the original
variable-shift packing as the performance baseline.

TTIR/NPU IR inspection confirms that the optimized packing lowers to
vector transpose, multiply, and reduction operations; the previous
tensor-wide scalar shift loop is absent.

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Correctness revalidation environment:

- Ascend 910
- Python 3.12.13
- Torch 2.10.0
- torch-npu 2.10.0.post4
- Triton-Ascend 3.2.2
- CANN 9.1.0

The NPU regression test passed against both version-specific interfaces:

- pinned vLLM main `84030bbe3` four-field API: `4 passed`.

The performance data above was collected with Triton-Ascend 3.2.2.

The regression test verifies:

- random sparse token positions and a vocabulary size not divisible by eight;
- active and inactive rows, including `num_sampled_tokens > 1`;
- NaN and positive/negative infinity exclusion;
- non-contiguous `logits` with `stride(1) == 2` and an unmodified caller view;
- exact packed masks, counts, and decoded token IDs;

title: [Refactor][Ops] Replace custom LI and MoE operators with CANN native operators
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Replace the remaining plugin-owned quantized Lightning Indexer and standard MoE gating kernels with the corresponding CANN operators exposed by `torch_npu`. This removes duplicate kernel code and its build and Torch registration paths.

- `BaseDeviceAdaptor` now calls `torch_npu.npu_quant_lightning_indexer` for the quantized Lightning Indexer path. Both the base and A5 paths pass `INT64_MAX` for the native `pre_tokens` and `next_tokens` arguments; A5 already used this native operator before this PR.
- `BaseDeviceAdaptor.moe_gating_top_k` now calls `torch_npu.npu_moe_gating_top_k`, maps `bias_opt` to the native `bias` argument, forwards the other routing options, and continues returning expert IDs as `int32`. The existing A5 override is unchanged.
- Remove the `lightning_indexer_quant` and `moe_gating_top_k` custom kernel directories, their `build_aclnn.sh` entries, and the `_C_ascend.npu_lightning_indexer_quant` and `_C_ascend.moe_gating_top_k` bindings and meta implementations. The hash router and quantized Lightning Indexer V2 implementation remain.
- Update the MoE device and nightly tests to exercise the adapter and update the SFA unit test to check the native LI call arguments.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. The affected paths use the CANN operators through `torch_npu`. The `DeviceOperator` interface remains, including `int32` expert IDs for standard MoE gating. Direct calls to the removed private `torch.ops._C_ascend.moe_gating_top_k` and `torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_lightning_indexer_quant` schemas need to migrate to the native APIs.

### How was this patch tested?

The results below were recorded before the 2026-09-23 rebase onto vLLM Ascend `main` at `4cc4e0ef7`. After rebasing, `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed. UT and NPU tests were not rerun after the rebase, as requested.

Test environment: CANN 9.2.0-beta.2, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, Ascend 910B4-1.

```bash
python3 setup.py build_ext

PYTHONPATH=/dev/shm/vllm_verified_a97dacb \
  pytest -q tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py --maxfail=1
# 47 passed

ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
PYTHONPATH=/dev/shm/vllm_verified_a97dacb \
  pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_npu_moe_gating_top_k.py \
  --maxfail=1
# 216 passed
```

 Validated on DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8 with TP16 and LI C8 enabled: inference requests completed successfully, and runtime logs confirmed calls to both native CANN operators.

### Kernel performance comparison

This pre-rebase comparison was run on CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 and Ascend 910B4-1 with isolated old/native processes. Each case used 50 warmups and 20 `torch_npu.profiler` samples; the reported value is the median target-kernel `Duration(us)`, excluding input generation, H2D copies, compilation, correctness checks, and profiler setup. CV is the population standard deviation divided by the sample mean.

- `lightning_indexer_quant`: 19 eligible cases covering prefill/decode, variable lengths, sparse counts, 127/128/129 block boundaries, TND and PA_BSND layouts, masked/unmasked modes, and tied scores. Across all cases, the old/native median kernel durations were `24.98 us / 22.87 us`. Representative measurements were `19.99 us / 15.38 us` at the 128-token block boundary and `42.94 us / 41.70 us` for the long sparse case. The two non-64-head cases were excluded because the old custom kernel raised an AICore address/UB error before profiling.
- `moe_gating_top_k`: 292 cases covering the baseline matrix plus large shapes, FP32/FP16/BF16, bias, group configurations, Softmax/Sigmoid, renorm, `out_flag`, and routed scaling factors. Across all cases, the old/native median kernel durations were `3.70 us / 4.40 us`; for the 16 large-shape cases they were `18.15 us / 18.75 us`. Representative large cases were `64.90 us / 64.55 us` for FP16 2048x256 and `119.30 us / 119.87 us` for FP16 2048x512. The measurements are in the same microsecond range overall; the native implementation does not show a general MoE kernel-time improvement in this matrix.

The complete per-case kernel tables and raw CSV/JSON results are retained with the test artifacts used for this comparison. These results are kernel-only and eager-mode; no graph capture/replay performance claim is made.
