title: [BugFix][Model] Apply DeepSeek-V4 attention sinks through the weight loader
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Split out of #16355 (first of three PRs).

A live/layerwise weight update runs inside vLLM's layerwise reload: the layer is parked on the meta device, and only writes made through `param.weight_loader` are buffered and replayed by `finalize_layerwise_reload`. DeepSeek-V4's sink branches wrote the attention sink with a direct `param.data.copy_` / `copy_`, which bypasses that buffer and lands on the meta tensor, so the write was silently dropped.

Consequence: after any live weight update the attention sinks kept their dummy initialisation (the ±1e-3 `initialize_dummy_weights` values, visible as absmean 5.3e-4 instead of the transferred 1.0e-2). A parameter-level diff between a server that loads the transferred payload at startup and one that received the same payload live showed exactly that: `model.layers.{0..3}.self_attn.attn_sink` stayed at the dummy values while every other parameter matched. The DeepSeek-V4 lane of the weight-update E2E oracle added in #16355 cannot pass without this fix.

Changes:

- Route the sink through the parameter's loader, keeping the existing `enable_dsa_cp()` (full sink) and per-rank narrow semantics. A plain parameter falls back to `default_weight_loader`, which is the same copy as before, so normal startup loading is unchanged. All three copies of the branch are fixed: the target model (`model.py`), the MTP head (`mtp.py`) and the DSpark draft (`dspark.py`), which previously used a slicing `copy_` and had the same problem.
- Add `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_weight_loader_reload.py`: it drives the real `load_weights` over a model whose parameter set is exactly one sink and pins both behaviours — with a `weight_loader` the per-rank narrowed tensor must reach the loader and not `param.data`, and a plain parameter must keep the previous default-loader semantics. It covers the target model and the MTP copy.

The sink is a plain parameter, so the loader it resolves to is vLLM's `default_weight_loader`, which only asserts the shapes and copies. Tensor parallel sharding stays owned by `load_weights`: the checkpoint ships one sink per head and each rank receives `num_attention_heads // tp_size` consecutive heads starting at `tp_rank * heads_per_rank`. That arithmetic is untouched by this PR, and the unit test now pins the offset at TP > 1 so a future change that re-partitions an already narrowed sink (for example swapping in `row_parallel_weight_loader`, which narrows 1-D parameters as well) fails instead of silently sharding twice.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Behaviour only changes for layerwise/live reloads, where the sink write previously did nothing.

### How was this patch tested?

**NPU container run (Ascend 910, torch 2.10 + torch_npu, python 3.12.13):**

- `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_weight_loader_reload.py` — **45 passed**. The sink branch is exercised for tensor parallel TP=1, 2, 4 and 8 (every rank) for the target model and for the MTP copy, asserting the per-rank slice that reaches the weight loader, that the loader is used instead of `param.data`, and that a plain parameter still falls back to the default loader. The test imports and runs the real `AscendDeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights` / `DeepSeekV4MTP.load_weights`, not a copy of the branch.
- Regression on the neighbouring suites with the same overlay applied: `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_moe.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_indexer.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_compressor.py` — **24 passed**; `tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer/` — **73 passed**.
- The run was executed from a standalone directory with the repository's `tests/ut/conftest.py` disabled, because that conftest fails during `adapt_patch()` on the container's current vLLM checkout (`ImportError: cannot import name 'SituAndMul'`), which is unrelated to this change. Afterwards the container tree was restored to its pre-run state and verified: the three touched files match their backups byte for byte and the pushed test file was removed.

The startup-load oracle E2E in the follow-up PR reported "first live weight update does not match normal startup loading of the same weights" before this change and passes after it, on Ascend 910 with the DeepSeek-V4-Flash reduced case (NPU IPC, packed and unpacked).

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `py_compile` pass on the changed files; `git diff --check` is clean.

Refs #16355, #16322.

title: [Performance][DSpark] Stack DeepSeek V4 context WKV projections
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR ports the DeepSeek V4 DSpark context WKV stacking optimization from upstream vLLM:

* Upstream PR: vllm-project/vllm#54674

In the current vLLM Ascend DSpark implementation, each draft layer independently applies its WKV projection to the same `context_states`.

This PR stacks the per-layer WKV projections into a single `MergedColumnParallelLinear` projection and splits the result back into per-layer KV states before the existing per-layer KV normalization, RoPE, and KV-cache insertion logic.

Conceptually, this changes the context WKV path from multiple small projections:

```text
X -> WKV_0
X -> WKV_1
X -> WKV_2
```

to one stacked projection:

```text
X -> [WKV_0 | WKV_1 | WKV_2]
```

The goal is to reduce projection launches and improve GEMM utilization on Ascend while preserving the existing DSpark KV-cache semantics.

Compared with the upstream NVIDIA implementation, vLLM Ascend already uses an independent `wkv` projection rather than a fused Q/KV projection, so this PR only ports the cross-layer WKV stacking optimization.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No.

This is an internal DSpark performance optimization and is intended to preserve model outputs and speculative decoding behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

Current status:

* [ ] Unit tests
* [ ] DeepSeek V4 DSpark model loading on Ascend
* [ ] Functional / correctness verification
* [ ] Performance benchmark on Ascend 910B

1. Per-layer WKV checkpoint parameters are duplicated into the corresponding shards of the stacked projection.
2. Context WKV projection is executed once and its output is split correctly for individual DSpark layers.

Performance and full Ascend verification results will be added to this PR before it is marked ready for review.

The goal is to reduce projection launches and improve GEMM utilization on Ascend while preserving the existing DSpark KV-cache semantics.

Compared with the upstream NVIDIA implementation, vLLM Ascend already uses an independent `wkv` projection rather than a fused Q/KV projection, so this PR only ports the cross-layer WKV stacking optimization.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No.

This is an internal DSpark performance optimization and is intended to preserve model outputs and speculative decoding behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

Current status:

* [ ] Unit tests
* [ ] DeepSeek V4 DSpark model loading on Ascend
* [ ] Functional / correctness verification
* [ ] Performance benchmark on Ascend 910B

A unit test is included to verify that:

1. Per-layer WKV checkpoint parameters are duplicated into the corresponding shards of the stacked projection.
2. Context WKV projection is executed once and its output is split correctly for individual DSpark layers.

Performance and full Ascend verification results will be added to this PR before it is marked ready for review.

title: [Performance][GDN] Share group-invariant metadata across kv-cache groups
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Background**

Hybrid models such as Qwen3.8 / Qwen4-Exp (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B) interleave
GDN (linear-attention) layers and full-attention layers at 3:1. The hybrid KV cache
manager aligns kv-cache group sizes to the least-numerous layer type, which splits
the GDN layers across **3 kv-cache groups**. As a result, `_build_attn_group_metadata`
invokes the GDN metadata builder's `build()` once per group on **every step**.

Within a single `_build_attention_metadata` call, every GDN group receives an
identical `common_attn_metadata` **except its own `block_table_tensor` /
`slot_mapping`**. However, the full metadata pipeline is executed 3x per step:

- spec sequence classification + fold (1 `.item()` host sync per group)
- batch statistics (4 `.item()` host syncs per group)
- stable argsort + `repeat_interleave` token reorder
- spec / non-spec `query_start_loc` cumsums and accepted-token reorder
- chunked-prefill chunk indices/offsets (6 CPU `prepare_*` calls + H2D per group)
- causal conv1d metadata and `has_initial_state`

**What this PR changes**

- Add `GDNGroupInvariantCache` to `gdn_attn_builder.py`.
- `AscendGDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` accepts an optional
  `group_invariant_cache` argument.
- The model runner creates one cache before the kv-cache-group loop and passes it
  to every GDN group's build. The **first group (fingerprint miss) performs the
  full build and fills the cache**; subsequent groups **reuse the group-invariant
  intermediates and only recompute the state-index tensors derived from their own
  block table**.

Effect per step: host-device syncs drop from 3x5 to 5; the argsort,
chunked-prefill metadata and conv1d metadata drop from 3x to 1x.

**Safety properties**

- Only block-table-independent results are cached. `spec_state_indices_tensor`,
  `non_spec_state_indices_tensor` and `prefill_state_indices` are always
  recomputed from each group's own block table.
- Cached tensors are shared read-only; per-group full-graph padding still writes
  each builder's own persistent buffers, so captured graph addresses are unchanged.
- An O(1) shape-level fingerprint falls back to a full build on any mismatch.
- Callers that pass no cache (drafting, cudagraph capture, external callers)
  keep the original path unchanged.
- Guarded to non-ubatched calls (`ubid is None`): the shape-level fingerprint
  cannot distinguish same-shaped ubatches, so ubatched GDN builds fall back to
  full computation instead of silently reusing stale entries.

This mirrors the existing DSA precedent (`shared_dsa_draft_cache`).

### Benchmark

**GDN metadata `build()` per-step cost** (single forward):
- **Before**: all 3 kv-cache groups each run the full build, ~`2.1 ms/group`, total `6.3 ms`.
- **After**: the first group still builds fully (`2.1 ms`); the 2nd and 3rd groups
  reuse the cache (`1.2 ms` each), total `4.5 ms`.
- Saves **~1.8 ms / step (≈28.6%)** per forward. With speculative decoding
  (MTP, k=3) this is another forward per step, so the wall-clock benefit compounds.

**End-to-end benchmark** — Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, TP=2, 8k-token random input, 350 output tokens:

| Metric                | Before   | After    | Δ        |
|-----------------------|----------|----------|----------|
| Throughput (tokens/s) | 222.28   | 227.36   | +2.29%   |
| TTFT (ms)             | 1162.65  | 1156.24  | -0.55%   |
| TPOT (ms)             | 23.21    | 22.74    | -2.03%   |
| E2E Latency (ms)      | 9262.48  | 9094.04  | -1.82%   |

Throughput improves by **+2.29%**, and TTFT / TPOT / E2E latency all drop
(by roughly 0.6% ~ 2%). The win comes entirely from removing the redundant
host-device syncs (`.item()`), the repeated NPU argsort, and the duplicated
chunked-prefill / conv1d metadata across the 3 GDN groups.

**Accuracy regression check** — GPQA-diamond benchmark:

| Dataset       | Before | After |
|--------------|--------|-------|
| GPQA-diamond | 0.8622 | 0.868 |

Accuracy is preserved (0.8622 → 0.868), confirming the metadata reuse does not
degrade output quality.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is a pure internal optimization of attention metadata construction.
No API, configuration or behavior change. The produced metadata is field-by-field
identical to the original full build (verified by UTs).

title: - [Feature] Materialize only the local padded MC2 input shard
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

MC2 preparation currently pads the complete hidden-state and router-logit tensors before selecting the local tensor-parallel shard. With one decode token and TP=4, each rank materializes four rows while consuming only one.

This PR computes the local shard boundaries first and materializes only the required data:

- Fully valid shards return contiguous slices.
- Fully padded shards allocate independent local zero tensors.
- Partially valid shards pad only their local slice.

The implementation preserves `torch.tensor_split` semantics, including uneven splits, global padded shapes, MC2 masks, and the finalize contract. The sequence-parallel / `replace_allreduce` path remains unchanged.

#### Performance

Prior serving A/B measurements of this implementation used GLM-5.2 W4A8 on Ascend 910C with TP=4 and fused MC2 enabled. Both versions already included the RoPE contiguous-cache optimization; the candidate added only this MC2 padding change.

| Input tokens | Output tokens | Requests / concurrency | Baseline TPOT (ms) | Optimized TPOT (ms) | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100000 | 1024 | 4 / 4 | 52.1215 | 49.9419 | 4.18% |
| 8192 | 512 | 8 / 8 | 52.9287 | 50.5735 | 4.45% |

Each value is the median of three per-round **mean TPOT** measurements, using matched seeds 42/43/44. Profiling was disabled during timing.

These measurements were collected on the deployment branch before porting to community main. They represent short, fixed-load workloads, not saturation-throughput results. Prefix caches were not reset.

Profile inspection also confirmed that the targeted full-tensor padding Concat operations disappeared on the inspected DP0 TP0/TP1 ranks.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API, configuration, or environment-variable changes.

The optimization applies when MC2 preparation requires padding and TP > 1. Zero-only outputs use independent storage, avoiding shared mutable padding buffers.

### How was this patch tested?

The ported community-main source passed:

- **230 unit tests**, covering empty and noncontiguous inputs, FP32/FP16/BF16, TP sizes 1/2/4/8, uneven splits, masks, global padded shapes, and existing prepare/finalize behavior.
- **12 NPU graph tests**, covering all four TP ranks and three dtypes, with changing input values and alternating graph sizes.
- All applicable pre-commit checks for the three changed files.

Commands:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/ops/test_mc2_local_padding.py \
  tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py

python -m pytest -q \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_mc2_local_padding.py
```

Prior serving regression checks passed 12/12 cases for both versions, with identical answers and token sequences. This was a correctness smoke test, not a comprehensive model-accuracy evaluation.

Full-tree `bash format.sh ci` encountered an existing duplicate `pp_rank` parameter in `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py:63`. The error is also present in the unmodified base commit and is unrelated to this PR.

title: [Feature][MRV2] Support o_proj TP in model runner v2 (graph-mode scope)
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enables `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` (fine-grained TP for the attention output projection) on model runner v2, scoped to its real deployment: a PD decode node (`tp == 1`, `dp > 1`, MoE) running a graph mode with the recompute scheduler.

The o_proj exchange (`all_to_all` → partial GEMM → `reduce_scatter`) is an `all_to_all_single` without split sizes: every rank must forward the same number of tokens per step, or the collectives hang silently. In graph mode the upstream dispatch already guarantees that group-uniform count, so this PR adds no runner-side padding — it adds the contract that keeps the count uniform, and guardrails that turn a silent hang into an explicit failure:

1. Graph mode is required: `cudagraph_mode == NONE` (which covers `enforce_eager`) is rejected at config load.
2. Capture-bound check: the knob is kept only if the largest capture size covers the largest possible step (`min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs * decode_query_len)`); otherwise it is disabled with a warning and the deployment still starts.
3. A guard at the top of `NPUModelRunner.prepare_inputs` — the only post-dispatch hook, reached by real steps only — raises an explicit `RuntimeError` if a step still dispatches to eager. Armed only for a real split (`> 1`).
4. PCP (`prefill_context_parallel_size > 1`) is rejected: its per-rank token recount breaks the uniform step size.
5. With `> 1`, the KV connector chain must carry `PreemptOffloadConnector` — startup fails without it — and an offload failure at preemption aborts the request instead of sending it back to P. Checked in `platform._check_ascend_config` because MultiConnector children re-derive the config from per-child copies that cannot see their siblings.

Existing preconditions unchanged: PD decode node (`is_kv_consumer`), `recompute_scheduler_enable=true`, `tensor_parallel_size == 1`, MoE.

Depends on #17128 (reclassifies the request-arrival boundary recompute as decode, so those steps stay on captured graphs); this PR is meant to land after it.

### Design conclusions (aligned with the SE)

The scope and guardrails of this PR implement conclusions aligned with the SE:

1. **No MRV1 parity goal.** Fine-grained TP is adapted to model runner v2 only where necessary and reasonable; the bar is expected functional correctness, not parity with MRV1.
2. **Preconditions are enforced at config load.** `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` requires the recompute scheduler, preempt offload, a graph mode, and a pure-DP PD decode deployment (`tp == 1`, `dp > 1`).
3. **No eager fallback from an oversized step.** A step whose token count exceeds the largest captured size dispatches to eager in every graph mode; a conservative config-time check verifies the capture bound covers the largest possible step and disables the knob otherwise. Other fine-grained TP knobs can follow the same pattern.
4. **No return-to-P fallback under this feature.** Recompute preemption is paired with offload; the stock path sends the request back to P when the offload itself fails. This feature rejects that branch — recomputation on P cannot guarantee computation equivalence — and fails the request immediately with an explicit error instead.
5. **`PreemptOffloadConnector` is mandatory.** Config load rejects a real split whose KV connector chain does not carry it.

### Memory cost and expected savings

The memory profile belongs to the feature, not to this PR — the validation and guard paths allocate no device memory. Measured on the test bed (DeepSeek-V3.1-arch W8A8 checkpoint truncated to 6 layers, `dp8 × tp1`, graph mode, identical connector config; per rank):

| Item | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed cost: HCCL buffers of the o_proj TP communication group | ~0.42 GB | measured (steady-state device delta; the freed weight is cancelled by the larger KV pool); allocated at graph-capture time |
| Weight saving per layer, 1-byte (W8A8/FP8) checkpoint | 0.109 GiB × (1 − 1/N) | measured: 0.33 GiB @ `oproj=2`, 0.49 GiB @ `oproj=4` on 6 layers |
| Full 61-layer extrapolation, W8A8/FP8, `oproj=8` | ~5.8 GB gross, ~5.4 GB net of the fixed cost | from the measured per-layer slope |
| Net savings, DeepSeek-R1-W8A8, `oproj=8` | 5.8 GB | feature guide (`Fine_grained_TP.md`) |
| DeepSeek-V3/R1 BF16, `oproj=8` | ~11.2 GiB net | from checkpoint dims (0.219 GiB per layer) |

The freed weight memory returns to the KV cache, and the fixed cost is recovered after ~8 layers at `oproj=2` (~4 at `oproj=8`) on a 1-byte quantized checkpoint — trivially met by production-scale MoE models.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` now works on the V2 runner in graph-mode PD-decode deployments; previously it was V1-only.
- New config-load rejections: `cudagraph_mode=none` / `enforce_eager`, `prefill_context_parallel_size > 1`, and — for a real split — a KV connector chain without `PreemptOffloadConnector`.
- Capture-bound auto-disable with a warning instead of rejection; raise `max_cudagraph_capture_size` to use the knob at large `max_num_seqs`.
- An eagerly dispatched step now fails the request with an explicit error instead of hanging; an offload failure at preemption aborts the request instead of returning it to P.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests**: new cases in `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` (graph-mode / PCP rejection, size-1 exemption, capture-bound matrix), `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_finegrained_tp.py` (eager-step guard contract) and `tests/ut/core/test_recompute_scheduler.py` (offload-failure abort). CI on the current head: `pre-commit` (incl. mypy) and `cpu-ut` green (5718 passed, 67 skipped).

**End-to-end** (single-node A3, 16 chips, PD disaggregation behind the LB proxy, 8-layer MiniMax-M3 with dummy weights — functional/consistency numbers, not real-weight performance): P = chip 0, `tp1` eager, Mooncake producer; D = chips 8-15, `dp8 × tp1`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` + recompute scheduler + `oproj_tensor_parallel_size=2`, Mooncake consumer; all traffic through the proxy.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| config rejections | graph-mode and PD-scenario rejections fail startup with explicit messages; `--max-num-seqs 600` (600 > 512) auto-disables the knob with a warning and startup continues into graph capture |
| continuous PD traffic, `oproj=2` | 100% of requests completed, guard fired 0 times, decode ran on captured FULL graphs, engine TPOT cc1/cc8 median 7.21 / 7.58 ms (990.7 tok/s at cc8) |
| vs `oproj=0` baseline | TPOT +0.07 ms (~1%); outputs token-identical on 5 fixed prompts in every round |
| negative control (same topology without #17128) | the first arrival step dispatches to eager → explicit `RuntimeError` within 3.7 s, no hang |
| offload chain (`MultiConnector`: Mooncake + `PreemptOffloadConnector`) | starts, graph capture OK, cc8 7.67 ms / 943 tok/s, outputs identical, CPU offload pool active on 8/8 decode ranks |
| tight-KV sweeps (`gpu-memory-utilization` 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.35, 100 MB CPU pool) | 100% of requests completed, outputs identical, no crash |

**Left uncovered** (for honesty): the preemption/offload runtime path (KV save/restore and the capacity fallback) was not triggered — preemption is unreachable on the 8-layer dummy model — so the abort-instead-of-return-to-P branch is covered by unit tests only; and the without-connector startup failure is a config-load check that has not been reproduced e2e yet (it was observed on the test bed while the check still warned).

title: [Performance][DSV4] Reuse filtered RoPE lookups
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR removes redundant DeepSeek V4 RoPE table indexing that remains on current main.

- adds an optional layer filter to `get_cos_and_sin_dsa` so draft attention queries only the RoPE config consumed by its layers
- resolves draft `*.swa_cache` layer names to their registered `*.attn` RoPE layer
- computes the ordinary RoPE cos/sin pair once before the DSpark context-KV layer loop and reuses it across all draft layers
- preserves existing target common/decode caching already present on current main

Current main has already absorbed part of the older optimization design, so this PR deliberately excludes that existing logic. It is independent of the block-table dirty-copy PR.

An earlier DSV4 DP16 decode profile showed that eliminating 26 redundant Index/IndexCheck pairs saved approximately 1.19 ms/step. On current main, only the draft config filtering and cross-layer context-KV reuse remain applicable, so a fresh profile is required before making a current-main performance claim.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or output change. RoPE values are queried for the same positions and config; the result is reused by layers that share that config.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added unit coverage verifying layer-based config filtering and `swa_cache` to `attn` resolution.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed: Ruff check/format, codespell, typos, gitleaks, import and policy checks, and DCO sign-off.

title: [Performance][GDN] Avoid AiCPU fallback for boolean token sorting
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #16865.

The GDN metadata builder stably partitions speculative and non-speculative tokens by sorting a boolean mask. The existing helper casts that mask to `int32`, which makes integer `argsort` fall back to AiCPU on the tested Ascend stack.

Cast **only boolean masks** to `float32` instead. Both values (0 and 1) are exactly representable, `stable=True` preserves token order within each group, and the returned indices remain `int64`. Non-boolean inputs are unchanged, including large integers that would lose precision if cast to float32.

This is a local dispatch optimization, not a global argsort replacement or a change to model activation precision. No new CANN operator, host transfer, configuration, hardware-specific branch, or scheduler behavior is introduced.

The nearby metadata-sharing optimization in #16246 is complementary: it reduces repeated metadata work, whereas this change addresses the sort's execution backend.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API/configuration changes. The affected boolean GDN partition uses AiCore sorting instead of the integer-sort AiCPU fallback on the tested stack. Other integer sorting calls are outside this PR's scope.

### How was this patch tested?

**Environment:** A2 910B3, TP2 for real-model validation, CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4. Final validation uses Ascend base `dd24be2fe924a77754ae472f77b439fe3eac3091` and its verified vLLM commit `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`.

**Regression tests:**

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_attn_builder.py
# 67 passed
pytest -q tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_gdn_stable_argsort.py
# 40 passed on one NPU
bash format.sh ci
# All hooks passed; the commit also passed a separate gitleaks scan.
```

- The 12 new boolean dispatch UT cases fail against the old implementation and pass with this change. They verify dispatch dtype as well as stable ordering, since output-only tests would not catch an AiCPU performance regression.
- NPU tests cover empty/singleton, constant, alternating and random masks, including non-contiguous inputs.
- An additional standalone comparison verified exact old/new index equality in 90 cases, up to 65536 elements.

**Real weights and controlled trajectory:**

- Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8, TP2, MTP=3: 25 baseline FULL_DECODE_ONLY requests and 75 patched requests (50 FULL_DECODE_ONLY + 25 eager) completed. The original ArgSort fallback warning was observed in the baseline and absent from uninstrumented patched service logs.
- Free-generation runs were not bitwise reproducible even when repeating the old implementation. Therefore those runs are service smoke/stability evidence, not an exact numerical comparison.
- For a separate controlled test, used synchronous eager scheduling, disabled prefix caching, fixed each request's output to a repeated token via a singleton allow-list, and recorded/replayed MTP draft proposals at the runner boundary. The real target and MTP forwards still execute. This is diagnostic instrumentation, **not** upstream Trace Replay (which currently rejects speculative decoding).
- Four different prompt lengths, 64 output tokens each; old/new implementations each run twice after warmup. On both TP ranks, all comparisons matched exactly: scheduler records, target forward input/position hashes, GDN partition masks/indices, returned tokens, and raw logprob dictionaries (top-5 plus selected token). Each run had 59 scheduler steps, 58 target forwards and 27 affected partition calls per rank. Every affected call also shadow-compared old/new indices directly.
- Diagnostic synchronization/shadow-sort overhead is excluded from performance measurements. No diagnostic hooks are included in this PR.

**Performance:**

For 8192 elements, a standalone 10-call kernel profile changed from `aclnnSort_SortAiCpu_Sort` to `aclnnSort_SortAiCore_Sort`; median sort-kernel duration was **579.382 µs → 11.740 µs**. A separate cast+sort microbenchmark measured **591.89 µs → 58.18 µs** (median across five synchronized 100-call rounds). These are operator-level results, **not** claims of equivalent model throughput gains. No significant end-to-end speedup is claimed from the small service workload.

**Known baseline test failures / limits:**

The broader five-file GDN UT run reports 76 passed / 2 failed with this patch, versus 63 passed / the same 2 failed on unmodified `dd24be2fe`:

- `test_connector_observes_updated_gdn_state_for_each_compiled_call`
- `test_mixed_non_spec_reuses_rearranged_qkv`

Both CPU-mock tests enter the available fused-GDN path and pass CPU tensors to NPU Triton l2norm (`Pointer argument ... cannot be accessed from Triton`). They do not originate from this change; no unrelated fixes are bundled here. Full repository tests, A3/A5 validation and long-duration soak testing are not claimed.

title: [Feature][KV Cache] Support non-contiguous KV cache in hybrid models like Qwen3.5 and GQA models
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds non-contiguous KV cache support for hybrid Attention/Mamba models on Ascend, including Qwen3.5 and GQA-based models.

The current Ascend implementation requires Attention and Mamba cache pages to use the same page size and materializes contiguous cache views. This wastes memory and prevents hybrid models from using independent logical page layouts.

This PR:

- Supports independent Attention and Mamba KV cache page sizes.
- Creates stride-based cache views for hybrid layouts instead of materializing padded cache regions.
- Preserves existing legacy paths for pure Mamba/SSM models, separate K/V allocations, KV-transfer layouts, shared-backing layouts, and legacy MLA paths.
- Adds optimized `gather_ssm_states` and `scatter_ssm_states_` Triton kernels for non-contiguous Mamba state access.
- Documents and validates the supported state layout contract:
  - Only the first state stride may contain physical page padding.
  - Inner state dimensions must remain contiguous.
  - State indices select physical rows and may be unsorted or non-contiguous.
  - `has_initial_state=False` produces a zero initial state without reading the cache.

Generic advanced indexing is inefficient and unsafe for padded non-contiguous state storage when used with the fused recurrent GDN path.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new user-facing CLI option is introduced.

The change is internal to Ascend KV cache allocation, layout construction, and hybrid GDN state access.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

- State gather/scatter correctness tests: 18 cases passed.
- MRV2 cache layout tests: 49 cases passed.
- Covered dense and padded layouts, block boundaries, multi-block tails, `int32`/`int64` indices, real GDN state shapes, unselected rows, padding preservation, empty-cache validation, and non-contiguous Attention K/V views.

#### End-to-end model tests

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8:
  - V1 engine.
  - ModelRunner V2.
  - FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode.
  - Short, long-context, repeated, and concurrent requests.
- Qwen2.5-7B GQA:
  - 28 attention heads and 4 KV heads.
  - Runtime logs confirmed non-contiguous K/V views.
  - Short, long-context, repeated, and 32-way concurrent requests passed.
- All request matrix tests completed successfully with zero failed requests.

#### Performance before and after this PR

The pre-PR baseline used vLLM-Ascend commit `af277b2681443089e4d29684b1101707e2eb6426` with Custom GDN operators.

The post-PR configuration used vLLM-Ascend commit `fc4f6ffd97aafd7ad897c387031a46da05ce1d91` with FLA PR #559 operators and non-contiguous KV cache.

Both configurations used:

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8.
- TP=2 and EP.
- MTP=3.
- FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode.
- `fused_mc2=0`.
- `gpu_memory_utilization=0.90`.
- GSM8K full dataset: 1319 requests.
- Concurrency: 64.
- Maximum output length: 512 tokens.

Two opposite-order runs were completed:

| Run | Configuration | TTFT | TPOT | Output throughput | Total throughput | Duration |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Pre-PR Custom | 627.1 ms | 35.8 ms | 1715.13 tok/s | 1954.16 tok/s | 393.008 s |
| 2 | Post-PR FLA | 612.3 ms | 36.0 ms | 1702.93 tok/s | 1940.23 tok/s | 395.881 s |

#### State I/O ablation

Under the same FLA, model, graph mode, and non-contiguous layout:
| Run | Configuration | TTFT | TPOT | Output throughput | Total throughput | Duration |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Old advanced-indexing path | 1491.2 ms | 87.8ms | 692.26 tok/s | 788.72 tok/s | 973.891 s |
| 2 | New gather/scatter path| 612.3 ms | 36.0 ms | 1702.93 tok/s | 1940.23 tok/s | 395.881 s |

The old advanced-indexing path caused both severe performance degradation and abnormal early termination under the non-contiguous layout.

#### Environment

- vLLM: `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`
- CANN: 9.2.0
- Ascend 910
- FLA
- TP=2, EP enabled
- `fused_mc2=0`
- FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode
- `gpu_memory_utilization=0.90`

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [CI] Add non-Flash GLM5.x reduced-checkpoint builder and gates (11-layer logits + performance)
body:
Draft PR adding CI gates for the **non-Flash GLM-5.x** reduced checkpoint (11 main
layers plus one retained MTP layer). Three commits:

- `36e93d504` GLM reduced-model nightly gates and prefix parity probes
- `72a3fb0a3` truncated-logits gate: fixed 200 GSM8K samples, all 20,693
  prediction positions, A1 argmax agreement >= 90%
- `313b11baa` 11-layer offline performance gate (this change)

## What is in this PR

- The profile-based reduced-checkpoint builder/preparer under `tools/glm_reduced`
  (`profiles.py`, `reducer.py`, `prepare.py`, `safetensors_io.py`).
- The fixed-position truncated-logits gate (11-layer GLM-5.2 W4A8, 20,693
  positions, A1 argmax agreement >= 90%).
- The offline 11-layer performance gate (this change).

The builder is the provisioning prerequisite for both gates; the three are kept
in one PR on purpose rather than split.

## Scope: non-Flash GLM5.x only

- Both gates target non-Flash GLM5.x DSA checkpoints. The currently registered
  model is `Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w4a8` reduced to 11 main layers plus one retained
  MTP layer (MTP disabled in the gate).
- Flash and hybrid/linear-attention models are rejected before any measurement:
  both gates run the shared `validate_model`, which raises
  "Flash models are excluded from this gate" when the model id or the config
  mentions flash, and which requires `model_type == glm_moe_dsa` with every
  `layer_types` entry equal to `deepseek_sparse_attention`.
- The reduction tooling under `tools/glm_reduced` is profile-based and can
  describe other families, but neither gate applies a GLM5.x baseline to another
  family. Other non-Flash GLM5.x models need their own registered baseline, and
  this PR claims nothing about Flash models.

## Performance gate

- Offline single-round runner (no OpenAI server), mirroring the logits gate.
- Compares a fresh run against a pinned, host-scoped baseline; model, hardware
  tag, runner architecture, engine settings, workload shapes and iteration
  counts must match exactly or it fails closed.
- Thresholds: output throughput >= 90% of baseline; TTFT/TPOT/whole-workload
  latency <= 120%. Derived from a three-start A/A calibration, not chosen to let
  a candidate pass.
- CI never writes or bootstraps a baseline; evidence directories are never
  overwritten.

## Calibration

Three independent starts on the lab x86_64 A3 host, one warmup plus three
measured iterations each. Cross-start relative MAD: 4.22% throughput, 10.19%
TTFT, 4.42% TPOT, 4.40% whole-workload latency. The earlier single-launch
baseline was an optimistic outlier (8.7%-13.3% above the three-start median), so
the baseline is now the median of three starts.

## Boundaries

- The baseline is scoped to `linux-x86_64-a3-800i-8-167`; there is no aarch64
  calibration yet, so the nightly registration is left commented out in
  `nightly_config.yaml`. Enabling it on aarch64 would fail closed by design.
- `enforce_eager=True` and MTP disabled: this is a regression baseline, not a
  deployment peak, and it does not extrapolate to the full 78-layer model.
- The 3% relative-MAD stability cap used by the earlier Reduced8 gate is not met
  on this shared host, so the thresholds carry roughly twice the worst observed
  one-sided ratio (0.9578 low-side throughput, 1.1019 high-side latency).
- A confirmation round with the calibrated baseline was not completed: the
  attempt hit resource contention on the shared host. The runner pipeline itself
  was exercised end-to-end once.

## Testing

- 15 CPU gate tests (`tests/ut/tools/glm_reduced/test_perf_gate.py`); ruff check
  and ruff format clean.
- Logits gate: 20 CPU tests, single-round NPU agreement 20,693/20,693, exit 0.
- No GitHub nightly has been run.

body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
In the scenario where GLM5.2 enables dspark, the seq_lens in attention_v1 requires a device-to-host synchronization (on the NPU, seq_lens has num_rejects subtracted, whereas on the CPU it does not), causing a large number of bubbles between the main model and the draft model. Empirical tests show that using seq_lens without num_rejects has almost no impact on the model acceptance rate, but greatly improves performance.

title: [Feat][MRV2] Adapt Qwen3.8 Flash Next to ModelRunnerV2 (graph  + MTP + async scheduling)
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
This PR is based on #16981 for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.

It adapts the qwen4_exp hybrid model to the V2 model runner on Ascend, enabling V2 serving with FULL aclgraph decode mode, MTP speculative decoding and async scheduling. Three commits, one per functional layer:

**1. Six-region KV cache consumption in the V2 runner** (`attn_utils.py`)

The qwen4_exp hybrid model uses a six-region KV cache layout: one shared slot backing carries six physical slabs (GDN states, QSA main K/V, raw/compressed QSA states, PLE n-gram states). The V2 runner previously had no consumption path for this layout, so the V1 contract (shared backing allocation + per-role view rebuild in the reshape step) is mirrored into the V2 allocation/reshape entry points. Configurations that cannot take the shared backing (KV transfer connectors outside the allowlist, DSV4) still fall back to vLLM's own allocator.

**2. Hybrid FULL aclgraph replay** (`aclgraph_utils.py`, `qwen4_exp/model_state.py`, `qwen4_exp/qsa.py`)

FULL aclgraph replay previously assumed a single executable attention backend and a model state that stores attn_metadata. Both assumptions break for qwen4_exp:

- Hybrid models own more than one executable backend (main attention, QSA side cache; GDN groups are metadata-only), so `_get_graph_update_backends` now collects all distinct backends with an executable attention impl and refreshes every one of them before replay.
- `AscendQwen4ExpModelState` is added via multiple inheritance (`Qwen4ExpModelState` + `AscendMambaHybridModelState`): MRO keeps the upstream PLE input preparation while `prepare_attn` resolves to the Ascend implementation that builds and stores attention metadata for replay.
- QSA kernels are custom Triton ops reading persistent buffers rewritten per step, so `update_graph_params` is a documented no-op for QSA, mirroring the V1 gate for sparse/compressed models and the MiniMax-M3 indexer precedent.

**3. MTP draft support in the autoregressive speculator** (`speculator.py`)

The qwen4_exp MTP draft reuses the target model's QSA backend, which derives from vllm's `FlashAttentionBackend` (not `AscendAttentionBackend`) and therefore missed the architecture classification in `set_attn`. QSA is now classified into its own branch whose draft KV semantics follow the GQA behavior group (standard block-table slot mappings), and the host-side FIA metadata patch is skipped for QSA since its metadata aliases the shared input buffers and the patched fields do not exist on `QSAForwardMetadata`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No.

### How was this patch tested?
Tested on 8 × Ascend 910C (A3) with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8 (TP8/EP8): V2 serving starts up normally in graph mode with MTP enabled, and single-curl requests return correct responses in all four configurations (V2 eager, V2 + graph, V2 + MTP, V2 + graph + MTP).

Multimodal (image) input is also verified on V2: the same base64-image chat request returns a correct answer (dominant color + shape recognition) with identical prompt token counts as the V1 baseline, confirming the vision encoder path works under the V2 runner.

Depends on #16981

title: [Performance][MoE] Use bf16 router GEMM with fp32 accumulation for bf16-origin weights
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`AscendGateLinear` (PR #9617) forces fp32 weights and fp32 computation for the MoE router gate, because the previous `bf16×bf16→bf16` path (bf16 accumulation, no fp32 output) caused expert-selection errors in agent workloads on NPU.

However, the fp32 path (`aclnnMatmulV2`) is ~6x slower than necessary for bf16-origin weights — the common case for models like Kimi K3, whose gate weights are stored as bf16 in safetensors.

This PR makes the bf16 GEMM the default for bf16 router weights, rebuilt on the same tier architecture as upstream vllm `GateLinear`:

```python
# Tier 4: bf16 weight + bf16 input + fp32 out_dtype + no bias
torch.mm(x, self.weight.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)
```

which dispatches to `aclnnMm MatMulV3` — bf16 multiplication with **fp32 accumulation**. For bf16-origin operands this is numerically equivalent to the fp32 path (each `bf16×bf16` product fits exactly in the fp32 accumulator; the only difference is K-dim summation order, ~1e-5).

Two changes make this work end-to-end:

1. **`AscendGateLinear` follows upstream tier-4/tier-5 semantics.** Gate weights follow the model dtype (no fp32 upcast), so a bf16-origin checkpoint loads into bf16 params — `self.weight.dtype` is the checkpoint dtype. The fast-path eligibility is checked at forward time, mirroring upstream's cuBLAS `out_dtype` epilogue tier. `force_fp32_compute` is honored exactly like upstream: with no NPU specialized kernel, it stores the weight in fp32 so the fallback tier computes in fp32.

2. **`AscendMoERunner` stops forcing fp32 precast on ctor gates.** The forced `precast_fp32_weight` materialized `weight_fp32` for every internal-router gate, which made `_compute_router_logits` always bypass the gate's own forward — so a gate-side fast path could never actually run for internal-router models (GLM5Next, MiniMax-M3, upstream DeepSeek-V2 family). fp32 is now a model-level opt-in: DSV4 sets `precast_fp32_weight` itself and keeps the direct `F.linear(hidden_states_fp32, gate.weight_fp32)` path; everyone else routes through `gate(hidden_states)`.

### Key design decisions

- **Weights follow the model dtype** (upstream semantics): no fp32 param upcast, no `weight_loader` dtype recording, no bf16 weight cache — `self.weight.dtype` *is* the checkpoint dtype. In-place RL weight updates are reflected naturally.
- **Eligibility checked at forward time** (mirrors upstream tier 4): bf16 weight + bf16 input + fp32 `out_dtype` + no bias (`torch.mm` has no bias term). Any miss falls to tier 5.
- **Tier-5 fallback matches upstream**: cast `x` to the weight dtype, compute via `ReplicatedLinear.forward`, cast the output to `out_dtype`.
- **`out_dtype=None` defaults to fp32 on NPU** (upstream leaves None and computes natively): this keeps the historical Ascend fp32-logits contract for the downstream topk kernels, lets bf16-weight models with the `out_dtype=None` wiring (upstream DeepSeek-V2 family / GLM5Next) take tier 4 directly, and resolves the fp32-weight + bf16-input dtype-mismatch edge.
- **Forced fp32 stays opt-in**: `params_dtype=torch.float32` (e.g. MiniMax-M3) or `force_fp32_compute` → fp32 weights → tier-5 fp32 compute; DSV4 keeps its `precast_fp32_weight` path routed by the MoE runner; the 310P runner still forces precast (a forward-time Cast cannot be captured by ACLGraph on 310P).
- **ACLGraph-safe by construction**: no path casts a weight per forward — the #16189 failure mode (`gate.weight.to(torch.float32)` emitting an aclop Cast inside the captured region) is structurally unreachable. Tier 4 contains zero casts at all.

## Background: why the old path was slow

PR #9617 forced fp32 because the pre-existing path was `bf16×bf16→bf16` (bf16 accumulation). The fast path uses `bf16×bf16→fp32` (fp32 accumulation via `out_dtype=torch.float32`), which avoids the precision issue while being ~6x faster:

| Path | Multiply | Accumulate | Output | NPU kernel | Speed |
|------|----------|------------|--------|------------|-------|
| Pre-#9617 (bf16 F.linear) | bf16 | bf16 | bf16 | aclnnMatmulV2 | baseline (broken) |
| #9617 (fp32 F.linear) | fp32 | fp32 | fp32 | aclnnMatmulV2 | 84.8µs |
| **This PR (bf16 mm + fp32 out)** | **bf16** | **fp32** | **fp32** | **aclnnMm MatMulV3** | **13.7µs (6.2x)** |

## Path routing per model

| Model | Gate wiring | Path after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Kimi K3 | model-side call, bf16 weights, `out_dtype=fp32` | tier 4 (bf16 mm) |
| DeepSeek-V2 family / GLM5Next | runner internal router, bf16 weights, `out_dtype=None` | tier 4 via `gate()` (fp32 default) |
| MiniMax-M3 | explicit `params_dtype=torch.float32` | tier 5 (fp32, model intent preserved) |
| DeepSeek-V4 | `precast_fp32_weight` (own) | runner `F.linear(weight_fp32)` — unchanged |
| 310P internal-router | 310P runner forced precast | unchanged |

## Precision verification

**Methodology**: the fp32 path (`F.linear` → aclnnMatmulV2) and the bf16 path (`torch.mm(out_dtype=fp32)` → aclnnMm MatMulV3) both run **on NPU** with the production ops; the float64 reference runs **on CPU**. Shape: N=896, K=7168 (Kimi K3 router).

### M-sweep vs the float64 reference (16 shapes, M = 1 to 896)

Fixed bf16-origin weight [896, 7168]; 16 M values uniformly spaced over [1, 896]; relative-error denominator = |y_fp64| clamped at 1e-06 (near-zero logits excluded). In both tables, **ratio = bf16 error / fp32 error** (each measured against the same float64 reference); ratio < 1 means the bf16 path is closer to the reference. Top-16 expert selection (N=896, k=16, per-row expert-set match) is measured on the same outputs and reported alongside the absolute-error table.

Findings:

- The bf16 path is closer to the float64 reference on **16/16 shapes** in both metrics: absolute-error ratio stable at **0.52–0.57** (avg 0.55), relative-error ratio at **0.56–0.68** (avg ~0.60).
- mean_abs is essentially flat across M (fp32: 4.34–4.41e-05, bf16: 2.25–2.46e-05) — the error is set by the K=7168 fp32-accumulation structure, not by M; max_abs grows slowly with M purely by extreme-value statistics.
- mean_rel sits at the ~1e-06 scale; max_rel is dominated by near-zero logits and saturates.
- **Top-16 expert selection is 100% consistent at every shape in this sweep**: bf16 vs fp32 matches on **7176/7176** rows across all 16 shapes, and both paths vs the float64 reference are likewise 100% (7176/7176 each).

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. Router GEMM outputs are unchanged for every model: bf16-origin weights get the numerically-equivalent `bf16×bf16→fp32` path, and models that require fp32 routing keep fp32 compute via their existing opt-in (`params_dtype` / `precast_fp32_weight`).

## How was this patch tested

- Precision test on NPU (Ascend910): compared fp32 path, bf16 path, and float64 CPU reference across M=3/24/961 with bf16-origin weights (a true-fp32-weight control, forced through the bf16 math, degrades to 66.7% top-16 consistency — confirming why the weight-dtype condition matters)

- Layout micro-benchmark (nz_bench.py): ND / FRACTAL_NZ / pre-transposed-NZ bf16 weights produce bit-identical outputs; ND + `.t()` selected (pre-transposed NZ ~40% slower)
- Unit tests (new): tier-4 fast path (mocked `torch.mm`, asserts `out_dtype=fp32` and the weight view); params follow the model dtype unless `force_fp32_compute`; tier-5 fallback casts the output to `out_dtype`; `out_dtype=None` defaults to fp32 (tier 4 fires directly, fp32-weight + bf16-input edge resolved)

title: [Feature][Sparse Attention]custom fused_infer_attention_score (Blasst) op and i…
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds **BlasstAttentionScore (BlasST)**, a custom AscendC attention operator, and integrates it into the v1 attention backend as an opt-in path alongside the torch_npu FIA baseline.

The built-in FIA kernel is a black box and cannot be extended with block-sparse skipping. BlasST implements the full flash-attention pipeline itself (QK/PV GEMM mainloops + online-softmax epilogue), which enables two optimizations:

- **Block-sparse skipping** on both prefill and decode paths: KV blocks whose contribution to the online-softmax denominator falls below the `sparse_lambda` threshold are skipped entirely (QK GEMM, softmax and PV GEMM for the block).
- **FlashDecode split-KV scheduling** for small decode batches over long KV: the KV dimension is split across idle cores and merged via cross-core LSE rescale.

vLLM integration is opt-in via `blasst_config`: eligible batches route to the custom op, everything else stays on the FIA baseline (fallback is automatic). Both eager and ACL-Graph capture (decode buckets) are supported.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. New `additional_config` key `blasst_config` (`enabled: bool = False`, `sparse_lambda: float = -99.0`). Default-off; enabling it on a build without the registered op (non-A3 SoC) raises `RuntimeError` at startup. No behavior change when disabled.

### How was this patch tested?
| Metric | baseline (FIA) | λ=-5 | λ=-3 | λ=-2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LongBench-v2 accuracy (eager) | 41.43% | 40.48% | 42.86% | 40.95% |
| LongBench-v2 accuracy (graph) | — | 41.43% | 41.90% | 38.10% |
| TPOT | 94.35 ms | 91.7 (−2.8%) | 88.51 (−6.2%) | 87.97 (−6.8%) |
| Output throughput | 329.6 tok/s | 345.2 (+4.7%) | 351.0 (+6.5%) | 353.2 (+7.2%) |

No accuracy loss at the production setting λ=-3 (delta within noise).

title: [Feature][MRV2] Adapt Ascend attention to upstream PCP decode sharding
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Requires vllm-project/vllm#52162 plus the companion [pisceskkk/vllm#10](https://github.com/pisceskkk/vllm/pull/10).** The tested upstream is `d13f6525041b103fd566335945b0afefa321a6b0`, based on #52162 head `42fc76a63aa382ff0ebe3b0adad346b5d38b91c0`. The companion fixes structured KV-cache initialization and adds the A/B switch; #52162 alone is insufficient for this Ascend setup.

MRv2 assigns PCP-only decode requests to individual PCP ranks. Ascend must distribute those owners' KV updates before local attention, including ranks with no owned requests.

- Reuse upstream request assignment, layout indices, write masks and output gathering.
- Synchronize dense MLA KV and SFA main/indexer KV, preserve empty-rank collective participation, and restore the global output layout.
- Align the paired upstream's UVA, model/index-group and graph-manager constructors, SFA CPU-length metadata and split cache-binding APIs. Avoid eagerly importing an optional model architecture missing from the paired revision.
- Keep native preprocessing where fused paths bypass synchronization, with explicit gates for unsupported combinations.
- Retain Ascend sequence-parallel MoE for the TP-only DSA-CP comparison: DP=1, TP>1, PCP=1, EP enabled and `allgather_reducescatter`. The platform patch preserves the upstream predicate for other layouts. DSA-CP still requires an indexer and automatically enables FlashComm; disabling both DSA-CP and FlashComm still disables SP MoE. This replaces the benchmark's temporary property override.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The paired upstream enables decode sharding by default for PCP>1 and DCP=1. Use `--enable-pcp-decode-sharding` / `--no-enable-pcp-decode-sharding` or Python `enable_pcp_decode_sharding=False` to compare sharded and replicated decode without changing topology.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <DeepSeek-model-path> \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --async-scheduling --enforce-eager \
  --additional-config '{"enable_mlapo":false}' \
  --enable-pcp-decode-sharding
```

For A/B, change only the last flag. Native preprocessing (`enable_mlapo=false`) must be held identical in both arms. The full KV cache remains replicated.

Initial sharding support is eager, non-hybrid DeepSeek V2/V3/V3.2 with RoPE and MLA/SFA. Dense MLA requires unquantized KV. Graph execution, speculative decoding, KVPP and PCP O-proj weight sharding are rejected when sharding is active. MRv1, PCP=1 and DCP>1 retain their existing decode policy.

A TP16 DSA-CP baseline instead uses TP16/PCP1, EP and `additional_config={"enable_mlapo":false,"enable_dsa_cp":true}`. DSA-CP reuses the TP group and does not add ranks.

### How was this patch tested?

**CPU regression on the updated Ascend patch:**

Current Ascend head: `8b50fc3de5942ed921daa30a3638c3dbb86e27e1`.

- `python -m pytest -q tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py`: **115 passed**, including single-DP DSA-CP, disabling FlashComm again, and unsupported EP/TP/PCP/backend layouts.
- PCP manager, MRv2 runner, MLA, SFA, SFA PCP, indexer, UVA, DeepSeek patch and KV-binding suites: **499 passed, 49 skipped**. These use the repository CPU-mock harness; skipped release-only and fused-preprocessing cases are not device validation.
- Paired upstream CLI/configuration selection: **10 passed** previously, covering default/on/off, topology eligibility, world size and config hashing.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. No complete upstream CI or full hook-suite pass is claimed.

**Standard-entrypoint full-weight startup check on the current patch:** full DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8, TP16/PCP1/DP1, EP and asynchronous scheduling, eager, `enable_dsa_cp=true` and `enable_mlapo=false`. Started `python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server` without the temporary property/detokenizer wrapper. Logs confirmed DSA-CP and FlashComm remained enabled; model loading used 46.14 GiB/rank and the KV planner exposed 93,056 tokens. Two concurrent completion requests both returned HTTP 200 and exactly 32 output tokens. This proves startup and basic generation on this configuration, not full-model accuracy or the requested three-way performance comparison.

**Full DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8 generation and pure-decode comparisons:** Ascend `851a3ded7`, upstream `d13f652504`, 16 logical Ascend A3 NPUs, TP8/PCP2/DCP1, EP and async enabled, eager, native preprocessing in both arms. Input 2049 / output 256 tokens; 2048-token prefix prewarmed, no KV preemptions.

- Shared prefix, concurrency 1/2/4/8/16/32/64, three rounds per point and switch state: **42 rounds completed; all 381 paired outputs matched token-for-token**.
- Distinct prefixes, concurrency 2/4/8/16/30, three rounds per point and state: **30 rounds completed; all 180 paired outputs matched token-for-token**. Each request had a distinct first cache block. Steady decode throughput changed by -2.9% to +0.2%; no clear TP8/PCP2 pure-decode benefit was established.
- This is deterministic generation equivalence for these workloads, not a full model accuracy evaluation.

**Five-layer dummy mixed-prefill/decode experiment:** input 128K, output 1K, 90% prefix hits, server `max_num_seqs=32`, token budget 32K, AIS Bench submits 100 requests concurrently. Each arm completed 100/100 with no KV preemption. TP1/PCP16 OFF/ON measured 849.37/944.82 output tokens/s and 30.4/26.8 ms mean TPOT. TP16+DSA-CP measured 872.65 tokens/s and 28.9 ms with the equivalent single-DP compatibility adapter. These are single-pass synthetic reduced-layer measurements, not full-model performance. All mixed arms used the slow incremental detokenizer to work around long-prompt frontend blocking; that workaround is not included in this PR, and upstream #51281/#57330 address that area.

The requested full-weight TP1/PCP16 three-way comparison is not complete: checkpoint tensors alone require at least 64.76 GiB per rank at EP16 (25.96 GiB replicated plus 620.77/16 GiB routed experts), exceeding the current 64 GiB devices before KV/activation overhead. Do not treat the dummy results as full-weight PCP16 validation.

Earlier DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat TP1/PCP2 tests covered unequal lengths, empty owners and prefix replay, with 14 outputs / 669 tokens matching replicated decode using native preprocessing. A reduced two-layer random V3.2 SFA smoke also completed 14 requests / 672 tokens with finite logprobs. Those are separate from the full-weight tests above.

Environment: isolated ARM64 Ascend container, Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10.0+cpu and torch_npu 2.10.0.post4; image-provided compiled artifacts. `VLLM_VERSION=0.29.1rc1` selects the development API path because the image version file labels the checked-out code as release 0.29.0. Source SHAs identify the actual code.

Developed with OpenAI Codex assistance at the human submitter's request. This remains a draft pending human review of the upstream dependencies and validation boundaries.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Feature][EC Connector] Add Mooncake EC transfer support for ModelRunner V1
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
Add an Ascend adapter for the upstream `ECMooncakeConnector` so V1 workers can transfer multimodal encoder outputs between encoder and prefill/decode instances.
The adapter reuses the upstream scheduler, reservation state machine, and worker lifecycle, with NPU-specific memory and synchronization handling.

Related to the EPD roadmap in issue #6026 which tracks Mooncake-based cross-node encoder-cache sharing among other work. This PR adapts the `ECMooncakeConnector` TransferEngine data plane for Ascend.

- Register the Ascend implementation under the existing `ECMooncakeConnector`
  name through the Ascend plugin entry point.
- Reuse `MooncakeTransfer` with the process-local Ascend TransferEngine. Allocate
  registered staging and receive buffers with 2 MiB alignment, and reject direct
  registration of arbitrary source tensor views when staging is unavailable.
- Use NPU events to track source readiness and delay receive-buffer reuse until
  device work completes.
- Start EC worker services after model loading and shut them down with the worker.
- Return EC completion information from V1 encoder-only execution and steps that
  skip model forward. Previously, these return paths could omit the information
  the scheduler needs to advance asynchronous transfers.

The change also allocates the MoE load counter directly on NPU, removing the intermediate CPU allocation and device copy. V2 runner support is outside this PR.

The V1 runner changes belong in Ascend's existing `execute_model()` override:
that method owns the encoder-only and no-forward return paths where EC output must be collected. Patching the upstream runner would not update these overridden paths; replacing the Ascend method through a runtime patch would add indirection to code already maintained here. Both no-forward exits share one helper, which preserves KV output and invokes the existing EC lifecycle when metadata is present. The connector continues to own transfer scheduling and memory management. Worker shutdown follows the upstream KV-then-EC order.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Yes. On Ascend, `ec_connector="ECMooncakeConnector"` selects the NPU adapter. The adapter defaults to the `ascend` transport protocol and maps the default CUDA buffer setting to NPU. Explicit non-Ascend transport protocols are rejected.

Transfers use the configured `ec_buffer_size`. If the producer cannot stage a batch in its registered pool, it reports a transfer failure instead of falling back to registering the original tensor addresses.

### How was this patch tested?
Added `tests/ut/distributed/ec_transfer/test_mooncake_adapter.py` and ran it in the existing Ascend container after synchronizing the changes to the editable runtime
checkout:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/ec_transfer/test_mooncake_adapter.py
```

Result: **12 passed**. Tests cover connector registration, protocol validation, shared-engine reuse, write failures, failed-unregistration ownership and cleanup, direct-source rejection, Producer/Consumer worker initialization and dispatcher shutdown, and V1 no-forward EC output handling. TransferEngine calls are mocked.

The following checks passed locally:

```bash
bash format.sh
bash format.sh ci
git diff --check
```

The format checks used ARM64 Gitleaks and ShellCheck, a writable Ruff cache, and initialized pre-commit environments with compatible Go and Node versions. Python syntax checks also passed. These are local checks, not hosted CI results.

#### Real-NPU TP2 validation

The TP2 consumer regression passed on three Ascend 910B1 NPUs, using a real Mooncake sender and two HCCL consumer ranks. Each rank handled six reservation callbacks on non-main control threads with the correct receive-pool device bound, including `npu:1` on rank 1. Tensor equality, cancellation, buffer reuse, pool reclamation, and cleanup checks passed.

An EPD correctness test compared a TP2 monolithic baseline with one encoder plus a TP2 consumer on the same PD devices: Qwen3.5-9B, MRV1, BF16, eager, CANN 9.1.0, and torch/torch_npu 2.10.0. Eight serial requests contained one or three 224×224 images (16 images total), with greedy decoding and 32 output tokens each. All requests completed without EC transfer errors.

- **Transfer correctness:** all 16 source embeddings matched both TP ranks'
  received tensors bit-for-bit in two diagnostic replays, including one with
  reads deferred until after sending and consumer prefill. Staging tensors also
  matched in the full-capture replay; no transfer corruption was observed.
- **Baseline comparison:** the monolithic baseline batches two images together
  on one vision rank, while EPD encodes images individually. With the baseline
  changed only to encode images individually, all 16 image embeddings, merged
  inputs on both ranks, all 80 captured logits tensors (five steps per request
  per rank), and **8/8 complete output token sequences matched bit-for-bit**.

The original batched-baseline comparison matched 6/8 outputs; both diagnostic replays matched 7/8. The reproducible mismatch was traced to batch-dependent visual numerical differences affecting greedy token selection, independently of Mooncake. 

#### End-to-end benchmarks

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (W8A8_DYNAMIC, BF16 activations), 4 × Ascend 910B (64 GiB), CANN 9.1.0, torch/torch_npu 2.10.0, vLLM `a97dacb7106e`. Each setup uses four NPUs: DP4EP4 or 1 Encoder + 3 PD for both EPD connectors.
Client concurrency is 128; output is fixed at 64 tokens. Eager execution, no MTP, prefix caching, or profiling. DP4 and Encoder use OMP8; PD uses OMP1.

Identical inputs are used across setups within each workload. The large-image workloads keep 526 non-visual input tokens; six images double the visual tokens. Latency columns below are means. Parentheses show changes relative to Example:
higher throughput and lower latency are better.

body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix the W4A4 MXFP4 MoE activation lifetime regression introduced by the MoE MLP refactor. When the dispatcher does not provide a dynamic scale, local dynamic MXFP quantization produces a separate FP4 activation tensor. body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #17272 for `releases/v0.26.0rc`.

The layerwise proxy currently retries every HTTP and transport failure. A P notification may already have admitted the request before a response error or post-send failure, so replaying it can create duplicate admissions and KV transfer rounds.

Retry only failures that occur before delivery: `ConnectError`, `ConnectTimeout`, and `PoolTimeout`. Propagate HTTP errors and ambiguous post-send transport failures without replaying the request.

Yes. Side-effectful prefill notifications are no longer re-POSTed after HTTP, read, or write failures.

title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Suppress PD send after pool load failure
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

When a layerwise MemCache load loses its GVA/lease, AscendStore reports the invalid block to the scheduler. The SFA producer can still have queued layer send tasks for the same request and may publish `READ_READY_BATCH`, including a success completion marker, for KV that was never loaded.

This change records failed request IDs in a process-local, TTL-bounded registry and filters those requests before the SFA producer builds PD notifications. The marker remains visible across all queued layer tasks.

This complements #16876: that PR fences writes back to the shared pool, while this PR prevents forwarding the failed local prefix to the decode side.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. A request whose layerwise MemCache load fails is no longer advertised as a successful PD transfer.

title: [BugFix][KV Pool] Preserve per-layer load plan ownership
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Layerwise load tasks in the same cache group do not necessarily describe the same transfer. Independent layers can retain a local prefix and load `[local_hit, end)`, while reused layers load `[0, end)`. The current implementation builds one descriptor from the first task in a group and assigns it to every layer, which can omit required blocks.

`LayerBatchBuilder` also reuses internal NumPy buffers. A second descriptor build can overwrite arrays retained by an already queued task unless each task owns a snapshot.

This draft PR:

- builds shared load metadata from each task's own block ranges;
- copies `block_ids_arr` and `block_gvas_arr` before queuing;
- validates the GVA descriptor invariant;
- adds a regression test using two task plans backed by the same reusable arrays.

This overlaps the layerwise transfer refactor in #16377. The intent of opening it as a draft is to make the correctness bug and regression test reviewable so the fix can either merge first or be incorporated into that refactor.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration change. Layerwise loads now use the block range prepared for each layer instead of reusing another layer's plan.

title: [BugFix][Worker] Support non-uniform KV cache page sizes
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

AscendKVBlockZeroer assumed that every KV-cache segment had the same physical page size. Hybrid KV-cache layouts can contain segments with different page sizes, for example 16384 and 4096 elements. The uniform page-size assertion therefore aborts engine initialization before a request can be served.

Track the page size for every cache segment and pass the metadata to the Triton zeroing kernel. The kernel uses the largest segment only to size the launch, then masks chunks beyond each segment boundary. The kernel block size is selected from the common power-of-two divisor of all segments, preserving valid addressing and the existing uniform-page-size behavior.

The change adds CPU metadata regression coverage for uniform and non-uniform page sizes, and keeps the device-memory zeroing check in one-card NPU CI because it executes a Triton kernel.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Hybrid models with non-uniform KV-cache page sizes can initialize and serve without failing with: AssertionError: Non-uniform page sizes: 16384 vs 4096.

### How was this patch tested?

- UT validation completed.

- Successfully reproduced the pre-fix issue with the vllm serve command: AssertionError: Non-uniform page sizes: 16384 vs 4096.

Signed-off-by: bianpeizhi <bianpeizhi@huawei.com>

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds GLM-5.3-Flash Model Runner V2 integration for hybrid cache layout, decode graphs, and MTP. MRV2 must preserve the cache capabilities, shared physical pages, and circular tail addressing contract used by MRV1.

Refs #15665
Refs #16755

- Reuse main's `view_glm5_next_cache()` for kernel-granularity NoPE/indexer views and the packed tail region. Preserve shared MLA/Mamba pages and per-layer bindings.
- Build copy-on-write views in the existing MRV2 cache utility, then reuse upstream block copying. Shared MLA/Mamba pages are copied once; separately packed indexer and tail components retain their own strides.
- Pass the original cache spec and explicit kernel block size to storage-stride-aware SFA/KPool builders. Other MRV2 builders delegate to the original factory. SFA reads logical geometry from the spec rather than maintaining duplicate fields.
- Carry graph capture lifecycle in KPool metadata, including warmup and rebuilt metadata during multi-step drafting, instead of reading `_EXTRA_CTX.capturing` in the backend.
- Obtain speculative-history requirements from `get_kpool_tail_ring_capacity()` and retain power-of-two ring alignment for the no-prefix coordinator's scheduler-block divisibility contract.

title: [Optimize][Triton][Ascend] Optimize _triton_rope_siso using CANN extension slice operations
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR optimizes the `_triton_rope_siso` kernel by moving offset and mask calculations outside the loop and using CANN extension slice operations (`extract_slice` and `insert_slice`) for more efficient memory access. It also adds documentation for the Triton RoPE kernels and introduces a new end-to-end test for the SISO RoPE kernel with cos/sin cache.. This PR reduces global memory traffic, eliminates redundant computations, and adds explicit in-place reuse through five changes:

1. **Split input/output pointers for explicit in-place reuse.**
   The kernel signature is changed from a single `qk_ptr` (used for both read and write) to two separate pointers: `qk_ptr` (input) and `output_ptr` (output). The host function `rope_forward_triton_siso` passes the **same tensor address** to both parameters, enabling in-place operation. Splitting the parameters makes the in-place reuse explicit at the call site and allows the compiler to better reason about read/write aliasings, which helps avoid unnecessary buffer copies and improves kernel execution performance on Ascend.

2. **Hoist loop-invariant offsets/masks out of the token loop.**
   `cos_sin_offsets`, `qk_offsets` and their masks are now computed once before the `for row_idx` loop instead of once per iteration.

3. **Single contiguous load for cos/sin (USE_COS_SIN path).**
   Previously: two non-contiguous loads (`cos_offsets` and `sin_offsets`) from the `cos_sin_cache` row.
   Now: one full-row load + `extension.extract_slice` to separate cos and sin halves. The `else` path (separate cos/sin) also benefits from the hoisted unified offsets.

4. **Single-tile load for qk.**
   Previously: compute `first_half_offsets` -> load left half -> compute `second_half_offsets` -> load right half.
   Now: one `tl.load` of the full `(pad_n_h, pad_rope_dim)` tile, then `extension.extract_slice` to split into halves (NeoX) or even/odd pairs (interleaved).

5. **Single-tile store for qk.**
   Previously: compute and store `new_qk_tile_1`, then compute and store `new_qk_tile_2` - two stores.
   Now: compute both halves, recombine via `extension.insert_slice`, and write with a single `tl.store`.

Net effect per token row:
- Original: **4 loads** (cos, sin, qk_L, qk_R) + **2 stores** = 6 global ops
- Optimized: **2 loads** (cos_sin_row, qk_tile) + **1 store** = 3 global ops
- In-place reuse eliminates one full tensor allocation per call.

Numerical results are identical (same rotation math, same masks).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal performance optimization for _triton_rope_siso.

### How was this patch tested?

- Correctness: `_triton_rope_siso` output matches the reference RoPE implementation for both NeoX and interleaved styles, and for both `cos/sin` and `cos_sin_cache` input paths.
- In-place reuse verified by passing the same tensor as both `qk` and `output`; result identical to out-of-place path.
- A new end-to-end test `test_rotary_embedding_triton_kernel_siso_with_cos_sin_cache` was added in `test_rope.py`.
- **Performance:**

| cases | InputShape (num_tokens, num_heads, head_dim, rotary_dim) | IS_NEOX_STYLE | USE_COS_SIN | runtime before opt (us) | runtime after opt (us) | gains (speedup) |
|-----|------------|---------------|-------------|--------|--------|--------|
| 1 | (1024,32,32,32) | True | 1 | 67.86 | 11.92 | 5.69x |
| 2 | (1024,32,32,32) | True | 0 | 66.14 | 11.56 | 5.72x |
| 3 | (1024,32,64,64) | True | 1 | 42.72 | 13.70 | 3.12x |
| 4 | (1024,32,64,64) | True | 0 | 43.60 | 13.48 | 3.23 |
| 5 | (1024,32,128,128) | True | 1 | 32.72 | 15.78 | 2.07x |
| 6 | (1024,32,128,128) | True | 0 | 33.05 | 16.52 | 2.00x |
| 7 | (1024,32,256,256) | True | 1 | 36.32 | 26.68 | 1.36x |
| 8 | (1024,32,256,256) | True | 0 | 36.84 | 25.60 | 1.44x |
| 9 | (1024,32,64,64) | False(GPT-J) | 0 | 61.60 | 59.22 | 1.04x |
| 10 | (1024,32,128,128) | False(GPT-J) | 1 | 100.48 | 96.12 | 1.05x |

### Notes

- The optimization requires `triton.language.extra.cann.extension`  (`extract_slice` / `insert_slice`), which is available on Ascend Triton.
- Only `_triton_rope_siso` is modified; `_triton_rope` (separate q/k) and `_triton_rope_fp8` are untouched.
- **NeoX vs interleaved style on Ascend**: The current optimization yields significant gains for the **NeoX style** (half-split layout), while the benefit is limited for the **interleaved style** (GPT-J, even/odd pair layout). This is because Ascend NPU primarily uses a **SIMD execution model**, where the NeoX-style contiguous half-split maps naturally to vectorized load/store operations, whereas the interleaved strided access pattern requires gather/scatter-like sequences that are less efficient on SIMD hardware. Therefore, when deploying RoPE operators on Ascend, it is recommended to use the **NeoX-style data layout** whenever possible to maximize kernel performance.

title: [v0.26.0rc][BugFix][KV Transfer] Suppress PD send after pool load failure
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #17291 for `releases/v0.26.0rc`.

When a layerwise MemCache load loses its GVA/lease, queued SFA producer tasks can still advertise `READ_READY_BATCH`, including a success marker, for KV that was never loaded. This change records failed request IDs in a process-local, TTL-bounded registry and filters them before building PD notifications.

This is complementary to the release save-fence backport: save fencing prevents publishing bad KV to the shared pool, while this change prevents forwarding the failed local prefix to D.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. A request whose layerwise MemCache load fails is no longer advertised as a successful PD transfer.

On Ascend 310P, enabling MTP for small models (e.g. Qwen3.5-2B) regresses decode latency because SpecDecoding FULL ACLGraph still pays empty update↔compute handshakes and repeated D2H syncs for rejection/prefill metadata. title: [v0.26.0rc][BugFix][SFA PD] Converge failed transfer lifecycle
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport of #17293 for `releases/v0.26.0rc`, adapted to the release protocol without main-only PP handshake changes.

This makes SFA PD failure handling converge:

- retry only pre-delivery connection failures (`ConnectError`, `ConnectTimeout`, and `PoolTimeout`); do not replay HTTP non-2xx or post-send read/write failures;
- cap outer rendezvous retries and publish a failed consumer terminal with the destination blocks;
- serialize failed terminals through the read thread and defer cleanup until the terminal is reported;
- filter duplicate or late batches before destination lookup/copy using TTL-bounded tombstones;
- clear prior terminal state when an external request ID starts a fresh round.

This PR does not include the proxy backport (#17323), producer load-failure suppression (#17322), main-only PP protocol changes, or a vLLM core scheduler monkey patch.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Failed SFA PD requests terminate instead of waiting indefinitely, and potentially side-effectful notifications are not re-POSTed.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added focused regression coverage for retry classification, failed metadata propagation, receive terminals, deferred cleanup, tombstone filtering, and request rearming.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` pass.
