title: [BugFix][Worker] Select local communication endpoints by bound NPU
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The NPU visible-to-physical device mapping from #16256 is merged in upstream main as `9750add07ee64aa966ce2d03e86c8e070b46e9f6`. This PR builds on that merged implementation and contains only the endpoint-selection fix.

DP workers can share `local_rank=0` while binding different visible NPUs. The old `setup_ascend_local_comm_res()` indexed `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` with this rank, which could select the wrong `ub_endpoint_npu_<id>.json`. Containers exposing only part of a host's NPUs additionally require runtime-to-host conversion.

Pass the bound `visible_device_index` from the worker into the helper, then resolve its host physical ID through `current_platform.visible_device_id_to_physical_device_id()` merged by #16256. Select the endpoint file using that physical ID and propagate mapping errors. Calls without endpoint configuration still return without performing conversion.

Rebased onto upstream main `e2f7e3110` after #16256 merged. The PR now contains one endpoint-fix commit and four files: `vllm_ascend/utils.py`, `vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py`, `tests/ut/test_local_comm_res.py`, and `tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py`. No prerequisite platform or native-binding commits remain in this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Endpoint files configured through `ascend_local_comm_res_path` are selected by the bound NPU's host physical ID. This uses the native conversion binding already merged by #16256 and requires an extension built with a supporting CANN version.

### How was this patch tested?

- 12 focused unit tests passed for the combined stack, including endpoint selection, error propagation, platform delegation, and passing the bound visible ordinal instead of local rank.
- Built and installed the native extension with CANN 9.1.0 for Ascend950DT (`ascend950dt_9582`).
- All 13 independent process checks passed across non-privileged container mounts `0,1,2,3`, `2,3`, `1,3`, and `3`. Each used vLLM local rank 0 and checked device count, host physical ID, real endpoint-file selection, and invalid IDs. Visibility was unset or restricted to the last container logical device.
- The hardware and focused-UT results above describe the earlier combined stack. No model-serving or P/D transfer workload was run. For the latest rebase, the endpoint patch is unchanged (`git range-diff`), Python syntax checks, Ruff 0.14.0 lint/format checks on all four changed files, and `git diff --check` passed. The merged platform interface and worker device-binding order were reviewed. Hardware tests were not rerun on this rebased checkout; CI will validate the rewritten commit.

Runtime validation used vLLM `2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a` and vLLM-Ascend `f8481287a07cd7c407a3142f5d4188d71d964467`, existing connector changes, and the combined patch (SHA256 `6509d3bdd0f3ab437e505329bd5fc01124d7010a1b73ed0d76c789c557005db6`). The installed torch_npu requires ascending visibility lists; descending lists fail before the binding.

### Additional partial-container validation (2026-09-11)

Tested on Ascend950DT with CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu, and torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, using the previously validated image `vllm-ascend:npu-id-fixed-v2-20260910`. title: [BugFix][P/D][KVOffload]: fix preempt offloading multi D2H on MRV2 & fix mamba align mode resume index

title: [Performance] Commit only dirty block table ranges to NPU
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4 decode currently copies every active block-table row to the NPU on each scheduler step, even though a step usually appends only a small number of block IDs.

This PR keeps the device block table persistent, tracks the dirty range of each CPU row, packs only those ranges into double-buffered staging buffers, and updates the device table with a Triton scatter kernel. Dummy-run and graph-capture paths continue to use the full-table commit. `VLLM_ASCEND_BLOCK_TABLE_NO_COMMIT_OPTIMIZE=1` provides a compatibility and profiling fallback to the original full-copy path.

On an 8-NPU DeepSeek V4 W8A8 decode run with `--max-model-len 65536`, the rank-0 Ascend profile showed:

| Metric | Full-copy baseline | Dirty-range commit |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Decode steps | 107 | 108 |
| Stream-47 memcpy calls per step | 98 | 92 fixed + dirty updates |
| Stream-47 memcpy time per step | 108.474 us | 90.681 us |
| Direct memcpy saving | - | 17.793 us/step |

The optimized trace contained 31 scatter launches and 62 dirty-range H2D copies (packed block IDs plus metadata). Their total cost was 185.743 us, or about 5.99 us per dirty update. The end-to-end notify interval changed from 47,287.189 us to 47,224.280 us on this short capture; that sample is too short to claim a statistically stable end-to-end gain, while the eliminated full-table copies and their direct cost are visible in the trace.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or serving behavior change. The dirty-range commit is enabled by default and can be disabled with `VLLM_ASCEND_BLOCK_TABLE_NO_COMMIT_OPTIMIZE=1`.

### How was this patch tested?

- 15 CPU unit tests covering dirty tracking, row add/append/move/swap/clear behavior, runtime commit fallback, staging-buffer reuse, and environment parsing.
- 8 NPU tests covering the Triton scatter kernel.
- Ascend profiling with the following actual serving script at `/home/w00943508/ds_v4/scripts/serve_dsv4_block_table_opt.sh`:

<details>
<summary>Serving command used for profiling</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
cd /home/w00943508/ds_v4
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libjemalloc.so.2:$LD_PRELOAD
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export VLLM_ASCEND_BLOCK_TABLE_NO_COMMIT_OPTIMIZE=0

exec vllm serve /home/weights/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-w8a8-mtp \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --served-model-name dsv4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
  --quantization ascend \
  --port 8000 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 1,"method": "mtp","enforce_eager": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":true,"enable_static_kernel":false},"enable_cpu_binding":true,"enable_dsa_cp":true,"enable_flashcomm1":true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/home/w00943508/ds_v4/profiling/block_table_opt_0260","torch_profiler_with_stack":false}'
```

The request used `model=dsv4`, prompt `你好`, `max_tokens=1000`, `temperature=0`, and `ignore_eos=true`. Profiling started about one second after sending the request and stopped after five seconds.

title: [Performance][Ops] Add FLA NPU backend for GDN prefill on A5
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds an opt-in FLA NPU fused backend for Gated Delta Net (GDN) prefill on Ascend A5.

- Adds a dedicated `ascend_gdn_prefill_backend` additional-config key so the Ascend selector does not conflict with vLLM's upstream-injected `gdn_prefill_backend` key.
- Keeps the existing Ascend GDN prefill behavior when the new option is unset: use the built-in CANN fused operator when available and supported, otherwise fall back to the Triton Ascend implementation.
- Accepts only `fla_npu` as an explicit value. 
- Dynamically loads `fla_npu.ops.ascendc.chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` from the external `flash-linear-attention-npu` package only when `fla_npu` is configured. This path targets Ascend A5 and currently requires PCP world size 1.
- Documents the configuration contract and default behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can opt in to the external FLA NPU backend with:

```bash
vllm serve MODEL --additional-config='{"ascend_gdn_prefill_backend":"fla_npu"}'
```

When `ascend_gdn_prefill_backend` is omitted, existing users keep the automatic CANN-to-Triton fallback behavior. If the option is specified, the only valid value is `fla_npu`.

### How was this patch tested?

Added CPU unit-test coverage for:

- the unset default and preservation of the existing backend path;
- loading the external FLA operator through a fake module, without installing or cloning the external repository in standard CI;
- the missing-dependency error path;
- the external operator's extended return tuple and forwarded kernel arguments;
- recurrent-state scattering when empty sequences are filtered from the kernel batch.

CI results for commit `8e2805715`:

- pre-commit: passed;
- mypy: passed;
- CPU unit tests: passed;
- DCO, PR validation, documentation link checks, and Read the Docs builds: passed.

A real A5 end-to-end numerical and performance validation with a compatible `flash-linear-attention-npu` package is still required before merge. The remaining `ci-gate` check requires a maintainer to add one of the repository's ready labels.

title: [Performance] Fuse GLM-5.3-Flash KDA decode output writeback
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

For ordinary decode-only GLM-5.3-Flash KDA batches, combine recurrent-output padding masking, destination zeroing and the final copy into one Triton writeback kernel. The native recurrent operator still computes its usual temporary output and state. Mixed prefill/decode and speculative paths retain their existing behavior.

DP validation exposed two issues in the initial implementation. Fully masked blocks beyond the source allocation could fault on Ascend; the kernel now skips these loads, including the empty-source case. Varying request counts and DP padding lengths also caused repeated compilations; these dimensions are now non-specialized runtime scalars. Tiles are limited to 16KB (8192 FP16/BF16 or 4096 FP32 elements) to amortize bounds checks without exceeding FP32 local-memory limits.

The Triton kernel and its Python entry point live together in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/output_writeback.py`; the model imports `write_recurrent_output` from this operator module.

The [output_writeback.md operator document](https://github.com/lijiahang226/vllm-ascend/blob/f5668dfbb8cf3b8ae9dec418d59c33a3d3fdb5c4/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/output_writeback.md) follows the repository Triton template and describes the formula, parameter/layout contract, padding behavior, graph replay constraints, hardware validation scope and existing test entry point.

Refs #15665.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Reduces decode writeback and dynamic-shape compilation overhead without changing recurrent arithmetic or adding a configuration option.

The current optimized implementation completed a focused TP4 × DP2 / EP8 comparison: input 3500/output 256, global concurrency 8 and 64. At concurrency 8, mean TPOT decreased **2.95%–5.23%** relative to the two baselines; every candidate round was faster than every accepted baseline round. At concurrency 64, the mean difference was **0.14%–0.96%**, within observed variation, so no stable high-concurrency benefit is claimed.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Relocation validation:** The recurrent output writeback operator was relocated intact to vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/output_writeback.py; after line-ending normalization, its bytes match the previous module exactly (SHA256 b0052b9a0965156bf90ca94a0cc3c78d8d702397a1169cf8f666c554260c5110). The caller and existing nine NPU cases change only their import path, and no obsolete output_writeback import remains in this branch. The current test file LF-normalized SHA256 is abafbd9a4493413ccfb241b68583bacc25b810faec95ce67500779ecf0821b38. Changed-file Ruff check, Ruff format --check, and git diff --check passed after correcting import order and mixed line endings. Post-relocation NPU tests and local CPU UT were not run: node 167 reset three authorized SSH sessions before remote command execution, and the local environment lacks torch_npu and vllm. Previously reported nine-case NPU results predate this relocation and are historical evidence only; current-head Linux CI is reported separately below.

- **Committed operator coverage:** following the existing Triton single-card pattern (for example `test_precopy.py`, #15032), add only `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_glm5next_output_writeback.py`: **before this relocation, 9 real-NPU cases passed on node 167, Ascend A3, in 36.43 seconds**. The 70-line file compares against a CPU PyTorch reference with zero tolerance: FP16/BF16/FP32 valid-row copies and padding zeros, empty source/output, single-token decode, unaligned destination guards, and the allocation-end 63-to-1771-token DP regression with graph replay after updating input values and query ends. NaNs poison invalid rows and destinations. This is a compact operator suite, not the previous 129-case matrix. No new PR tests, CI runtime registration, or UT were added. The existing 18 CPU contract/dispatch cases remain unchanged from their passing run. The current automatic PR selector does not collect this nightly directory; the NPU result is an explicit hardware run, not a claimed PR CI gate. It used the existing operator conftest and `--confcutdir` at the ops directory, with the then-current test-file hash and production operator hash recorded. The relocation changes the test import path; that historical run is not a new-path NPU execution.
- Validated implementation `a06119e4f93debd21caf08b9fbc180d3feaa9be5`: **142 NPU cases and 21 CPU contract/dispatch tests passed** on node 167, Ascend A3 (163 total, 101.63 seconds). Production/test SHA256 match the committed files. Covers FP16/BF16/FP32, empty/ragged shapes, storage guards, allocation-end large padding, changing query counts and graph replay. All output comparisons are exact. This is a historical broader shape sweep; current committed coverage is the compact suite above.
- Fresh-cache dynamic-length comparison: eight combinations of source length, destination length and query count produced **8 kernel variants before versus 1 after**. Their cumulative first-call time was **28.515 seconds versus 4.432 seconds**, with exact outputs. This measures compilation plus first execution, not end-to-end model throughput.
- Warm microbenchmark: seven alternating-order samples, each graph containing 128 writes, across 16/32/64 heads. At 63 source → 1771 destination tokens, median graph time fell **130.58→33.96 / 260.72→66.64 / 519.99→131.51 microseconds**, respectively. Single-token graph time remained approximately 2.3 microseconds. Host eager dispatch can add about 1 microsecond for small cases; the completed DP comparison below shows a low-concurrency benefit but no clear high-concurrency benefit.
- An earlier runtime-scalar/1024-element draft removed recompilation but slowed large writes, so it was rejected. An unconditional 8192-element tile failed FP32 compilation because of local-memory limits; the final dtype-sized tile passed the complete suite. Failure evidence and tuning measurements are retained.
- Allocation-end reproduction of the former DP failure (63 source → 1771 destination, 16 heads) faulted before the safety guard and passed with it. Previous head `c2b15544` also completed TP4×DP2/EP8, input/output 256, concurrency 128: two warmups plus three compilation-free rounds (768 measured requests), no device fault and zero preemptions. Its next concurrency-256 sweep exposed the recompilation problem; that matrix was intentionally interrupted to prioritize this fix, with all results preserved.
- The focused TP4 x DP2 / EP8 campaign is complete: input 3500 / output 256, global concurrency 8 and 64, two full-output warmups and three accepted rounds per cell. Temperature 0, seed 1024; FULL_DECODE_ONLY plus breakable graphs, captures 1/2/4/8/16/32/64/128, max batched tokens 2048. Prefill is not fully captured. All eight workers used the intended source hashes, the same #17109 host fix, 791 cache blocks and a common frozen cache seed. All 432 accepted fixed-output requests in each arm matched the first baseline token-for-token; both engines recorded zero preemptions. All 200 sampled ownership records across four arms (including the original before-baseline performance run) had no external occupants. The original six before-baseline performance rounds were reused after the Docker working-directory client-launch failure; they were not rerun or reported as new measurements.

| Global concurrency | Before / candidate / after TPOT (ms) | Reduction vs before / after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 55.4755 / 52.5740 / 54.1705 | 5.23% / 2.95% |
| 64 | 196.6617 / 196.3902 / 198.3028 | 0.14% / 0.96% |

At concurrency 8 all three candidate rounds (52.4806/52.6318/52.6097 ms) were below all six accepted baseline rounds (minimum 53.3453 ms), supporting a benefit for this measured configuration. The baseline means drifted by -2.35%, so the headline reduction is a range rather than a single universal percentage. At concurrency 64, candidate rounds were 192.5977/202.3217/194.2513 ms; the slower round remains included. The 0.14%-0.96% mean difference is small relative to the candidate variance and +0.83% baseline drift; no stable high-concurrency benefit is claimed.

- Full GSM8K: **1259 / 1266 / 1266 out of 1319** (before / candidate / after), zero request errors. The unchanged baselines differ on 21 question grades. The candidate is wrong on 6 questions correct in both baselines and correct on 5 wrong in both. These are genuine numeric-answer differences, not format-only failures; equal aggregate scores do not establish per-question equivalence or attribute all differences to scheduling. Raw answers/grades are preserved.
- All accepted rounds had no changed Triton cache metadata. One separate candidate attempt with new metadata was excluded under the declared rule. No slow accepted round was removed. TP2 x DP4 / EP8 and TP1 x DP8 / EP8 are not claimed complete for this head. The independent conv DP16 result is not evidence for this candidate.
- Earlier TP8 accuracy audit: fixed-cohort runs of two baselines and the original candidate all scored 1254/1319 with identical final numeric answers/grades. Normal-concurrency repetitions varied; these historical runs do not establish latest-head DP accuracy equivalence. An earlier real-native KDA audit also matched outputs/state in 100/100 cases and all 65,280 finite BF16 encodings.
- **Current source:** `f5668dfbb8cf3b8ae9dec418d59c33a3d3fdb5c4`, based on main `972fcd5c974d55a7970ebe630329daa4b4049c49`. This follow-up adds only `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/output_writeback.md`. Product code, existing tests, operator launches and CI configuration are unchanged from `bcb68c904a67edef0f203bea251905bf73895acf`. It introduces no new UT or nightly cases and no new hardware or whole-model performance/accuracy claim. The historical validation boundaries above still apply.
- **Current-head CI:** For documentation head f5668dfbb8cf3b8ae9dec418d59c33a3d3fdb5c4, the [Linux pre-commit job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35844190069/job/107126242669) passed, including markdownlint, Ruff check/format, all other listed hooks, and three mypy passes on 644, 39, and 819 source files. DCO, PR creation, and merge-conflict labeler passed. The [CPU UT job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35844190069/job/107127831503) is in progress; selected device tests and ci-gate have not reached a result on this head, so the full E2E workflow is pending. No current-head check has failed. GitHub reports MERGEABLE with mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, rather than a merge conflict.

title: [Performance] Optimize GLM-5.3-Flash convolution state copies
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reduce GLM-5.3-Flash conv-state copy cost by computing the source/destination addresses in the existing Triton copy kernels. The bounded grid covers each sequence's actual state elements without launching over the full padded physical page. The model's conv-state layout, state values, and cache capacity are unchanged.

The Triton copy kernel lives in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/conv_state.py`, following the direct-kernel pattern used by `batch_memcpy` and `precopy`. The model-side AscendC wrapper retains its existing launch-grid and argument reuse.

The [conv_state.md operator document](https://github.com/lijiahang226/vllm-ascend/blob/a78468a1eaa64bd4d85376ea07810380b059861c/vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/conv_state.md) follows the repository Triton template and describes the formula, parameter/layout contract, padding behavior, graph replay constraints, hardware validation scope and existing test entry point.

Refs #15665.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Improves conv-state copy latency without a new configuration or checkpoint conversion. The optimized implementation at `1ab020889e593ae67e9f9cc9d5a7ba674a346840` completed the requested compact TP1 × DP16 / EP16 long-input comparison on Ascend A3.

| Input / output tokens | Global concurrency | Before / conv / after TPOT (ms) | TPOT reduction vs before / after | Output throughput improvement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 32768 / 1024 | 16 | 56.850 / 49.664 / 56.745 | 12.64% / 12.48% | 10.70%–10.76% |
| 65536 / 4096 | 16 | 56.796 / 49.626 / 56.829 | 12.62% / 12.67% | 12.55%–12.61% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 64 | 179.196 / 149.039 / 179.229 | 16.83% / 16.84% | 15.09%–15.30% |

Before baseline and candidate have three accepted rounds per case. The after baseline has one accepted round per case under the predeclared adaptive rule: add two more if drift exceeds 3%, the candidate's margin is under 3%, or preemption occurs. None triggered after excluding compilation-affected rounds. The after-baseline sample is consequently weaker than a full three-round comparison. Baseline TPOT drift was -0.185%, +0.057%, and +0.019%; every candidate round was faster than every accepted baseline round in its case. These are observed improvements, not confidence intervals, and are not additive with independent PRs.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Relocation validation:** The convolution state kernel was relocated to vllm_ascend/ops/triton/kda/conv_state.py. An AST comparison confirms the kernel is identical apart from its public name, its block constants are unchanged, and the causal_conv1d wrapper is identical apart from references to that name. The two existing NPU cases remain in the operator test; its current LF-normalized SHA256 is c0221e72711ea45262320d896de6111dfdb4fe759bcd1066ff3b2204edf4eb35, and the new kernel file SHA256 is 367d7e5a8d87c88567e2cf1f88cee5bfaa7355104b2eeca5b0fcf5519e4f021b. Changed-file Ruff check, Ruff format --check, git diff --check, and relevant stale-reference scan passed. Post-relocation NPU tests and local CPU UT were not run: node 167 reset three authorized SSH sessions before remote command execution, and the local environment lacks torch_npu and vllm. Previously reported NPU results predate this relocation and are historical evidence only; current-head Linux CI is reported separately below.

- **Committed test scope:** no new PR or nightly cases and no CI runtime registration. Only the two cases already present in main's `test_glm5next_conv_state.py` remain, with the required argument/grid adaptation for the changed copy kernel. The expanded 229-case matrix has been removed from the PR. The previous 231-case A3 execution remains historical validation evidence; the retained cases were unchanged in that coverage-reduction follow-up. This relocation only updates their import and kernel name; the earlier A3 run predates the relocation.
- **DP16 long-input performance:** physical devices 0–15 on node 167; same W8A8 checkpoint, vLLM `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`, model runner v1, FULL_DECODE_ONLY with breakable capture sizes 1/2/4/8/16, max batched tokens 2048, temperature 0, seed 1024. Async scheduling, prefix caching, and MTP were disabled. Prefill was not claimed to run wholly in a graph. Each measured round submitted twice the global concurrency with fixed output length. Prior full-length baseline warmups were reused; candidate/after used a 32-token warmup and excluded rounds with new compilation. One candidate and one after-baseline round were excluded and retained as evidence.
- **Capacity and ownership:** all 16 workers in all three arms had matching source provenance, the same loaded KDA host library, and 166 cache blocks. Accepted measurements had zero preemption and no foreign-device occupancy. Candidate TTFT and p95/p99 TPOT were also lower in all three cases. The test controller and its three model services have exited.
- **Fixed long-output token checks:** all 576 candidate sequences across nine accepted rounds matched the corresponding before-baseline token sequences exactly, including every token of 4096-token outputs. All 192 paired after-baseline sequences also matched. This tests those fixed prompts, not universal generation identity.
- **Long-context accuracy:** 32/32 numerical answers for all three arms. Original strict `ANSWER:` formatting scores remain 27/32, 28/32, and 27/32; the other answers were correct bare numbers. The numerical audit is separate from, and does not overwrite, the strict scoring.
- **Full GSM8K:** all 1319 questions at global concurrency 64, temperature 0, seed 1024: before **1260/1319**, candidate **1263/1319**, after **1262/1319**, with zero request errors. Before versus candidate had 8 correct-to-incorrect and 11 incorrect-to-correct answers; the two baselines themselves had 9 and 11. After versus candidate had 11 and 12. Six candidate errors were correct in both baselines. There is no observed aggregate accuracy regression; individual generations differ, so this is not a claim of universal numerical equivalence or improved accuracy.
- **Copy correctness:** 229 NPU shape cases passed. In the previously failing mixed batch, 34 layers × 2 steps × 4 TP ranks produced 272 paired comparisons with bitwise-identical copy outputs and complete state storage.
- **Individual kernel timing:** on A3, TP8 / 8 sequences, current bounded-grid implementation: state read **27.92 → 22.01 us**, writeback **218.14 → 21.80 us** per device call. Measured with 128 calls per captured graph and seven alternating-order device-event samples; these are individual kernels, not the whole wrapper or model latency.
- **Shared correctness dependency:** the earlier mixed-batch failure also reproduced on unmodified baseline. Its AscendC KDA workspace overlap is fixed separately in #17109. All three DP16 arms used the same verified fixed host library (`fe38d957bdde50008fef782228cab468c7521ee9fd0afcab0f05ed6544cea0a2`), so its benefit is not attributed to this PR. The captured failure fixture passed 40/40 after that fix and controlled baseline/conv replays both passed 26/26.
- **Current source:** `a78468a1eaa64bd4d85376ea07810380b059861c`, based on main `972fcd5c974d55a7970ebe630329daa4b4049c49`. This follow-up adds only `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/conv_state.md`. Product code, existing tests, operator launches and CI configuration are unchanged from `ab91ba1c20f7b98bf915232e33be1c747810de46`. It introduces no new UT or nightly cases and no new hardware or whole-model performance/accuracy claim. The historical validation boundaries above still apply.
- **Current-head CI:** For documentation head a78468a1eaa64bd4d85376ea07810380b059861c, the [Linux pre-commit job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35844179909/job/107126207370) passed, including markdownlint, Ruff check/format, all other listed hooks, and three mypy passes on 644, 39, and 818 source files. DCO, PR creation, and merge-conflict labeler passed. The [CPU UT job](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/35844179909/job/107127470243) is in progress; selected device tests and ci-gate have not reached a result on this head, so the full E2E workflow is pending. No current-head check has failed. GitHub reports MERGEABLE with mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, rather than a merge conflict.

Scope: this completes the user-approved reduced three-case DP16 comparison. It does not claim completion of the abandoned eight-case matrix, other hardware, or combined-optimization performance.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][Worker] Route vLLM 0.28 through legacy Spec+PP
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`use_legacy_spec_pp()` currently selects Ascend's legacy speculative pipeline-parallel transport only for vLLM 0.29.0. When the main-branch plugin is paired with vLLM 0.28.x, it skips the compatibility path even though that release predates the upstream sampled-token protocol.

Recognize the vLLM 0.28 and 0.29 release families, including local and release-candidate builds, while keeping vLLM 0.30 and newer on the native protocol. Update the DSpark loader comment and the version-routing regression matrix accordingly.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. vLLM 0.28.x deployments using speculative decoding with pipeline parallelism now select the required legacy transport and loader bypasses.

### How was this patch tested?

- `VLLM_PLUGINS="" PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/ut/worker/v2 tests/ut/worker/v2/test_pp_utils.py` — 28 passed.
- `uvx ruff check vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pp_utils.py vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_dspark.py tests/ut/worker/v2/test_pp_utils.py`
- `uvx ruff format --check vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pp_utils.py vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_dspark.py tests/ut/worker/v2/test_pp_utils.py`
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Performance][Sampler] Parallelize penalty updates across vocabulary tiles
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Distribute independent sequence/vocabulary tiles across vector cores so small batches no longer scan each vocabulary on one core. Preserve the penalty arithmetic and in-place updates.

On NPU, measured large-vocabulary updates improve **1.6–2.8×**, and the complete penalty pipeline improves up to **1.40×**. These are operator measurements, not model-throughput gains. This targets the legacy sampler; MRV2 uses a separate implementation.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Faster application of active penalties. Empty updates return without launching a kernel.

### How was this patch tested?

- 46 tests passed on NPU, covering dtypes, tails, strides, empty shapes, and the sampler wrapper.
- All 12 update and eight pipeline comparisons matched exactly; eight Qwen3.8-27B BF16 serving smokes produced identical outputs.
- Formatting and Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 targeted type checks pass; a benchmark is included.

Hardware measurements used the v0.26 overlay before the quotient-reuse indexing rewrite. Its CPU tile-coverage and integer-boundary checks pass; the current-main NPU rerun and A2/A3 measurements remain pending.

title: [Performance] Optimize QLI top-k merge workspace
body:
## What this PR does

Adapt the optimized QLI implementation from CANN ops-transformer commit [a8b19d16](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer/commit/a8b19d16da89e4d61766f2701312f3ea8175498d?ref=experimental&prId=12407).

The QLI v2 arch22 kernel previously reserved and transferred a fixed 2048-entry merge buffer even when `sparse_count` was smaller. This change:

- aligns the merge width to `sparse_count` (64-entry alignment)
- shrinks UB merge buffers and merge/extract lengths
- reduces LD workspace transfers for both the standard and P10 segmented paths

For the common `sparse_count=512` path, the merge workspace is reduced from 2048 entries to 512 entries.

title: [Feature][SpecDecode] Enable ACL graph mode for GLM-Next MTP draft models
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, draft model `glm5_next_mtp`) uses MTP speculative decoding with draft layers split across multiple physical KV-cache groups:

- primary MLA attention
- indexer KPool
- compressor tail

The generic GLM speculative-decoding path previously forced the draft model to run eagerly. In addition, the multi-KV-group runtime metadata was rebuilt using per-round tensor clones. Although correct in eager mode, these dynamically allocated tensors are incompatible with ACL graph replay, which requires the captured input addresses to remain stable.

This PR enables ACL graph mode for the specialized `AscendMultiKVCacheGroupMTPProposer` used by `glm5_next_mtp`. 

Other GLM speculative-decoding implementations remain forced to eager mode. Users can still explicitly keep the GLM-Next MTP draft eager by setting `"enforce_eager": true` in the speculative configuration.

The main changes are:

1. **GLM-Next MTP graph capability**

   The specialized multi-KV-group proposer declares support for GLM draft graph mode. The generic GLM forced-eager behavior remains unchanged for other GLM draft implementations.

2. **Graph-stable common metadata**

   Persistent per-`(KV-cache group, draft step)` slot-mapping buffers replace per-round clones. Capture and runtime drafting therefore reuse the same tensor addresses.

3. **Graph-stable KPool derived metadata**

   `AscendIndexerKPoolMetadataBuilder` keeps persistent buffers for:

   - compressed slot mappings
   - sequence lengths
   - cumulative query lengths
   - raw sequence lengths
   - positions

   The buffers are keyed by the persistent common slot-mapping address so that capture and replay bind the same storage.

4. **FULL graph padding support**

   Request-shaped KPool metadata buffers are sized using:

   ```python
   max(max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens)
   ```

   This covers FULL draft graph padding, where the padded request dimension may exceed `max_num_seqs`. For example, four requests with MTP K=3 use a 16-token graph bucket.

5. **Cache-only builder graph entrypoints**

   `build_for_graph_capture` and `build_for_drafting` are implemented for the KPool and KPool-tail cache-only metadata builders.

6. **Multi-group graph-capture routing**

   Graph capture builds a separate metadata view for each physical KV-cache group and routes executable and cache-only groups through their appropriate metadata-builder entrypoints.

7. **FULL-mode sequence-length robustness**

   `seq_lens_cpu` may be intentionally invalidated during the first MTP draft transition to avoid a device-to-host synchronization. The FULL-mode updater now handles the field being `None`, consistently with the existing guards for `_seq_lens_cpu` and `num_computed_tokens_cpu`.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes.

When ACL graph mode is enabled for the target model, `glm5_next_mtp` drafting now uses ACL graph mode by default. Other GLM speculative draft implementations remain eager.

Users can explicitly disable draft graph mode with:

```json
{
  "method": "mtp",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
  "enforce_eager": true
}
```

The first request using a previously uncaptured draft bucket may incur a one-time lazy graph-capture cost of approximately 10–15 seconds. Subsequent replays use the captured graph.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

Extended:

- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_multi_kv_cache_group_proposer.py`
- `tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kv_cache.py`

The tests cover:

- persistent address semantics across metadata rebuilds
- independent buffers for different MTP draft steps
- KPool graph-capture and drafting entrypoints
- FULL-mode operation with absent CPU sequence lengths
- padded `num_reqs` exceeding `max_num_seqs`
- multi-group graph-capture metadata routing

The targeted unit-test suites pass with 40+ test cases.

#### End-to-end validation

Hardware and configuration:

- Atlas A3, 8 × Ascend 910
- tensor parallel size 8
- expert parallel enabled
- GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8
- MTP K=3
- target graph mode: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`
- graph capture sizes up to 128

Results:

- draft buckets 4, 8, 16 and 32 passed
- request concurrency 1, 2, 4 and 8 passed
- all requests returned coherent output
- rejection-sampler acceptance remained 75%–100%
- greedy graph-mode output was bit-exact with the eager baseline across
  20 `(prompt, concurrency)` pairs
- repeated graph batches produced identical output, with no stale-metadata
  regression

Steady-state latency at concurrency 4 improved from 1.028 s to 0.863 s (approximately 1.19×).

At concurrency 8, graph mode also reduced latency. The measured mean was 1.984 s to 1.073 s, although the eager sample contained several approximately 5-second outliers; the corresponding median changed from approximately 1.25 s to 1.10 s.

### Notes

The remaining family-wide GLM forced-eager path is intentionally retained for GLM draft implementations that have not declared graph support.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Feature][MRV2] Extend fine-grained TP support (MLP, embedding) to model runner v2
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Extends fine-grained TP on model runner v2 beyond o_proj, on top of the framework landed in #16967 (and its prerequisite #17128). The four knobs split into two families with different contracts:

1. **MLP TP joins the o_proj (uniform-token) contract.** The MLP exchange (gate_up `all_gather` / down `reduce_scatter` over DP-axis groups) needs the same group-uniform token count per step as o_proj, so `mlp_tensor_parallel_size > 1` joins the graph-mode / PCP / `tp == 1` / PD-scenario checks, the capture-bound auto-disable (a miss disables both knobs together — the bound is a property of the step, not of a knob), the `PreemptOffloadConnector` gate, the offload-failure abort, and the eager-step guard (renamed `_check_finegrained_tp_graph_step`).
2. **Embedding TP is capacity-based and joins none of the uniform-token checks.** Its exchange pads every step to a fixed capacity inside the op, so it is step-shape-agnostic and cannot desync; the runtime capacity already floors at `max_num_batched_tokens`, so its one real failure mode fails fast on its own.
3. **The recompute-scheduler requirement covers all four knobs.** o_proj and embedding already required it on main; mlp joins as it enters the uniform-token contract, and lmhead joins so the whole `finegrained_tp_config` stays within the one configuration validated end-to-end. The first traffic test of the no-recompute path on the PD test bed produced deterministically wrong outputs with every knob off (a pre-existing defect unrelated to this PR, tracked separately), so that path stays outside the supported set until it is fixed.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- `mlp_tensor_parallel_size` now works on the V2 runner in graph-mode PD-decode deployments, with the same preconditions as `oproj_tensor_parallel_size`.
- All four `finegrained_tp_config` sizes require `recompute_scheduler_enable=true` (previously only o_proj and embedding did).
- At runtime, an eagerly dispatched step under o_proj/MLP TP fails the request with an explicit error (the message now names both knobs).

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests**: one new case in `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` (MLP capture-bound, incl. the both-knobs-disabled-together semantics); the remaining gates are shared conditions already covered by the existing o_proj cases. CI on the current head: `pre-commit` and `cpu-ut` green.

**End-to-end** — single-node A3 (16 chips), PD disaggregation behind the LB proxy; DeepSeek-V3.1-arch W8A8 checkpoint truncated to 6 layers (real weights, `--quantization ascend`). P = chip 0 (`tp1`, eager, Mooncake producer); D = chips 8-15 (`dp8 × tp1`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture size 512, recompute scheduler on, `MultiConnector` = Mooncake consumer + `PreemptOffloadConnector`); every request goes through the proxy. Each round: 8-concurrent × 256-token bench × 3 (6144 tokens) plus 5 fixed greedy prompts for consistency.

Positive rounds (all: 8/8 startup, 100% of bench tokens, knob reported enabled, zero guard hits, zero auto-disables, zero collective errors):

| Round | Engine TPOT | Output vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 7.12 ms | — |
| `mlp=2` | 7.33 ms | 1/5 prompts identical, the rest diverge at the first token (see note) |
| `oproj=2 + mlp=2` | 7.24 ms | same class as `mlp=2`; bit-identical to the three-knob round |
| `embedding=2` | 7.32 ms | **5/5 bit-identical** |
| all three knobs | 7.14 ms | bit-identical to the `oproj=2+mlp=2` round |

Consistency note: re-sharding o_proj/MLP changes the reduction order, and the truncated 6-layer test model has a near-flat output distribution, so the greedy pick can flip at the first token — the same class of difference as changing the generic TP size. The embedding exchange is pure data movement and stays bit-identical, including when stacked with the other two knobs.

Negative configs (rejected or disabled at startup, no hang):

| Config | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `mlp=2` + `--enforce-eager` | rejected at config load ("only supported in graph mode") |
| `mlp=2` without `PreemptOffloadConnector` | rejected with the explicit connector requirement |
| `mlp=2` without the recompute scheduler | rejected at config load in ~15 s with the recompute-scheduler requirement (the all-knobs gate above) |
| capture bound 512 < largest step 600 | both knobs auto-disabled with a warning; startup completes |

Base controls: the rounds above ran on the base before #17159; since #17159 reworked the embedding exchange, the embedding-relevant cells were re-run on the current base — baseline and `embedding=2` outputs are **bit-identical** to the pre-#17159 results (TPOT 7.52 / 7.18 ms). A no-recompute control on the current base produced deterministically wrong outputs with **every knob off** (a pre-existing defect, tracked separately); `embedding=2` on that path is bit-identical to the no-knob run, i.e. fine-grained TP adds no effect — this is the defect behind the all-knobs recompute requirement.

**Memory** (same bed): the family's fixed cost is one HCCL buffer set (~0.42 GB per rank, from #16967); MLP saves 0.55 GiB per rank at `mlp=2` on the 6-layer bed (dense-FFN layers × 1/2), o_proj 0.109 GiB per layer per rank on a 1-byte checkpoint (#16967).

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][KV Pool] Fix layerwise cache group indexing under PP

With layerwise AscendStore and multiple KV cache groups, a nonzero PP stage can raise `IndexError` in `LayerBatchBuilder._build_transfer_arrays()` when indexing `_layer_cache_entry_offsets_np`. The group map has used stage-local layer IDs since #16412, but #16208 added the global PP offset when looking up save/load tasks. title: [Feature](kv_transfer): add MooncakeHeterogeneousConnector for heterogeneous PD KV transfer
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

Impl https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/16353

Adds a P-side KV transfer connector, `MooncakeHeterogeneousConnector`, for **heterogeneous prefill-decode disaggregation**: an Ascend 910B NPU node runs Prefill and a separate GPU node (e.g. NVIDIA H20) runs Decode, with KV cache transferred between them over Mooncake RDMA P2P. The D side uses upstream vLLM's `MooncakeConnector` (`kv_consumer`) unchanged; this connector implements the P side (`kv_producer`) in vLLM-Ascend.

### Architecture (request-triggered, non-layerwise)

- `MooncakeHeterogeneousConnector`/`Worker`: on D pull, transfer all layers in one shot via `start_load_kv` + `mark_all_tasks_done` -> `FINISH`. Mirrors upstream P-side `send_kv_to_decode` timing.
- `MooncakeHeterogeneousXferAdapter` + `MooncakeXferMetadata`: cross-end wire protocol mirroring upstream vLLM (`CONTINUE`/`FINISH`/`ERROR`), bootstrapped via a TCP port (8998) where P registers its adapter address for D to fetch.
- **Heterogeneous KV layout**: P NPU NHD (k/v split) -> D GPU HND (4D, k/v interleaved in last dim) via `index_select` + `permute(0,2,1,3)` + `cat(-1)`, transferring 1 merged region per layer.
- **spec dispatch**: standard attention (k,v) and MLA/`SlidingWindowMLASpec` reuse the same `hnd_buf` branch; Mamba/linear-attention (GDN) raises `NotImplementedError` (SSM state transfer not yet supported).
- **Config**: 3 ENVs (`VLLM_ASCEND_KV_TRANSFER_HOST`/`_RDMA_HOST`/`_DEVICE`) + `VLLM_ASCEND_HETEROGENEOUS_CONNECTOR_PORT_OFFSET` + `kv_connector_extra_config` (prefill/decode `dp_size`/`tp_size`). `extra_config` > ENV > default. TP>1 binds per-rank ports (`kv_port + tp_rank + offset`).

### Quality

- Init `_pending_hnd_bufs` in `__init__` (drop `hasattr` lazy init); `hnd_buf` kept in `_pending_hnd_bufs` until `get_finished` confirms `FINISH` to avoid GC during async RDMA.
- `logger.debug` for MLA/SlidingWindow spec reuse branch.

## Tests

29 unit tests (mock `TransferEngine` + `global_te` + zmq, no NPU) covering scheduler logic, address computation, MLA reuse, Mamba raise, `get_finished` reporting

Reproduce (P: 910B,  D: h20):
```bash
# D (vllm): MooncakeConnector, kv_consumer
```

title: [BugFix][Sleep] Keep a dedicated 1 MiB HCCL lifecycle anchor
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`rl_config.sleep_mode_extra_cleanup` destroys HCCL process groups during sleep so EP/MC2 windows can be returned to the trainer. Destroying every multi-rank communicator can tear down shared CANN HCCP/AICPU state. After restore, the first DSA metadata op (`SparseAttnSharedkvMetadata`) then fails and `wake_up` returns 500.

This PR does not keep a business group (TP/DP/EP/world). Before teardown it creates a dedicated world-size HCCL group named `sleep_lifecycle_anchor` with a **1 MiB** buffer, initializes it with a device `barrier`, and uses that group as a temporary lifecycle nail:

1. Sleep creates the coordinator on the first cycle, or `restore_hccl()` on later cycles if the communicator was released after the previous wake-up.
2. A device barrier physically initializes the nail (HCCL `new_group` can be lazy).
3. All other HCCL groups are destroyed. If the nail cannot be established, teardown is skipped for that cycle.
4. Wake-up restores business groups and refreshes MoE/MC2 metadata. The nail stays up through ACL Graph recapture.
5. After recapture (or after the `kv_cache` stage of level-2 wake-up), all ranks barrier on the nail and `destroy_hccl()` it. The Python coordinator is kept (`device_group=None`) and reused next sleep, so the same group name is not registered twice.

`get_hccl_config_for_pg_options` returns the 1 MiB size for `sleep_lifecycle_anchor` **before** building the normal config map, so sleep-time creation does not call `calculate_dp_buffer_size()` / `get_current_vllm_config()`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Extra-cleanup creates one temporary 1 MiB world-size HCCL group for each sleep/wake cycle and releases it after graph recapture. There is no new environment variable or `rl_config` key.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests in `tests/ut/device_allocator/test_sleep_mem_optimized.py`:
  - first-cycle create + reuse / restore of the existing coordinator
  - destroy/restore business groups while skipping the nail
  - skip all HCCL teardown when nail init fails
  - release after recapture; keep the nail across staged `tags=["weights"]` wake-up


- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache
body:
[Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR introduces `ECMemcacheConnector`, a MemCache-backed L1 cache
for multimodal encoder outputs. It integrates with vLLM through the
existing EC connector framework and uses the multimodal feature
identifier (`mm_hash`) as the cache key.

Repeated image or video inputs can reuse previously computed encoder
embeddings instead of running the multimodal encoder again.

- Add a scheduler-side MemCache client that checks multiple `mm_hash`
  values in one request and records cache hits and misses.
- Send per-step load/save metadata from the scheduler to workers:
  cache hits are loaded from MemCache, while misses run the encoder and
  publish the resulting embeddings.
- Load multiple encoder outputs directly into preallocated NPU tensors
  with `batch_get_into`.
- Use `KeyInfo.size()` together with the model dtype and encoder hidden
  dimension to reconstruct each cached tensor as
  `[num_encoder_tokens, hidden_dim]`.
- Publish newly computed encoder outputs directly from NPU memory with
  `put_from`.
- Record an NPU event before dispatching the put operation to a background
  thread, so MemCache waits for encoder computation without blocking the
  model-runner thread.
- Save only from TP rank 0 and PCP rank 0. Encoder outputs are identical
  across TP/PCP ranks, so publishing from every rank would duplicate data
  and cause concurrent writes to the same `mm_hash`.
- Keep eviction management inside MemCache. The connector does not add a
  separate local eviction policy.
- Track cumulative cache hits, misses, and hit rate for debugging and
  observability.

This PR also extends MemcacheBackend with:
- batch_get_into, for copying multiple values into flat destination
  buffers.
- put_from, for publishing one value directly from a device buffer.
- Optional transfer-direction arguments for the existing get and put
  wrappers while preserving their previous default directions.
When the connector is not configured, the existing encoder execution and
cache behavior remain unchanged.

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
Yes, when ECMemcacheConnector is explicitly enabled.

The connector can be enabled without modifying vLLM:

```bash
vllm serve <model> \
  --ec-transfer-config '{
    "ec_connector": "ECMemcacheConnector",
    "ec_connector_module_path":
      "vllm_ascend.distributed.ec_transfer.ec_memcache_connector",
    "ec_role": "ec_both"
  }'
```

- **Evaluation Result**: Passed (Meets Standard)

title: [WIP][Feature] Support encoder-side SWA Bounded Replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Ports upstream **Encoder-side SWA bounded replay** (vLLM [#56227](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56227)) to Ascend, for DeepSeek-V4.1 on model runner V1.

On a prefix hit upstream rewinds the request to `replay_start = H - min(window, H)`, recomputes the hit's last window, and keeps the sliding-window KV out of the prefix cache so that the recompute is what rebuilds it: the group gets `prefix_cacheable=False` and `prefix_replay_tokens=window`, and the scheduler only ever names a request that it rewound.  The positions below `replay_start` were retired and replaced by the null block, whose KV upstream documents as all-zero: a window reaching into them does not read another request's data, it reads phantom keys that score zero and take weight in the replayed token's softmax -- wrong, quiet, and only on a prefix hit. Upstream applies the clamp per request inside its SWA kernel (`start_pos = max(start_pos, replay_start)`); this PR is the Ascend equivalent, in five parts.

- **Read side** (`attention/dsa_v41.py`) -- `build_replay_swa_visible_lens` turns `replay_start` into a per-token visible ori KV length and hands it to `npu_sparse_flash_mla` through `ori_topk_length` in band mode. The operator bounds a window with one scalar for the whole call (`ori_win_left`), which cannot express a per-token floor, so the floor travels on the one channel that can. Every layer reads the ori side from the same `metadata.swa`, so no layer escapes the floor.
- **Write side** (`worker/block_table.py`, `ops/triton/compute_slot_mapping.py`) -- a Triton pass writes `PAD_SLOT_ID` over the replayed positions of every prefix-cacheable group, so the replayed recompute cannot land in blocks still shared with other requests that hit the same prefix. The bounded-replay sliding-window group is the one that keeps writing them, because that write is what rebuilds its window.
- **Carrier** (`worker/model_runner_v1.py`, `attention/utils.py`) -- a per-request `replay_start` buffer on the runner, rebuilt from zero every step on the CPU and carried to the backends on `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata`. It is `None` rather than zeros on a step that does not replay, so a dummy/profiling/capture batch cannot inherit the previous real step's values.
- **Scheduler** (`patch/platform/patch_swa_bounded_replay.py`) -- upstream reports a rewind on `NewRequestData` only, because its V2 runner folds resumed requests into the new-request list. The V1 runner resumes a preempted request through `CachedRequestData`, and a resumed request is exactly the one that can be rewound a second time (preemption clears the computed count, so readmission runs the lookup again), so the field is declared on that payload and filled from the resumed requests.
- **Operator** (`csrc/attention/sparse_flash_mla/`) -- band mode now reads `ori_topk_length` as a per-token visible length and floors the window's left edge at `right - count + 1`: arch22 in the SWA block-vector mask and in the CSA band setup, arch35 in `ComputeS2LoopInfo` before `oriKvLoopEndIdx` (on that path the loop count is the only mask there is). The width stays the scalar `ori_win_left`, so the band remains the upper bound and a supplied count can only narrow it.

`_downgrade_swa_bounded_replay` additionally turns the switch off at startup for the Ascend scheduling modes whose `schedule()` is a pinned copy of an older upstream body: they cannot rewind a prefix hit at all, so they must not have the switch on. `resolve_bounded_replay` keeps upstream's other two conditions and adds nothing of its own.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, for DeepSeek-V4.1 on model runner V1 only. Prefix hits now recompute the hit's last window instead of reusing its KV, and the sliding-window group leaves the prefix cache (no new user flag -- upstream's switch defaults to on). That is a trade the feature makes deliberately: the window is rebuilt so it can be bounded at `replay_start`. Other models never read the switch, and the release lane has neither the field nor the constructor argument.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests, CPU only (no NPU required), 58 new cases in 5 files:

- `tests/ut/worker/test_replay_slot_padding.py` (19) -- the write side: which group is padded, the pointers and window that reach the kernel launch, and the per-request `replay_start` build.
- `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_cache.py` (6) -- the read side: the per-token counts for a replayed batch, for a step that does not replay, and for the requests in the same batch that are not replaying.
- `tests/ut/core/test_kv_cache_interface.py` (15) -- the spec gate, and the group merge carrying `bounded_replay` across.
- `tests/ut/core/test_swa_replay_downgrade.py` (9) -- the scheduling modes that must turn the switch off.
- `tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_swa_bounded_replay.py` (9) -- the `CachedRequestData` field surviving msgpack and being filled from resumed requests.

**Not executed locally.** This branch was written on a machine without vLLM or an NPU, so the unit tests above and e2e tests have not been run.

**Not yet covered**

1. Operator equivalence for a single `npu_sparse_flash_mla` call: band mode with a count >= the window must be bit-identical to band mode without a count, and with a count below it, equal to band mode with `ori_win_left` narrowed by hand. This is the check that the `csrc` change does nothing when it should do nothing.
2. That the PAD pass really reaches the slot mappings the kernels read -- i.e. that a shared block's KV bytes are unchanged after a replay step.
3. DeepSeek-V4.1 e2e, gsm8k two-pass with the switch on vs off: first pass flat, second within 0.5pt, and a TTFT drop on the second pass.

title: [Feature] Add sparse HCCL weight transfer
body:
## Summary

- Add the `sparse_hccl` weight-transfer backend for Ascend NPUs.
- Reuse the dense HCCL transport lifecycle and introduce `SparseWeightPatch`, which carries runtime parameter names, flattened `int32` indices, and replacement values.
- Validate parameter name, dtype, shape, index bounds, and update count before applying an in-place sparse update.
- Add a Ray example that compares one dense update with one sparse update and verifies the two post-update outputs are identical.

NPU IPC is intentionally out of scope for this PR.

## Scope

- Supports TP=1 and PP=1.
- Requires runtime-format parameter names and layouts.
- Does not support packed sparse transfer or draft models.
- Uses the standard lifecycle: `init_weight_transfer_engine -> pause -> start_weight_update -> update_weights -> finish_weight_update -> resume`.
- Uses `weight_nz_mode=0` in the Ascend example to avoid NZ-layout differences.

## Validation

- Unit tests: `28 passed`
- Two-NPU E2E test: passed
- Ray example: passed end-to-end, including `baseline_equal`, patch-selection/digest equality, identical dense/sparse post-update output, and an output change after update.
- `git diff --check` passes after rebasing onto the current upstream `main`.

## Sparse HCCL Profile Measurements

Warm profile traces on **x86 A5**, using Qwen3-1.7B BF16 with TP=1/PP=1 and one trainer NPU plus one vLLM worker NPU. Times are Trainer-side complete send windows from warm profile sweep `110230`, not end-to-end update latency.

| Hardware | Updated elements | Dense payload | Sparse payload | Dense HCCL | Sparse HCCL | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| x86 A5 | 1% | 3281.74 MiB | 98.45 MiB | 90.79 ms | 40.55 ms | 55.3% |
| x86 A5 | 10% | 3281.74 MiB | 984.52 MiB | 90.79 ms | 41.46 ms | 54.3% |

Reduction is calculated as `(Dense HCCL - Sparse HCCL) / Dense HCCL`. These measurements are informational, not a performance gate for this rebase, and do not cover TP/PP greater than one.

title: [BugFix][WeightTransfer] Destroy native HCCL communicators on shutdown
body:
HCCL weight transfer previously dropped its Python communicator reference on shutdown without destroying the native communicator. Reinitialization also replaced the previous communicator without closing it.

Add an idempotent `close()` that synchronizes the communicator's device before calling `hcclCommDestroy`. Call it during shutdown and before reinitialization. Reuse the existing availability flag to prevent repeated destruction and reject collectives on a closed communicator. Initialization, warmup, weight reception, and exception propagation remain unchanged; no restart policy or new exception type is introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Shutdown and reinitialization explicitly release the native HCCL communicator. Calling a collective on an already closed communicator raises `RuntimeError`.

### How was this patch tested?

- 65 unit tests passed in the device-communicator and weight-transfer directories using the repository's CPU/mock UT setup and CI-pinned vLLM revision `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c` (Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.10.0).
- Regression coverage verifies device synchronization before destruction, repeated/disabled close, close failures, rejection of collectives after close, and engine shutdown/reinitialization.
- Full `bash format.sh ci`, Mypy for the four changed files (`--follow-imports skip --check-untyped-defs`, Python 3.11 target), syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

```bash
pytest -q tests/ut/distributed/device_communicators tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer
```

A real two-pod/two-NPU Ascend A3 lifecycle smoke test also passed with this exact source revision and the same CI-pinned vLLM source (PyTorch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post2). Each rank completed three communicator initialization/destruction cycles. The test checked weight transfer, all-reduce and broadcast values, explicit-stream operations followed by reinitialization/shutdown, repeated close, and rejection of use after close. Each rank executed exactly three real native destroys; both processes exited successfully. The test used 256-element float32 tensors and a lightweight weight-loading callback.

title: [Performance] Optimize rotary embedding application in DeepSeek V4 by running in-place
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
`DSparkModel._project_shared_kv` now applies RoPE in place on the rope-segment view of the normalized kv tensor, instead of materializing the rope segment and re-assembling `[k_nope | k_pe]` with `split -> rope -> cat -> contiguous` . The previous implementation paid for a full extra read+write of the `[num_tokens, head_dim]` kv tensor on every call: the rope segment was detached via `split` , rotated into a fresh tensor, and then `torch.cat` reassembled a buffer that is numerically identical to `kv` itself (only the rope segment changes; the nope segment is passed through untouched). `ComplexExpRotaryEmbedding.forward` ends with `y.copy_(...)` , i.e. `npu_rotary_mul` writes its result back to the input storage. Running the rope directly on a view of `kv` therefore produces the same final values while the nope segment never moves and no concat buffer is allocated.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
NO.

### How was this patch tested?
`pytest tests/ut/ops/test_rope_write_back.py -q`

title: Fix/dspark standard cache a3
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek-V4 DSpark could not initialize on any device: the config patch routed the
draft to `DeepSeekV4DSparkMTP`, which is A5-only and does not expose
`get_draft_kv_cache_layer_names` required by `AscendDSparkProposer`. This PR routes
the draft to the standard-cache `DSparkDraftModel` path and completes the drafting
flow:

- Register `DSparkDraftModel`; fix unreachable imports (`models/deepseek_v4/` was
  shadowed by the `deepseek_v4.py` module; `get_rotation_path` now comes from
  `patch_draft_quarot`).
- Restore the missing `DynamicSpecScheduler` (`AscendDSparkProposer` failed at
  import time without it).

  draft context KV was previously never stored.

body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Vendor DeepSeek V4.1 AscendC `CompressorV2` from
[ops-transformer PR #12647](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer/pull/12647),
pinned to `958f7a70271e5064c33068390326d4225c92e60d`, under
`csrc/attention/compressor_v2/`. Original license notices are retained.

- Include host, tiling and kernel sources in the normal A2/A3/A5 custom-op build.
- Add a mutation-aware binding and symbolic Meta implementation.
- Replace V4.1 C2 with the A2/A3 AscendC path: fuse KV/gate projections,
  pooling and FP32 ring updates, then remap compact outputs to completion-token rows.
- Leave RMSNorm, RoPE, cache writers, C1 and the V4 operator unchanged.
- Fix the vendored arch22 long-prefill ring race: snapshot partial-group history
  before in-place writes can wrap over it. Short decode skips this extra synchronization.
- Add numerical, strided-state, padding, ring-wrap, adapter and graph-replay tests.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. V4.1 C2 directly uses AscendC; rebuilding custom operators is required.
The previous FP32-projection/Triton-pooling production path and opt-in switch are removed.
Both `wkv` and `wgate` are stored as BF16. Projections accumulate into FP32, and
ring state remains FP32. Converting BF16 checkpoint weights to FP32 in the old
path did not add weight precision; end-to-end equivalence still needs comparison.

title: [Feature][KV Pool] Support Mamba in Mooncake layerwise
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Mooncake hybrid layerwise currently rejects layouts containing recurrent Mamba state. Removing that check alone is unsafe: GDN, Kimi KDA, and other Mamba-like layers update conv/recurrent state inside attention, so an attention-entry PUT can publish the previous state while the following request reports a cache hit.

This change:

- identifies physical layers containing `MambaSpec`, including per-layer `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`;
- keeps full/sliding-window attention PUTs at attention entry;
- preserves the post-compute save hook for recurrent layers so Mooncake publishes updated state;
- reuses the stage-local layer mapping and PP-scoped key namespace from #17183, mapping global recurrent layer names to the correct local layer on each pipeline stage;
- applies the existing send-backlog policy to recurrent and record-only save paths;
- drains queued PUTs at step completion, including when the final layer has no ranges to save.

The generic GDN/Mamba load, deferred state-copy, and connector hooks from #12711 are already present on main. This PR only adds the Mooncake block-key publication semantics. The implementation and lifecycle coverage are based on #17194 and credit its author in the commit.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `AscendStoreConnector` with `backend="mooncake"` and `use_layerwise=true` now accepts hybrid recurrent-state groups using `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. This also composes with Mooncake layerwise pipeline parallel support from #17183. Existing topology and prefill/decode TP-mismatch restrictions remain unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Targeted Mooncake layerwise/Mamba mock tests: 26 passed.
- PP+Mamba worker regression: 5 passed, 2 subtests; the new case covers PP rank 1, global-to-local layer mapping, regular attention-entry PUT, and Mamba post-compute PUT for raw and uniform-wrapped specs.
- CI PP layer-count regression: 2 passed; non-layerwise partial worker initialization no longer reads layerwise-only cache specs.
- `test_pool_worker.py` excluding unrelated KVPP tests: 96 passed, 2 deselected, 48 subtests passed.
- Broader AscendStore mock suite: 440 passed, with the same 3 environment/mock failures reproduced on unmodified main (435 passed, same failures).
- `ruff check` passed for all changed Python files.
- `ruff format --check` passed for all changed Python files.
- `python -m py_compile` passed for all changed Python files.
- Added a raw-token lifecycle regression covering Mamba2, GDN, generic linear attention, Full/SWA, merged/per-layer specs, chunked prefill, decode, cache hits, shared prefixes, and missing-state fallback. This file requires a full vLLM/PyTorch CPU test environment and was not executed in the local Windows mock environment.
- The equivalent patch on commit `ca91dfa600373c56cfffc44be1d77028b0dd621d` was validated successfully by the contributor on the target deployment. This latest-main rebase preserves the same transfer semantics; real NPU/Mooncake validation was not rerun in the local development environment.

`bash format.sh ci` could not run locally because `pre-commit` is not installed.

title: [Feature][MRV2] Default Model Runner V2 for all configurations
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR makes Model Runner V2 the default on Ascend when `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` is unset. The old architecture, feature, platform, and Triton whitelist is replaced by a blacklist in `vllm_ascend/mrv2_utils.py`.

When the env var is unset, a request uses V2 unless it matches one of these V1 fallbacks:

**Models / platform**

- Hy3-preview (`HYV3*`)
- Gemma4 (`Gemma4*`)
- 310P
- encoder-decoder (Whisper)
- pooling KV

**Features**

- LoRA
- VL encoder disaggregation (`ec_transfer_config` / encoder-only)
- `draft_window_size`
- suffix speculative decoding
- ngram / `ngram_gpu`
- `parallel_drafting`
- dflash2 graph (DFlash2 without `enforce_eager`)

An explicit override still wins:

- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` forces V1
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` forces V2

Upstream GPU / Triton V2 validation does not apply; Ascend owns runner selection.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Unset `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` now defaults to Model Runner V2, except for the blacklist above. Keep V1 with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`. Explicit `0` / `1` is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests: `tests/ut/test_mrv2_utils.py` (default V2, blacklist fallback, env override)
- E2E / nightly: default V2 path, plus a few explicit `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` pins
- CI: cpu-ut / e2e on this PR

title: [BugFix][SFA][GLM5Next]Reset positions for dummy batches so sparse backends see a consistent token history
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`_dummy_run` builds a dummy batch whose `seq_lens` is `max_query_len` (1 for a uniform decode step), but it only resets `self.positions` when `use_compress` is set:

```python
if self.use_compress:
    self.positions.fill_(127)
    self._dsa_positions_cpu_buf.fill_(127)
```

`use_compress` is derived from whether the model's `hf_config` carries `compress_ratios`, which marks the DeepSeek V4.x compressed-cache family. Every other model keeps whatever the previous *real* decode step wrote into `self.positions`. Attention backends that derive per-token visibility from positions then plan for a history the dummy sequence lengths do not describe.

On Ascend A5 with GLM5Next's NoPE sparse MLA this is fatal. `SparseMLAMetadataState.prepare()` computes per-token top-k lengths from `positions`, so an idle data-parallel rank produces a plan that claims ~116 visible sparse indices for a sequence the same plan says is 1 token long. The plan lands in the persistent operator buffer, and the ACL Graph replay that immediately follows consumes it, which traps inside `SparseFlashMla`:

```
error code = 341
"The address for VEC to access UB is out of bounds"
```

An ACL Graph replay does not re-enter the module, so the backend's own `attn_metadata is None` early return cannot intervene: by the time the graph runs, the inconsistent plan is already in the buffer the graph was captured
against.

#### Scope

The reset applies only to the backends that read `positions` for addressing rather than for RoPE:

```python
self.uses_positions_for_attention = self.use_sparse or model_uses_kpool_indexer(
    getattr(vllm_config, "model_config", None)
)
```

`enable_sfa()` returns False for kpool models, so `use_sparse` alone does not cover GLM-Next. Together the two predicates select exactly the families whose metadata builders reach `SparseMLAMetadataState.prepare()`, which calls `indexer.get_topk_lengths(positions)` - the LightningIndexer SFA family and the GLM-Next kpool indexer.

Dense and MLA backends derive their addressing from `seq_lens`, the block table and the slot mapping, all of which a dummy batch already sets consistently. They consume `positions` only to compute RoPE cos/sin for a forward whose output is discarded, so they are left untouched.

#### Why this level

Ranks that are idle for the whole request never hit this: their positions are still 0, so any count derived from them is 1 and agrees with `seq_lens == 1`. Only a rank that just finished serving carries a stale history into its first idle step. Resetting positions makes that rank's dummy step identical to theirs, which is what every backend already assumes a dummy batch looks like.

Fixing it inside one backend would leave the same trap for the next backend that reads positions, which is why it belongs in `_dummy_run` next to the existing `use_compress` reset rather than in the SFA metadata builder.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Ascend A5, GLM5Next w8a8, ACL Graph enabled.

- DP4 / TP2 / EP8, one request with `max_tokens=100` and nothing sent afterwards: without this patch the request returns HTTP 200 with correct output and the service then traps with `error code = 341` in `SparseFlashMla` while idle; with it the idle step is survived and the failure signature is gone.
- DP8 / TP1 / EP8 with MTP (5 speculative steps), `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: the server starts and gsm8k completes with accuracy in the expected range. This exercises the multi-token dummy batch (`uniform_decode_query_len == 6`), where every dummy token reports position 0 while its sequence length is 6 - an under-statement that keeps `ori_topk_length <= seqused_ori_kv`, which the operator contract requires.
- `--enforce-eager` does not reproduce it: `_should_build_dummy_attn_metadata()` is only true for `force_attention` or
  `CUDAGraphMode.FULL`, so the reset path is not reached and no metadata is built from the stale positions. Configurations without data parallelism do not reproduce it either, because they have no idle dummy batches.


- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Feature][Attention] Add fused sparse attention overlap decode support for Ascend SFA KV offload
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This commit adds fused sparse KV offload support for the decode path in `vllm-ascend`. It introduces a new fused operator, `npu_fused_sparse_attention_overlap`, and threads it through the PyTorch bindings, meta kernels, and the sparse KV offload attention implementation. The goal is to combine sparse attention, selection-state management, and KV offload planning into one path, reducing orchestration overhead and enabling better overlap. It also adds LRU/planning support for the fused workflow and a new opt-in config flag, `SparseKVOffloadConfig.use_fused_overlap`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, but it is opt-in. Users can now enable `use_fused_overlap` in `sparse_kv_offload_config` to route decode attention through the fused overlap implementation. By default the flag is `false`, so existing behavior stays unchanged unless a user turns it on. The visible effect is mainly performance and execution-path behavior, not a semantic API change.

### How was this patch tested?

The commit adds and updates broad unit coverage for the new path, including:

- sparse KV offload config parsing and validation
- memory-planning logic for host/device KV offload
- fused-overlap selection-state invalidation and cache reuse
- external-plan wiring for the fused decode path
- planner-side C++ helpers
- a performance comparison test harness for the fused path vs. the existing flow
