title: [BugFix][EPLB] Cover redundant physical experts in A2 ALLGATHER expert maps
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #14080.

With EPLB (`num_redundant_experts > 0`) on A2 (910B) + MRv1, the MoE **ALLGATHER** path crashes during decode CUDA-graph capture / first forward:

```
Index out of range in dimension 0: index value 263 exceeds bounds 256!
index_check.h:130 IndexCheckKernel<int>::ProcessScalar ... (idx < bound)
```

Two independent data points, same signature (bound == logical expert count, index == a redundant **physical** expert ID):

| Case | Logical experts | Redundant | Crash |
|---|---|---|---|
| #14080 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, EP=2) | 128 | 2 | `129 > 128` |
| User report (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8, EP=4/TP=4) | 256 | 16 | `263 > 256` |

**Root cause.** With EPLB, vLLM allocates *physical* experts (`num_experts = logical + redundant`, e.g. 256+16=272) and the router maps logical topk IDs to global physical IDs via `log2phy` (`routed_experts.py::_select_experts`). The A2 ALLGATHER dispatcher then builds its routing mask as:

```python
# token_dispatcher.py (pre-fix)
global_num_experts = len(expert_map) + global_redundant_expert_num   # 272 — correct
mask = expert_map[topk_ids] != -1                                    # OOB — expert_map has length 256
```

`layer.ascend_expert_map` was built in `init_eplb_config` over **logical** IDs only (`torch.full((n_experts,), -1)`), so physical IDs in `[256, 272)` trip the CANN `Index` op's embedded `IndexCheckKernel` (`idx < bound`), where the bound is the tensor's dim-0 (256). The crash fires from the first forward because the initial EPLB placement already puts redundant copies into the tail physical slots — no rebalance cycle is required.

The `expert_num` passed to `npu_moe_init_routing` was already the physical total; the mask map was the one overlooked site. (Forensic elimination of the other in-graph indexing ops — `npu_moe_init_routing`, `log2phy[topk_ids]`, MC2/MegaMoe paths — is in the full analysis below.)

**Why only A2.** A3 selects `FUSED_MC2` (MegaMoe consumes `topk_ids` + `moe_expert_num` = physical total, never indexes this map) and plain MC2 passes `moe_expert_num = len(expert_map) + redundant`. A2 has no `CANN_MEGAMOE` capability and the capacity/expert-density selector falls to ALLGATHER (the only consumer that indexes `expert_map` with physical topk IDs). A2 without EPLB has `log2phy is None` (IDs stay logical) — unaffected.

**The fix.** One invariant: `ascend_expert_map` is always a **global-physical → local-slot** map of length `num_experts` (logical + redundant). All consumers use the physical length directly or the new `phys_to_logical` bridge. `log2phy` output stays logical-length (router input unchanged).

Two adjacent latent bugs on the same path are fixed too — without them dynamic EPLB would die one cycle after the crash fix:

1. **Heat collection shape mismatch**: `npu_moe_init_routing` returns per-*global*-expert counts (`[num_experts]`) while `moe_load` is sized `num_local_experts` → `add_` shape error at the first EPLB cycle. Now gathered to per-slot counts via a new `local_phys_expert_ids` NPU buffer (size-guarded so MC2/FusedMC2 per-local counts pass through untouched).
2. **Stale layer maps after rebalance**: only the CPU bookkeeping copy was refreshed; `layer.ascend_expert_map` / `global_expert_map` kept pointing at pre-rebalance slots (silent misrouting). `update_ascend_eplb_maps` refreshes them, and the record file is written with logical IDs (it previously stored physical slot positions).

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `vllm_ascend/eplb/core/eplb_utils.py` | `init_eplb_config`: per-rank maps built full-length; returns `phys_to_logical` (flat placement, uniform for generated and file layouts); `generate_log2phy_map(..., phys_to_logical=None)` — physical-row grouping, output stays logical-length; `None` keeps the legacy behavior exactly. |
| `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py` | stores `phys_to_logical`; new `compute_local_phys_expert_ids`; `init_eplb` builds the NPU `local_phys_expert_ids` buffer; `update_ascend_eplb_maps` refreshes runtime maps; `forward_impl` gathers the global histogram into per-slot counts. |
| `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py` | AllGather: `global_num_experts = self.num_experts` (physical total from `moe_config`) — value-identical in every existing case, immune to the map-length invariant; MC2: `moe_expert_num = len(expert_map)` (physical length) — value-identical. |
| `vllm_ascend/eplb/core/eplb_worker.py`, `vllm_ascend/eplb/eplb_updator.py` | `phys_to_logical` published through `shared_dict` during `warm_up_eplb` and consumed in `pack_update_info`. |
| `vllm_ascend/eplb/adaptor/vllm_adaptor.py` | record file converts physical → logical IDs; `do_update_expert_map` refreshes layer runtime maps. |

The EPLB worker machinery (global2local/local2global, policies) is slot-value based and layout-agnostic — unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API/interface change. Behavior change is limited to A2 + MRv1 + EPLB with `num_redundant_experts > 0`, which previously crashed: dynamic and static EPLB now run. A3 (FUSED_MC2/MC2/ALLTOALL), A2 without EPLB, and MRv2 paths are value-identical pre/post patch.

### How was this patch tested?

- CPU UT (vllm 0.28.0, torch 2.13+cpu), `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on touched files:

  ```
  pytest tests/ut/ops/test_routed_experts.py tests/ut/eplb tests/ut/quantization tests/ut/_310p
  ```

  All pass; full-suite delta vs. the base commit is zero (the same 16 pre-existing CPU-environment failures occur on the base commit).
- New regression tests pinning the crash invariant:
  - `test_eplb_utils.py::test_allgather_mask_indexing_covers_physical_topk_ids` — `log2phy`-mapped IDs index the physical-length map in range, with the expected owned/not-owned mask (N=8, R=2, EP=2).
  - `test_eplb_utils.py::test_generate_log2phy_map_physical_layout_matches_logical_layout` / `..._with_tp_rotation` — physical-row mode ≡ legacy logical-row mode; output stays logical-length.
  - `test_routed_experts.py::test_compute_local_phys_expert_ids_orders_by_slot`, `test_update_ascend_eplb_maps_refreshes_runtime_maps`.
  - `test_vllm_adaptor.py::test_do_update_expert_map_refreshes_layer_runtime_maps`, `test_export_tensor_to_file_writes_logical_expert_ids`.
- A standalone CPU script verified `init_eplb_config` for the dynamic, static-file, and no-EPLB layouts against hand-computed ground truths, plus the `do_update_expert_map`/export flows.
- NPU e2e not run locally; **please re-enable `test_moe_tp_ep_eplb_full_decode_only` (Qwen3-30B-A3B, EP=2, `num_redundant_experts=2`, A2) in the CI flow** — it is the #14080 repro and the direct acceptance gate for this patch (graph capture completes, traffic serves, EPLB cycles run without `IndexCheck` / shape errors after the first rebalance). A3 FUSED_MC2 regression is covered by the existing eplb e2e set.

Full root-cause analysis (forensic elimination, data-flow diagram, per-path equivalence argument) is available on request — the branch contains a single commit.

- vllm-ascend base: `ab730ad69` (main @ PR creation)

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Performance][GLM-5.3-Flash] Use device-specific KV cache scatter
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM-5.3-Flash currently writes its packed main KV cache with native `scatter_nd_update_`. Route these writes through `DeviceOperator.scatter_kv_cache`: use `_sk` on A2/A3, single-cache `scatter_pa_cache` on A5, and retain the native writer on 310P.

Skip negative padding slots in both `_sk` HP copy paths so fixed-shape graph replay cannot write before the cache. The device interface accepts prepared full-width rows and does not require `rope_dim=0`. A5 preserves the original cache storage and makes only the input views contiguous.

Refs #15665

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The KV write operator changes automatically with the device adaptor; no new configuration is required. Expected cache contents and model outputs are unchanged. End-to-end performance gains have not been measured.

### How was this patch tested?

- **62 unit tests passed:** `tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py` and `tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_nope_forward.py`.
- **A3 NPU:** 62 `_sk` operator cases passed, including padding regressions. Native and patched `_sk` each passed a 68-case comparison matrix.
- **A3 integration:** 16 real SFA `exec_kv` cases passed. The final device interface passed 32 NPU cases covering 512/576 feature widths, FP16/BF16, int32/int64 slots, block sizes 128/640, eager execution and graph replay, padding and cache guard pages.
- **A5:** adapter contract tests passed. The 32 A5-only NPU cases collect and skip correctly on A3; A5 hardware validation is outstanding.
- Ran `bash format.sh ci`. All applicable Windows checks passed; the three shell hooks that could not run there were executed successfully against the same changes in Linux, including gitleaks on the staged diff.
- Independent code review completed. GLM-5.2 full-model regression is in progress and is not included in the passing results above.

title: [Performance][Attention] Keep eager DSA-CP prefill token-sharded
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Eligible DSA-CP MoE layers gather token-sharded hidden states that attention immediately shards again. After full O-proj, they materialize a replicated output and reduce-scatter it even though each rank has already computed its complete local token output.

Keep hidden states and residuals token-sharded through eager attention, full O-proj, normalization and sequence-parallel MoE. Track the layout explicitly across dense/MoE boundaries and auxiliary-state capture, including N < TP and zero padding. Preserve the public SFA forward signature and enter the new layout through a dedicated wrapper.

The path requires the native DSA-CP backend, eager execution, full O-proj with `reduce_results=False`, and supported MoE/model layouts. DecodeOnly, SpecDecoding, MTP, DCP, compiled/captured execution and unsupported layouts keep the existing route. This PR does not contain cache-gather fusion or block cache writes and can be reviewed against main independently.

### Data flow: before and after

**Before:** MoE token shard -> hidden-state AllGather -> attention slices the same local shard -> local attention and full O-proj -> replicated output buffer -> reduce-scatter -> token-sharded MoE.

**After:** MoE token shard -> local attention and full O-proj -> local output and residual -> token-sharded MoE. Gather only where an existing model boundary or auxiliary-state consumer needs replicated states.

### Scope and related PRs

This PR contains only token-sharded eager prefill and targets main independently.

- Cache-gather fusion and large block cache writes are combined in #16915 as two commits.
- This token-sharded prefill change remains separate in #16974 and is not included in #16915.
- The former standalone cache-write PR #16975 is superseded by #16915.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No new configuration. Only eligible eager DSA-CP prefill backbone layers use the new layout; model outputs and existing unsupported-path contracts are preserved.

### How was this patch tested?

- Rebased independently onto vllm-ascend main `5c80630f28f8529aa82716e58b981a78819ec429`; this PR contains only its own optimization and tests.
- Applying all three split patches reconstructs the original combined patch's rebased production code exactly. The sequence-parallel NPU projection check was moved into its own test file with an identical test-function AST.
- CPU validation uses the repository's verified vLLM source `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c` in an isolated CPU-only container. Focused regression: **1060 passed, 16 skipped**. Full CPU run: **5342 passed, 67 skipped**, plus two startup-environment failures. **Both failed tests passed on rerun** after supplying generated version/device metadata, removing the version override, and exposing only the CPU HAL stub library to the test process. No tracked code changed for this environment repair. Current-head GitHub **static/mypy, CPU unit tests and DCO passed**. The merge gate requires a maintainer to add exactly one of `ready-precise`, `ready-all` or `main2main` to trigger the required selected/full hardware tests; the hardware jobs were skipped in this run. The source-archive CPU build uses `0.0.0+git.84030bbe3d74` as local version metadata for the verified main commit; it is not a released package version.
- Changed Python files pass Ruff, formatting, spelling, import, package, context-manager, function-length, symbolic-meta and logger checks; staged secret scan and `git diff --check` pass. Full Linux CI status is reported by this PR's checks.
- The original combined patch passed real A3 operator tests, including the relevant cases below. Those runs predate this split and rebase. No new NPU run was started because the shared-machine experiment is paused; new NPU CI remains pending.
- TP=2/8 full O-proj against real HCCL gather/reduce-scatter, including N < TP, partial shards and 8192 tokens. The projection test is now a separate NPU file. CPU tests cover unsupported-path guards, residual ownership, padding and auxiliary hidden states.

### Historical performance evidence

Historical cache fusion -> cache fusion plus token sharding: **1090.9025 -> 1114.2872 output token/s (+2.14%)**; mean TTFT **25817.1 -> 20631.0 ms**. In matched profiles, AICPU AllGather counts fall from 804 to 582 and reduce-scatter counts from 312 to 87.

**The +2.14% is an incremental measurement on top of cache fusion, not a standalone measurement of this main-based PR.** Remaining boundary/auxiliary gathers are expected.

The historical measurements used GLM-5.1 W8A8C8 with MTP on 64 A3 NPUs, P=DP4 x TP8 with DSA-CP and D=DP8 x TP4 without DSA-CP, P/D token budgets 8192/164, 128K inputs, 1024 outputs, request rate 1.52 and concurrency 64. Each run completed 256/256 requests with 33,699,475 input tokens and 262,144 output tokens. Profiling was collected separately from timing. The checkpoint uses BF16 indexer caches despite main-cache C8.

These numbers are historical measurements before the rebase onto current main; the split branches have not been benchmarked again. They are single staged runs, not a repeatability estimate for this individual PR. The original three-optimization bundle's repeated +13.82% result is not attributed to any individual PR. MTP acceptance had already recovered in the historical main baseline before these optimizations.

title: [Performance] Fuse DSA-CP cache gathers and optimize main C8 cache writes
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Native DSA-CP gathers main KV and indexer K/scale separately and uses generic scatter for main C8 KV writes. This PR contains exactly two commits:

1. **Fuse main and indexer cache gathers.** Pack per-token raw bytes into one collective, wait before unpacking, preserve dtype/scale representation, and keep indexer scoring weights local. Each cache retains its own slots and ownership. MTP `compute_topk=False` still writes the indexer cache.
2. **Optimize main C8 KV writes using the existing reshape setting.** Add `_use_c8_reshape_optim()` to the DSA-CP implementation, following the existing indexer method: main C8 must be enabled, the batch must be eligible, the existing P-only node role must match, and the existing user toggle `c8_enable_reshape_optim` must be true. Eligible main writes use existing SK on A2/A3 or PA on A5; otherwise the original scatter remains. Commit 2 makes no changes to indexer cache writes or indexer metadata.

The main-cache gate reuses the existing user toggle `c8_enable_reshape_optim` and the already initialized `is_kv_producer`/`is_kv_consumer` roles. It deliberately does not reuse the LI-specific derived `c8_reshape_optim_enabled`: main INT8 KV can coexist with a BF16 indexer. The indexer keeps its original LI C8 gate. No new user configuration is added. Disabling `c8_enable_reshape_optim` also disables the new main write path. Indexer K/scale retain their pre-existing `store_kv_block`/scatter selection. Shared operator helpers live in `attention/utils.py`; no additional module or native kernel is added.

Optimization 2 (token-sharded eager prefill) remains separate in #16974 and is not included. #16975 is superseded and remains closed.

### Data flow: before and after

**Before:** main KV -> main AllGather -> main scatter; indexer K/scale -> separate AllGathers -> existing C8 block write or scatter.

**After:** main KV + indexer K/scale -> pack bytes -> shared AllGather -> wait -> unpack -> main KV uses the existing reshape gate and safe-layout checks to select SK/PA or scatter; indexer K/scale use their unchanged block-write/scatter path. No new block-group metadata is constructed.

### Scope and layout contracts

- The new main-cache path is limited to ordinary, pure DSA-CP prefill batches with at least2048 actual tokens and the existing P-node C8 reshape gate enabled. Draft, graph capture, mixed/decode and PCP/DCP batches keep the original write path. Graph-enabled deployments can optimize ordinary prefill without requiring `enforce_eager=True`.
- Eligible prefill writes address distinct allocated slots. Trailing TP padding is removed using main KV's `num_actual_tokens`; no assumption is made that SK or PA ignores negative slots. Builders disable the new path for masked draft/parallel/capture layouts. Checks add no device-to-host slot synchronization.
- SK supports gaps between rows and a storage offset, with contiguous elements within each row. Read-only noncontiguous inputs use its adapter. PA requires a contiguous destination; only read-only inputs may be copied. Unsupported layouts/dtypes or unavailable operators fall back, and destination cache storage is never replaced.
- A5 PA has documented-ABI and CPU-mock coverage only, not real A5 kernel validation. Existing indexer behavior is unchanged on every platform.

### Validation

- Rebased onto main `c173a64a44dec4ba97aaba6277b1dfc1562eda19` at the user's request. Exactly two commits: `84021c009384566aa2a49bced3a6047417285130` and `85cc0bc7339ad23cd81da463aa77a372150f7e3d`. The range-diff preserves the optimization changes; commit 2 only picked up changed import context. Pinned vLLM remains `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`.
- **481 CPU tests passed on this exact head**, zero failures/errors/skips. Coverage includes main C8 with the LI-derived flag disabled, node roles, settings, per-layer/batch gating, SFA-CP, indexer, layout/fallback/padding, MLA, hardware profiles, KVPoolScheduler and Mooncake hybrid. Verified 4143 candidate source files and 1281 matching native artifacts; native/build sources are unchanged across this rebase. Ruff and changed-file format checks passed.
- **30 real A3 tests passed on this exact rebased head**, zero failures/errors/skips, in clean run `fusion_scatter-20260920T162750Z`. Covers cache backing storage, row gaps/offsets, noncontiguous sources, padding, TP2/TP8 gather-to-cache and MTP skipped-top-k/eager/graph. Main C8 writes are also exercised with the LI-derived flag false. Container exited0 without guard interruption; raw JUnit/logs and source/runtime hashes are retained under `pr16915-scatter-85cc0bc7339a-20260920T162155Z`. Earlier C8-specific probes remain identified by their earlier heads.
- **Explicit SFA C8 + LI C8 A3 probe passed on this head** (`c8-probe-20260920T163611Z`). P TP8/D TP4 configuration parsing selects INT8 caches and the69 exported LI-quantized layers; actual dynamic quantization, StoreKVBlock/cache reference checks, quantized LI, main SK and quantized SFA CPU-reference checks passed. Uses the isolated exporter-verified metadata overlay described below. No full model weights were loaded by this probe.
- Full-model controls and AISBench performance remain pending. Operator results do not establish throughput, acceptance-rate improvement or merge readiness.

### Main and C8 compatibility

Main now includes the scheduler stale-field fix [#17023](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/17023); the earlier `mamba_group_ids` CI failure is historical, not a current-head result. New-head GitHub checks must run independently.

The C8 user-switch restoration [#16952](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/16952) was already in the previous base. This rebase still does not add support for the model's per-layer `QK_INT8_DYNAMIC` metadata marker. Explicit C8 validation therefore uses a separately identified, read-only metadata overlay and explicit INT8 main/indexer cache dtypes; it does not modify shared weights or this PR's source. The exporter and GLM-5 adapter confirm that the 69 marked layers use per-token INT8 Q/K. Only those markers are normalized to the parser's supported `INT8_DYNAMIC` spelling; the 10 excluded layers remain excluded. The current-head runtime probe passed as recorded above; full-model validation and AISBench performance remain pending. Historical BF16-indexer performance is not an effective-LI-C8 result.

### Why the existing LI C8 optimization does not cover this workload

The archived pre-cache-optimization p2 profile contains INT8 main-cache writes (8192x656) and BF16 indexer writes (8192x128); its 32 workers have zero StoreKVBlock invocations. Its launch YAML did request LI C8. A read-only audit of the configured GLM-5.1 model's quantization description found 69 indexer `QK_INT8_DYNAMIC` entries and 79 `wq_b.weight=W8A8` entries. Both the historical p2 source and this fixed base accept only `INT8_DYNAMIC`/`W8A8_MXFP8` in their LI C8 layer filter, so none of those entries qualify. This metadata mismatch explains a per-layer BF16 path despite the requested global switch and matches the profile; it is not evidence that LI C8 was intentionally disabled. This PR does not change the quantization parser or metadata. The explicit-C8 benchmark profile described above separately verifies exporter compatibility and records its metadata hashes. The existing LI C8-only write path therefore did not optimize those BF16 indexer writes, and never handled the main KV call site. This does not imply the existing write operator is broken for supported LI C8 configurations. The historical p2/p3 block-copy measurements also included BF16 indexer writes; those gains are not transferable to this narrower main-only revision. The first commit's AllGather fusion remains independent of the write-kernel gate.

### Historical performance (different implementation and base)

Old base `5c80630` / combined block-copy head `4a03a5b`: baseline 1174.7210 output token/s; combination 1175.2988 and 1167.4850 output token/s, each 256/256 successful requests. Both combination samples missed the unchanged 1227.648684 token/s AISBench threshold. Baseline/candidate output differences and baseline repeated-input variation remain under investigation. These measurements do not establish performance for the new SK/PA implementation.

The pending matched benchmark keeps 256 requests, 128K input, 1024 output, rate 1.52, concurrency 64, the same dataset/warmup and fresh model/compiler/KV caches. Full AISBench logs and source/runtime identities are retained.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][Platform] Enable A5 custom ops through the shared loader
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

A5 currently lacks `RUNTIME_CUSTOM_OPS`, so `enable_custom_op()` returns `False` before attempting to load an installed custom extension. Add this capability to let A5 use the existing shared initialization path.

Remove A5's `BGMV_SGMV_META_REGISTRATION` capability at the same time: the standard ascend950 build excludes `VLLM_ENABLE_ATB_AND_DIRECT_KERNELS` and therefore does not provide the `bgmv_expand` / `sgmv_expand` schemas. Attempting their Python Meta registration would otherwise block shared initialization.

Update the existing capability-matrix test and remove the obsolete A5-disable comment. This PR is limited to the shared enable configuration; operator call sites and kernels are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. On A5, `enable_custom_op()` can now return `True` after successful initialization, allowing existing callers guarded by it to use custom ops. The existing batch-invariant guard, ImportError handling, and cached result remain unchanged. A2/A3/310P capability configurations are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

In an Ascend A5 environment, using this commit's Python source:

- `python -m pytest --noconftest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py -q`: **12 passed**.
- Three isolated-process loader checks: successful initialization returns `True`; batch-invariant mode returns `False`; a simulated missing-extension ImportError returns `False`. Repeated calls preserve each cached result.
- The successful path imports the real A5 extension and Python Meta registrations without BGMV/SGMV schemas, then executes AddRmsNormBias with Meta tensors. These checks reused an existing A5 compiled artifact, did not rebuild kernels, and confirmed the NPU runtime remained uninitialized.
- All 18 repository pre-commit hooks passed across all files, using cached system Node/Go toolchains for their environments.

No device-kernel execution or end-to-end model validation was performed for this configuration-only change.

title: [Performance][Attention] Optimize long cached prefill with BNSD on A2
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds an experimental, opt-in A2 attention path for long cached-prefill queries.

The core contribution is a selective mixed-layout strategy:

- keep short decode requests in compact TND;
- route one eligible long cached-prefill query through BNSD;
- retain the native paged NHD KV cache instead of converting it to HND; and
- fall back to the existing TND implementation for unsupported hardware, shapes, dtypes, or batch composition.

The path is guarded by `enable_prefill_bnsd` and is disabled by default. It currently requires Atlas A2, BF16, 256-dimensional heads, a 128-token paged-KV block size, and exactly one cached/chunked prefill query of at least 4096 tokens in the scheduler step. PCP, sliding-window attention, sinks, and non-decoder attention retain the existing path.

#### Reference measurements

The measurements below were collected with Qwen3.8-27B on Atlas A2 using tensor parallel size 2 and an experimental prototype based on vLLM Ascend commit `f4a08bddd` and CANN 9.0.1. The profiled attention shape had 12 query heads, 2 KV heads, and a head dimension of 256. 

Single-operator benchmark, approximately 7680 query tokens attending to a 100000-token paged KV cache:

| Path | Median latency | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TND query + NHD paged KV | 62.7079 ms | baseline |
| BNSD query + NHD paged KV | 54.4916 ms | -13.10% |

Mixed batch with query lengths `[7680, 4, 4, 4]`, including query reorder and output placement:

| Path | Median latency | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mixed TND | 66.1986 ms | baseline |
| Long prefill BNSD + short decode TND | 55.4271 ms | -16.27% |

The long-prefill output had maximum absolute error `1.2207e-4` and relative L2 error `5.8668e-4`; the short decode slices matched exactly in the prototype test.

Service A/B with 40 requests at concurrency 8, 100000 input tokens per request (80000 shared-prefix tokens + 20000 unique tokens), and 16 output tokens:

| Metric | Existing path | BNSD prefill | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean queue time | 18.573 s | 18.132 s | -2.37% |
| Mean prefill time | 14.703 s | 14.446 s | -1.75% |
| Mean TTFT | 36.372 s | 35.588 s | -2.16% |
| Mean E2E latency | 58.024 s | 56.967 s | -1.82% |

Both service runs had identical prefix-cache counters and zero preemptions.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It adds the optional `enable_prefill_bnsd` field to `--additional-config`:

```bash
--additional-config '{"enable_prefill_bnsd":true}'
```

The option is disabled by default and unsupported cases automatically use the existing TND path.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added unit coverage for configuration parsing and default behavior.
- Added hardware-profile coverage confirming that the capability is A2-only.
- Added attention-path coverage confirming that decode remains TND, the eligible long prefill uses BNSD, output slices are restored correctly, and multiple prefills fall back.
- Ran Ruff 0.14.0 check/format on all changed Python files.
- Ran Python `compileall` on the changed implementation and tests.
- Ran `git diff --check`.
- Ran the Atlas A2 prototype operator, mixed-batch correctness, and service A/B measurements documented above.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode]  Update MRV2 eager draft attention metadata before decode
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Ascend V2 autoregressive speculator rebuilds draft attention metadata for every draft step in eager mode. Previously, the Ascend-specific CPU-side sequence lengths were updated only after the draft forward. That update was too late for the current FIA call and was then discarded when the next draft step rebuilt its metadata. As a result, later Eagle3 draft positions used stale sequence-length metadata and had lower acceptance rates.

This PR updates the freshly built attention metadata inside `_build_draft_attn_metadata`, before it is consumed by the upcoming draft decode. It also adds a regression test that verifies the current draft step and request count are applied before the builder returns.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It improves speculative-decoding acceptance and throughput for the V2 model runner when using Ascend eager autoregressive draft decoding. There is no API or configuration change.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit test:

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q tests/ut/spec_decode/test_autoregressive_draft_metadata.py
```

Result: `2 passed`. `python -m py_compile` and `git diff --check` also passed for the changed files.

End-to-end benchmark used Qwen3-32B with its Eagle3 speculator, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, V2 model runner, `--enforce-eager`, full GSM8K (1,319 samples), and concurrency 64. All sampling and server settings were kept identical.

| Run | Accuracy | Overall acceptance | Position 1 / 2 / 3 | API inference time | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V1 baseline | 95.8302% | 66.6667% | 82.9463% / 66.7158% / 50.3380% | 176.62 s | 1703.4 token/s |
| V2 before | 95.5269% | 65.5024% | 83.0093% / 65.7108% / 47.7872% | 144.62 s | 2082.0 token/s |
| V2 after | 95.5269% | 66.6017% | 82.8641% / 66.7343% / 50.2068% | 137.61 s | 2187.5 token/s |

The V2 acceptance rate improved by 1.0993 percentage points and is now within 0.0650 percentage points of V1. The largest recovery is at the third draft position (+2.4196 percentage points versus the previous V2 run). The post-fix counters were 200,984 accepted tokens out of 301,770 draft tokens.

title: [Feature][Kernel] Extend split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope with value normalization for Gemma4
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Gemma4 runs its pre-attention chain, qkv split, per-head q/k RMSNorm, RoPE, and a weight-less per-head **v** RMSNorm, as separate ops on Ascend, so it cannot use the existing fused `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` kernel, which copies V straight out of the fused QKV tensor. The existing `qknorm_rope_fusion_pass` cannot cover it either: it has no notion of the V norm, and Gemma4 alternates sliding and full attention layers with different `head_dim`, kv head counts and RoPE type, while `torch.compile` matches a single pattern against every attention layer. This PR adds a `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope_vnorm` Triton kernel and wires Gemma4 to it. **Kernel.** A variant of `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` that normalizes V instead of copying it. Because V now needs the same float32 reduction scratch as Q and K, the separate wide-tile V loop that the base kernel uses for the plain copy no longer pays for itself, so V is folded into the q/k loop: - one `tl.load` covers the whole fused row (`total_hidden_size`) instead of two separate column segments; - one RMSNorm reduction covers every q, k **and** v head of the tile, reshaped to `(tile * (q_head_num + 2*kv_head_num), HEAD_DIM)`; - Q, K and V are then cut out with three `extract_slice` calls at head offsets `0`, `q_head_num` and `q_head_num + kv_head_num`. Q and K apply their weights and RoPE; V has neither, so it is a cast and a store that reuses the K output index and mask. This is valid because Gemma4's `v_norm` is the same per-head RMSNorm with the same `eps` and no learnable scale, the weight application is what moves after the shared reduction. The kernel keeps everything else from `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope`: the 1-D grid over vector cores, the batched UB tiling, the per-tile cos/sin gather shared by all heads, and partial-RoPE support. The UB tiling factor grows by `4 * kv_hidden_size` to account for the V columns now living in the tile. Full attention layers use proportional RoPE, which `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding` implements by zero-padding `inv_freq` and passing `rotary_dim=head_size` to the base class, so its cos/sin cache is an ordinary full-width cache and the kernel needs no layer-type knowledge. `Gemma4Attention.__init__` is patched as well to resolve the fusion decision at build time and log it. Model construction never runs inside a compiled region, so this keeps the branch out of the traced graph and keeps the outcome observable in every compilation mode, unlike a check inside `forward`, which `torch.compile` evaluates once at trace time and an ACL graph then replays without Python. Layers fall back to the upstream unfused chain, with the reason logged, when: the layer is KV-shared; `v_norm` carries a learnable scale; any q/k/v norm carries a bias; the three norms use different epsilons; weights or the cos/sin cache are not bfloat16; the rotary embedding is not neox-style; or one token's tile exceeds the vector core unified buffer (which excludes full attention layers below tensor parallel size 4). ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No API or interface change. Gemma4 on Ascend picks up the fused pre-attention path automatically; every layer that does not qualify keeps the existing behavior and logs why. ### How was this patch tested? Tested on 910B1, TP=4, dtype bfloat16 with gemma4-31b-it. **Performance** **Accuracy** | Benchmark | Unfused (baseline) | Fused (this PR) | |-----------|-------------------:|----------------:| | HumanEval | 96.74 | 96.74 | | GPQA | 76.09 | 76.28 | Averaged over 3 runs. **Correctness** pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][Spec Decode] Correct rejected token seq_lens in MRV1
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

ModelRunner V1 does not subtract rejected target tokens from the device-side `seq_lens` before building the later one-token draft decode steps. SFA and DSA consume this tensor as the exact KV sequence length. Consequently, their later draft Attention steps use an overestimated sequence length that still includes rejected token positions.

The issue was observed by printing the rejected-token count and the device-side sequence lengths used by three consecutive draft steps:

```text
[V1_DEVICE_SEQ_LENS] rejected=[3] steps=[[47], [48], [49]]
[V1_DEVICE_SEQ_LENS] rejected=[2] steps=[[56], [57], [58]]
[V1_DEVICE_SEQ_LENS] rejected=[3] steps=[[98], [99], [100]]
```

The sequence lengths advance by one for each draft step, but their baseline is not reduced by the corresponding rejected-token count. Therefore, the device-side `seq_lens` is overestimated by 3, 2, and 3 tokens in these examples. SFA-style model backends pass this incorrect value to both the sparse Indexer and the Attention kernel as the exact KV sequence length. As a result, both the Indexer and Attention execute with an overestimated KV length that includes the rejected token positions.

This PR preserves the unadjusted sequence lengths used by merged step 0, then copies them to an independent NPU buffer and subtracts rejected tokens for the remaining one-token draft decode steps. The CPU-side sequence lengths remain an optimistic upper bound to avoid an NPU-to-CPU synchronization.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

N/A

title: [Feature][EC Connector] Support ECMooncakeConnector with Ascend Direct
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it

Refs #15898.

This PR adds Ascend support for the upstream `ECMooncakeConnector` introduced by vllm-project/vllm#41567, enabling multimodal encoder outputs to be transferred from an Encoder instance to a PD instance through Mooncake Ascend Direct.

#### Architecture

The implementation keeps the common ECMooncake control plane in upstream vLLM, including the scheduler, consumer reservations, producer push management, and transfer metadata. `AscendECMooncakeConnector` is registered under the standard `ECMooncakeConnector` name and selects an Ascend worker while reusing the upstream scheduler.

```text
    Router / proxy                Encoder / producer                    PD / consumer
           |                               |                                  |
           |--------image request--------->|                                  |
           |<-------image metadata---------|                                  |
           |----------------------metadata-only decode----------------------->|
           |                               |-------reserve destination------->|
           |                               |<-------session + address---------|
           |                               |======Mooncake batch write=======>|
                                                                              |
                                                                              v
                                                                       PD model runner
```

The Ascend worker supplies the NPU-specific data path:

- Allocates and registers 2 MiB-aligned NPU memory for the producer staging pool and consumer pool.
- Tries the producer staging pool first. When an encoder output cannot fit there, it registers the source memory for direct transfer and uses a shared bounce arena for any bytes that cannot be transferred directly.
- Packs source fragments into transfer waves and submits batched Mooncake writes. Registrations, bounce leases, and source tensors remain valid until their transfers finish, including failure and shutdown paths.
- Initializes the Ascend Mooncake TransferEngine, validates the `ascend` protocol and NPU buffer device, and integrates worker-service startup and shutdown with the Ascend worker lifecycle.

```text
Producer NPU allocation (registered once)
+----------------------+-----------+---------------------+
| Staging pool         | alignment | shared bounce arena |
|                      | padding   |                     |
+----------------------+-----------+---------------------+

NORMAL: the output batch fits in staging
  encoder output -> copy into staging -> Mooncake write -> PD EC pool

FALLBACK: the output batch does not fit in staging
                         encoder output
                                |
                  +-------------+-------------+
                  |                           |
           prefix (if any)           remainder (if any)
                  |                           |
        copy to bounce arena    register original NPU storage
                  |                           |
                  +-------------+-------------+
                                |
                                v
                     batched Mooncake write
                                |
                                v
                   PD EC pool (original order)
```

The bounce arena is a reusable part of the producer's registered allocation. In the fallback path, it carries only a source prefix that cannot be covered by a valid aligned registration; the remaining bytes transfer directly from the original NPU storage. Both fragments join the same batched write.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Encoder and PD instances can select `ECMooncakeConnector` with an NPU EC buffer and the Ascend Mooncake protocol. For example, the measured EPD configuration used the following `--ec-transfer-config` values:

Encoder (`ec_producer`):

```bash
--ec-transfer-config \
'{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_producer","ec_buffer_size":3221225472,"ec_buffer_device":"npu","ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"ascend"}}'
```

The producer can also set `ascend_mooncake_bounce_arena_size` in `ec_connector_extra_config` to size the shared bounce arena in bytes. It is additional registered NPU memory, separate from the `ec_buffer_size` staging pool. For example, to request a 64 MiB arena, set the producer's `ec_connector_extra_config` to:

```json
{"mooncake_protocol":"ascend","ascend_mooncake_bounce_arena_size":67108864}
```

PD (`ec_consumer`; use a distinct `ec_port` for each PD instance):

```bash
--ec-transfer-config \
'{"ec_connector":"ECMooncakeConnector","ec_role":"ec_consumer","ec_ip":"127.0.0.1","ec_port":8301,"ec_buffer_size":3221225472,"ec_buffer_device":"npu","ec_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"ascend"}}'
```

The E2E and benchmark runs used Model Runner V2.
### How was this patch tested?

#### Model Runner V2 E2E validation

On Ascend hardware, the E+PD E2E test passed both cases: a normal staging transfer and a forced fallback transfer with a one-byte staging pool. The latter repeats requests to exercise direct registration, bounce-buffer transfer, and resource reuse. The test checks single-image and two-image responses against a single-server baseline.

#### Multi-image performance comparison

The benchmark used two 910C with the model `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8`. The three deployments processed the same 750 MMIU multi-image requests in the same order. Each had separate warm-up requests, eight client processes, concurrency 96, identical generation settings, and prefix caching disabled. Graph execution was enabled. The ECMooncake runs used 3 GiB producer and consumer EC pools. All three runs completed 750/750 measured requests with HTTP 200 and zero client failures.

| Metric | 1E3PD, ECMooncake | 2E2PD, ECMooncake | DP4EP4 baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

title: [Performance][Attention] Reuse device cache-store dispatch for SFA C8
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Route both native and DSA-CP main SFA C8 cache writes through `DeviceOperator.try_scatter_cache`, following MiniMax's actual-token-prefix calling pattern. The device adaptor selects the existing SK path on A2/A3 and PA path on A5. It also executes `torch_npu.npu_scatter_nd_update_` itself when the fast path is unavailable or does not support the input, so the SFA caller has one call and no separate fallback branch.

The public method performs cache writes in place and returns `None`. `_scatter_cache` is called in a separate statement, and its internal result controls whether generic fallback is needed. Both paths preserve the original destination storage and actual-token slicing. Native preprocessing keeps the packed NoPE/RoPE/scale byte order and supplies its own SFA slot mapping; padding beyond num_actual_tokens is excluded. Operator exceptions propagate without retrying a possibly partial write. Layouts the original generic operator cannot handle remain unsupported; no contiguous destination copy is introduced.

Remove `prefill_cache_write_enabled`, its 2048-token threshold, the `fast_cache_store` metadata field/gate, and capture-builder overrides that only disabled that gate. Dispatch no longer depends on prefill state or node role. Native operator implementations, MiniMax callers, LI C8, and compressed-cache callers are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

SFA C8 batches attempt the existing device-specific cache store regardless of prefill/decode state or batch size. There is no new configuration setting.

**Known unresolved boundary:** actual-token slicing excludes tail padding but does not filter negative slots inside the active prefix. No negative-slot or native-kernel fix is included. An earlier instrumented model run observed eight active `-1` slots during non-capture speculative prewarm and stopped before invoking SK. Safety for that case or model graph metadata containing active negative slots is not established by this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

Current commit: `1279724cf2d5a8a7a7d8294324b6411b49a44bf8`.

- **311 unit tests passed** with CPU-only mocks (`TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0`): `tests/ut/attention/test_cache_store.py`, `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`, `tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_cp.py`, `tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py`, and `tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py`. Coverage checks the `None` return contract for fast and generic paths, platform dispatch, exactly one generic fallback, actual-token slicing, destination storage, shape guards, and exception propagation without a second write.
- Ruff lint, Ruff format, and `git diff --check` passed. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but could not run because local `pre-commit` is not installed.
- **28/28 A3 NPU tests passed** on Ascend910_9362 with unchanged native binaries: 24 fast-path cases compare the complete backing storage across dtypes, widths, row strides, offsets, and token counts; one case checks supported generic float32 fallback including negative slots; one compares unsupported inner-stride behavior with the original generic operator; two exercise native SFA C8 packing and actual-token writes with 3/2049 tokens and negative padding outside the active prefix. The runtime verified 4142 source files and 1281 native manifest entries. Test source hashes match the committed production code. The test container exited 0 and its NPU processes/device locks were released.
- A2/A5 hardware and full-model throughput have not been validated for this head. Four-machine attempt `opt3-20260922T084208Z` stopped during instrumented model prewarm before any benchmark request: all 64 workers passed the SFA/LI C8 runtime audit, but all 32 decode workers reached the native main-KV store with 128 active negative slots (`int8 [128,656]`, not capturing). The validation guard stopped execution before invoking SK. This is not an observed native-kernel crash or a measured throughput regression. No benchmark client was created and no throughput value was obtained, so the unchanged 1265.6172 × 0.97 = 1227.648684 output tokens/s target remains unverified. All four task-owned containers exited and their NPU processes/locks were released; automatic retries are paused pending resolution of the warmup boundary. Negative-slot success on the generic fallback does not establish negative-slot support in SK or PA.

Earlier cache-write microbenchmark results were collected for the call layout at `4af67117a`, before moving fallback into the adaptor: 24/24 A3 cases matched reference bytes, with unchanged native binaries, int8 width 656, continuous and row-stride-672 layouts, valid unique active slots, and negative padding outside the actual-token prefix. Continuous-layout eager medians in microseconds were 22.98 → 39.47 for 8-token writes, 89.51 → 40.59 for 512-token writes previously using generic scatter, 111.85 → 40.75 for 4096-token writes previously using generic scatter, and 40.97 → 40.87 for 8192-token pure prefill where both versions used SK (baseline `70aea64c`). These are historical microbenchmarks, not a timing rerun of the current head: small eager batches regressed, larger generic-scatter writes improved, and large pure-prefill writes were similar. They do not exercise a real mixed scheduler or establish the four-machine target of 1227.648684 output tokens/s.

### Follow-up experiment: metadata-only padding mapping (not included in this PR)

An independent variant based on `1279724cf2d5a8a7a7d8294324b6411b49a44bf8` maps SFA C8 `-1` slots to reserved slot 0 in `build`/`build_for_drafting`, using stable private buffers; the write sites only consume this metadata. Native operators and shared/indexer metadata are unchanged. This experiment has not been committed or pushed to this PR.

- A3 boundary/graph tests: 24/24 passed across native/DSA-CP callers, int32/int64 slots, contiguous/stride-672 caches, and capture followed by changed slots/keys. Slot 0 payload is intentionally excluded, while other cache bytes, row padding and guard rows are checked.
- Initial long/short phase: 16/16 responses correct, maximum actual prompt length 14333 tokens. The extra sustained mixed wave hit `pin_memory()` host-allocation OOM (`aclrtMallocHostWithCfg 207001`), leaving 4 failed request attempts. Full mixed stress validation and a fresh reference-output comparison remain incomplete.
- Four-machine attempt `opt3-20260922T093848Z`: interrupted by an external NPU workload during model startup. No benchmark client or warmup/measured requests were started. Output throughput is unavailable, and the original **1227.648684 output tokens/s** target remains unverified. All task-owned model containers, NPU processes and device locks were released; no external task was stopped.

- Four-machine retry `opt3-20260922T101852Z`: an external Python process (PID 1526822) in the same `/cls` container on node 157 triggered the foreign-workload guard during startup. No benchmark client or requests started; output throughput and the 1227.648684 tokens/s target remain unverified. All four task-owned containers exited and their NPU processes, clients and locks were released. This is an interrupted attempt, not a measured throughput regression.

These experimental checks do not replace the tests of the actual PR head or establish A2/A5 correctness.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [BugFix][KV Transfer] Register class-name aliases for KV connectors
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`MultiConnector` keys per-request transfer stats by `__class__.__name__`
(`multi_connector.py::get_kv_connector_stats`) and, on the logger side, resolves
those keys back through `KVConnectorFactory.get_connector_class_by_name`. The
factory registry is indexed by the `kv_connector` config name, so any connector
registered under a config name that differs from its class name fails the stats
reconstruction lookup with:

```
ValueError: Connector 'AscendOffloadingConnector' is not registered.
```

That exception is raised in `AsyncLLM.output_handler`, which propagates it and
tears down EngineCore (in-flight requests then fail with 500).

This PR registers the class names as additional aliases for the two KV
connectors that emit stats while being registered under a different config name:

- `AscendOffloadingConnector` (config name `OffloadingConnector`)
- `UCMConnectorV1` (config name `UCMConnector`)

`AscendSimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (config name `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) does
not override `get_kv_connector_stats` and inherits the base no-op that returns
`None`, so it never enters this path and needs no alias. Likewise, connectors
that are registered under their own class name (e.g. `AscendStoreConnector`) are
unaffected.

A matching upstream guard against unknown connectors in
`MultiConnector.build_kv_connector_stats` is proposed separately in vLLM.

Fixes #16932

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API/interface change. It restores KV transfer stats for the two connectors
above (previously lost) and prevents an EngineCore crash. The alias names are
not intended to be used as `kv_connector` config values.

### How was this patch tested?

- New regression test
  `tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_connector_registration.py` asserts both
  aliases are registered. It fails without the source change and passes with it.
- Related existing tests:

  ```
  pytest tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/ tests/ut/simple_kv_offload/test_simple_kv_offload.py
  ```

  → 46 passed, 28 subtests passed.
- `bash format.sh ci` equivalent (pre-commit on the changed files) passes:
  ruff-check, ruff-format, codespell, typos, gitleaks and the local hooks.

Environment: CPU UT (vllm 0.28.0, torch 2.13.0+cpu); NPU paths are mocked per
`tests/ut/conftest.py`.

title: [Feature][CPP] Support async scheduling on Model Runner V2
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds asynchronous scheduling support for Chunked Pipeline Parallelism (CPP) on Model Runner V2.

- Introduces `ProfilingChunkAsyncScheduler`, preserving CPP chunk scheduling while integrating vLLM async placeholder accounting and the MRV2 pipeline-parallel decode cadence.
- Selects the async CPP scheduler when CPP and `--async-scheduling` are enabled together.
- Disables online wall-clock calibration in async mode while retaining startup profiling.
- Supports the Short Request First waiting queue with the async CPP scheduler.
- Rejects CPP async scheduling on Model Runner V1 with a clear configuration error because its PP execution path does not provide the required async sampled-token cadence and broadcast guarantees.
- Updates the CPP documentation and adds unit/E2E coverage.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can enable CPP together with `--async-scheduling` when using Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Attempting this combination with Model Runner V1 now fails during configuration with an actionable error.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added scheduler unit coverage in `tests/ut/core/test_profiling_chunk.py`.
- Added platform configuration coverage in `tests/ut/test_platform.py`.
- Updated the four-card CPP performance E2E coverage in `tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/test_profiling_chunk_performance.py`.

title: [Feature][MoE] Improve shared expert multistream overlap for quantized paths
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up to #15352.
Refs #15353.

The shared-expert registered-linear-wrapper path currently waits for `router_output_ready` before invoking the wrapper. For runtime-quantized linear methods, the wrapper owns both Vector/AIV activation preparation and the Cube-heavy matmul, so the wait also delays quantization that could overlap the routed Router Gate.

This PR introduces a scheme-owned `PreparedLinearInput` contract and `prepare_input_for_overlap()` capability. Eligible schemes prepare Gate-Up activation inputs before `router_output_ready`, while the Gate-Up matmul remains after that wait. After the shared activation, the same hook prepares the Down input before `routed_combine_start`, allowing Down quantization to overlap routed GMM2 while the Cube-heavy Down matmul remains behind the combine milestone. Quantization-specific padding, scale algorithms, output dtype, and transforms remain owned by the registered scheme.

For the internal router, FP32 input preparation is separated from the Gate linear and shared_input_ready is recorded between them. Shared Vector/AIV preparation therefore starts after the activation Cast and overlaps the Router Cube MatMul instead of competing with the Cast. External-router behavior is unchanged.
Existing CV scheduling remains milestone-driven: Gate-Up still follows `router_output_ready`, activation and requantization follow the backend-selected `shared_activation_overlap_start`, and the Down matmul still follows `routed_combine_start`. Regular MC2 and All2All publish the semantic activation milestone after dispatch, giving shared Vector/AIV work the routed GMM1 plus GMM2 Cube window. AllGather continues to publish the routed GMM2 boundary, while FusedMC2 preserves the event-free fallback. The fused A8 INT/MXFP and registered-linear-wrapper paths consume the same semantic milestone.

Covered schemes:
- W8A8 dynamic/static, W8A8 FP8 dynamic, W8A8 MXFP8, and W8A8 PDMix;
- W4A8 MXFP;
- W4A4 MXFP4, MXFP4 FlatQuant, FlatQuant, and LAOS;
- FP8 Block when it delegates to MXFP8 on A5.

A16, dense, unsupported shapes, non-MX FP8 Block, and active LoRA preserve the original fully wrapped path.

No communication-backend branching is added to the shared-expert executor. Each routed backend maps its preferred stage boundary to the same `shared_activation_overlap_start` semantic milestone.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No public API or configuration change. When shared-expert multistream overlap is enabled, eligible registered quantization wrappers may enqueue activation preparation earlier; numerical operators and checkpoint formats are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Static validation on the current host:
- `ruff format --check` on all changed Python files — passed.
- `ruff check` on all changed Python files — passed.
- `python -m compileall -q` on all changed modules and tests — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Added unit tests covering both the shared-linear scheduling order and the internal-router order `Cast -> shared_input_ready -> Router MatMul -> router_output_ready`:
`prepare Gate-Up input -> wait router_output_ready -> Gate-Up -> wait shared_activation_overlap_start -> activation -> prepare Down input -> wait routed_combine_start -> Down`.

The targeted pytest command could not collect because the local matching upstream vLLM checkout requires the `openai` package, which is not installed on this host:
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai'`.

Real Ascend NPU accuracy, profiling, and performance validation are pending and will be added when the hardware environment is available.

title: [Performance][Triton][Ascend] Adaptive calculation of ROW_BLOCK_SIZE in triton_q_rms for improved performance
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`triton_q_rms` currently uses a hardcoded `BLOCK_M` derived from `ROW_BLOCK_SIZE = 16`, which is a safe default but does not adapt to different hidden sizes (`dim`) or activation dtypes. This leaves the Unified Buffer (UB, 192 KB on Ascend A2/A3) either underutilized (small `dim`) or at risk of UB overflow (large `dim`).

This PR replaces the hardcoded constant with an **adaptive BLOCK_M calculation**:

```python
available_ub_size = get_ub_size_bytes() - resv_buffer  # reserve buffer 6KB to prevent UB overflow
element_size = element_size()                                      # bytes per element (e.g. 2 for bf16)

# data_multiplier accounts for intermediate tensors in flight:
#   fp32: input(4bytes) + offsets(4bytes) + mid_out(4bytes) + output(4bytes) + others(4bytes) = 5x
#   fp16/bf16: input(2bytes) +offsets(4bytes) + mid_out(4bytes) + output(2bytes) + others(2bytes) = 7x
data_multiplier = 5 if element_size == 4 else 7

ROW_BLOCK_SIZE = int(available_ub_size / (dim * element_size * data_multiplier ))
raw = min(ROW_BLOCK_SIZE, batch_per_core)
BLOCK_M = 1 << (raw.bit_length() - 1)   # ≤ raw power-of-two
```

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No. This is an internal performance optimization for triton_rms_kernel.

### How was this patch tested?

**performance:**
| cases | input shape (bs, head_num, dim) | BLOCK_M before opt | BLOCK_M after opt | time before opt(us) | time after opt(us) | Gains (speedup) |
|-------|-----------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|-------|
| 1 | (100, 256, 64) | 16 | 128 | 24.34 | 10.2 | 2.39x |
| 2 | (100, 256, 128) | 16 | 64| 22.87 | 12.28 | 1.86x |
| 3 | (100, 256, 256) | 16 | 32| 25.52 | 20.02 | 1.27x |
| 4 | (100, 256, 512) | 16 | 16| 36.09 | 36.20 | - |
| 5 | (100, 256, 1024) | 16 | 8| UB overflow | 72.20 | √ | 
| 6 | (100, 256, 2048) | 16 | 4| UB overflow | 145.72 | √ |

title: [Ops][Misc] Performance tuning for rms_norm_cast kernel
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

The fused `rms_norm_cast` kernel (RMSNorm producing both the low-precision `y` and the widened `y_fp32` consumed by HashTopK routing) previously serialized MTE2 load → vector compute → MTE3 store per row, and stalled the issuing thread on a per-row scalar round trip (V_S/GetValue/S_V) to fetch rstd. The fused op was therefore slower than the unfused `torch_npu.npu_rms_norm` + `Tensor.float()` sequence at ≥512 tokens despite moving ~20% less data.

This PR restructures the kernel:

- **Row pipelining**: double-buffered x / fp32 slots with a one-row MTE2 prefetch and asynchronous MTE3 stores; `y` rides the x slot so neither copy pipe blocks the vector critical path. Vector-pipe utilization rises from 61% to 91%.
- **Vector-pipe rstd broadcast**: `Gather` replicates rstd into a 32B block and a stride-0 `Mul` applies it — an in-pipe dependency replacing the scalar round trip (bit-identical numerics; the issuing thread never stalls mid-row).
- **Fewer vector passes**: 1/N folded into the post-reduction scalar; gamma widened once per core (bf16 path) instead of per row.
- **Safe event handling**: event ids via `AllocEventID`/`SetFlag`/`WaitFlag`/`ReleaseEventID` (the TQue pattern); flags are raised only when their consumer exists, leaving zero dangling SetFlags at kernel exit.
- **tiling**: per-dtype UB budget (22 B/col bf16, 18 B/col fp16 + 352 B fixed).

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. Outputs are numerically identical — `y_fp32 == y.float()` holds bitwise and is asserted per test case.

### How was this patch tested?

- The existing `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_rms_norm_cast.py` (8 cases) passes on Ascend 910B3 with CANN 9.1.0.
- Latency (NPUGraph replay, hidden=7168, vs the previous kernel):

| tokens | bf16 before → after | fp16 before → after |
|---|---|---|
| 512 | 23.2 → 16.7 µs (-28%) | 22.3 → 16.3 µs (-27%) |
| 1024 | 42.1 → 29.0 µs (-31%) | 40.1 → 28.1 µs (-30%) |
| 2048 | 91.2 → 54.9 µs (-40%) | 87.9 → 54.5 µs (-38%) |
| 4096 | 208.2 → 176.4 µs (-15%) | 203.6 → 182.4 µs (-10%) |

At 2048 tokens the kernel is ~29% faster than the unfused `npu_rms_norm` + `float()` reference; decode shapes (1–16 tokens) are unchanged within noise.

title: [WIP][Moe] Support Kimi K3 MegaMoe (SiTU activation + EP128 + W4A8 scale normalization) on main
body:
WIP follow-up adaptation of #15872 (Kimi K3 MegaMoe) onto current main (base: 44518f429).

Carries the adaptation and fixes we validated while bringing up K3 W4A8 MegaMoe on A3 with CANN 9.2.0:

1. **Adaptation of #15872 onto main**:
   - `moe_utils.py`: SiTU -> `situglu` activation mapping (`get_cann_mega_moe_activation_settings`), coexisting with the MiniMax swigluoai `select_mega_moe_activation_kwargs` probe already on main.
   - `ascend_forward_context.py`: MegaMoe EP whitelist extended to 128 (`_CANN_MEGAMOE_SUPPORTED_EP_SIZES`) and tokens-per-rank limit raised to 16384.
   - `moe_comm_method.py`: MegaMoe W4A8 path wiring (enable_fused_mc2 == 2 semantics, fused dispatch+combine), situ support gated on `activation == "situglu"` so the swigluoai path is untouched.
   - `w4a8.py` / `ascend_config.py`: K3 W4A8 per-expert scale normalization ([N,1] F32, 896 experts / EP64 = 14 per rank).

title: [Test][Ops] Fix and stabilize Triton RoPE kernel for test_rope
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Running `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_rope.py` on Ascend 910B encountered several stability, correctness, and compiler issues:

1. **FP16 SISO 100% Mismatch (Diff = 0.0)**: In `test_rotary_embedding_triton_kernel_siso`, unbounded values from `torch.randn` for `cos`/`sin` exceeded the \([-1, 1]\) range. Within the narrow dynamic range of `float16`, multi-dimensional matrix operations accumulated into `Inf` and subsequently `NaN`. Because \(NaN \neq NaN\), PyTorch reported a 100% mismatch with a difference of 0.0.
2. **BiShengIR Compiler Crash on FP8**: `test_rotary_embedding_triton_kernel_fp8` failed during Triton JIT compilation with `MLIRCompilationError` (`LLVM ERROR: unsupported datatype for arith::TruncFOp to hfusion`). The current Ascend BiShengIR backend lacks lowering support for `arith::TruncFOp` to FP8.

#### Key Changes:
- **Stabilize Numerical Range**: Bound `cos` and `sin` generation strictly within \([-1, 1]\) on CPU using real trigonometric functions (`torch.sin`/`torch.cos` over phase angles), and scale input tensor variance (`* 0.1`) before copying to NPU to avoid intermediate accumulation overflow.
- **Isolate Device Execution**: Removed `torch.set_default_device(device)` and standardized the workflow: generate inputs on CPU \(\rightarrow\) transfer to NPU \(\rightarrow\) execute kernel \(\rightarrow\) move outputs back to CPU for `torch.testing.assert_close`.
- **Compiler & Hardware Constraint Guards**:
  - Enabled `pytest.skip` for the FP8 RoPE test case with detailed documentation on the BiShengIR `arith::TruncFOp` compiler limitation.
  - Guarded unsupported non-power-of-2 `rotary_dim` (alignment constraints) and GPT-J style (`is_neox_style=False`) to avoid exceeding the 910B physical 192KB Unified Buffer (UB) limit.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This change only updates the test harness and fixtures in `test_rope.py`, introducing no changes to public APIs or runtime inference behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

1. Executed the affected Triton unit tests locally on an Ascend NPU environment:
   ```bash
   pytest -sv --noconftest tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_rope.py

`test_mla_preprocess_nq.py` passed 4-D NZ-shaped caches while selecting `cache_mode="krope_ctkv"`, which is an ND cache mode. title: [Test][Ops] Fix MLA preprocess QDown test cache layouts
body:
## Why

`test_mla_preprocess_qdown.py` constructed both cache modes with 4-D NZ-like tensors and sized query outputs from the physical cache trailing axes. For `krope_ctkv`, the host expects an ND cache; for `nzcache`, the physical C1 axis must be derived from the logical dimension without multiplying by the query head count.

The mismatched shapes made host tiling derive incorrect block and RoPE dimensions and allowed the kernel to write beyond the undersized query buffers. The asynchronous device fault then surfaced at a later synchronization point as error 507015.

## What

- Build `krope_ctkv` caches as ND `[block_num, block_size, dim]` tensors.
- Build `nzcache` caches as physical NZ `[block_num, dim // 16, block_size, 16]` tensors.
- Allocate query outputs from `kv_lora_rank` and `rope_dim` rather than physical cache axes.
- Initialize outputs with NaN sentinels, synchronize explicitly, assert each expected output is written, and remove the skip.

## Notes

- Verified repeatedly on the same Ascend NPU environment; all cache-mode and RoPE parameter combinations pass:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_mla_preprocess_qdown.py
```

title: [Feature] Add FLA RecurrentGDN Backend
body:
### Overview
This change introduces a switchable backend for the GDN decode recurrent operator. A new configuration item, `gdn_decode_backend1`, allows selection between `fla_npu` and native custom operators. The mechanism covers all three decode paths:

| Path | Location |
| :--- | :--- |
| 2.1 MTP spec decode | `AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention.forward` spec branch |
| 2.2 Mixed-batch non-spec decode | `split_non_spec` decode branch |
| 2.3 Prefill chunk / pure decode | non-spec branch |

### Performance
We conducted tests across 50 scenarios at the single-operator level, comparing the performance of operators in the fla package against the original recurrent operators. For recurrent_gated_delta_rule, the fla implementation reduced the average latency from 538us to 148us.

### How to use
Add extra addtional-config : `vllm serve xxx --additional-config '"gdn_decode_backend1": "fla_npu"`

title: [Feature][KV Pool] Enable GLM-5.3-Flash non-layerwise pooling
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable GLM-5.3-Flash non-layerwise KV pooling with its mixed NoPE MLA, compressed indexer, request-private circular tails and TP-sharded KDA state. Private tails must not participate in prefix hashing or pool transfer, and an empty RoPE view must not be registered at address zero.

Reworks #16854 on current main, with the original author credited through `Co-authored-by: Pz1116 <zpbzpb123123@gmail.com>`.

- Exclude non-prefix-cacheable groups while preserving group-indexed slots and existing key formats.
- Resume full-prefix hits at a complete page/state boundary so the request-private tail can be rebuilt.
- Preserve shared MLA keys, per-rank KDA payloads and all-rank hit checks.

Scope is GLM-specific KV pooling adaptation. Quantization loading, MTP implementation, native SFA operators, PD environment fixes and acceptance instrumentation are outside this PR.

Common hybrid KV-load failure recovery is explicitly out of scope. This PR does not patch the upstream scheduler or change baseline synchronous/asynchronous hybrid invalid-block reporting. The baseline hybrid load-failure limitation remains unresolved and will be handled separately; this PR does not claim safe failure recovery.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Enables GLM-5.3-Flash non-layerwise pooling with the hybrid cache manager enabled and `--mamba-cache-mode align`.

Memcache layerwise support is a separate dependent PR. Upstream Mooncake layerwise restrictions for recurrent Mamba/KDA state remain unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

**This branch, updated to Ascend main `0003e1b75b8ff4d35a5871fee1b2e9e7860bc3f1`:**

No installed packages or running service sources were replaced.

title: [Feature][Model] Support DeepSeek V4 Vision with DSA-CP
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds DeepSeek V4 Vision support to the legacy MRV1 DSA context-parallel path after the base Vision support landed in #15457.

The regular DSA metadata builder already creates bidirectional sliding-window indices for image spans. The DSA-CP builder did not carry those indices into its rank-local metadata, so Vision requests with `additional_config.enable_dsa_cp=true` lost the image-aware attention mask.

This change:

- builds the global Vision SWA indices from `mm_req_doc_ranges` in the legacy DSA-CP metadata builder;
- pads and slices them to the token range owned by each TP rank;
- forwards the rank-local indices to the DSA attention operator;
- fixes MRV1 DP graph padding so padded request slots reuse the last cumulative token offset instead of repeating the real scheduled-token vector. The old behavior can produce a source/destination shape mismatch while capturing a padded FULL_DECODE graph.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek V4 Vision can now be served with the legacy MRV1 DSA-CP path by setting `additional_config.enable_dsa_cp=true`.

title: [BugFix] Add off-stride graph capture size ceilings
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix off-stride default CUDAGraph capture sizes on Ascend. Fixes #16049 .

When `max_num_seqs` is not on the default capture-size grid, the largest decode batches could fall back to eager execution. This change preserves Ascend's reduced capture ceiling for memory savings while adding the exact ceiling to the capture-size list before upstream finalizes the graph configuration.

For example, `max_num_seqs=77` now produces a capture size of 77 and dispatches the largest decode batch to a FULL graph.

## Why this approach?

The exact ceiling is added while reusing upstream capture-size generation and filtering, so Ascend does not duplicate the upstream size-grid logic. Rounding the ceiling to 8/16, as in PR #16692, leaves the padded graph unreachable for FULL decode; duplicating the grid logic, as in PR #16623, increases long-term maintenance cost.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new configuration option is introduced. Off-stride default decode batches can now use CUDAGraphs instead of falling back to eager execution.

## How was this patch tested?

- `tests/ut/test_platform.py`
- A/B configuration and dispatcher check with `max_num_seqs=77`
- Baseline: capture sizes ended at 72 and batch 77 dispatched to `NONE`
- Fixed: capture sizes include 77 and batch 77 dispatched to `FULL`
- Result: `93 passed, 1 skipped`

title: [CPP][Spec Decode] Disable profiling chunk for draft models
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR prevents Chunked Pipeline Parallelism (CPP) profiling-chunk configuration from being applied to speculative draft models.

Draft models used by MTP, EAGLE, DSpark, and the 310P MTP path should not inherit the target model's profiling-chunk settings. Applying CPP to those draft models can create an unsupported scheduler configuration during speculative decoding. The target model keeps its CPP configuration; only the draft-model configuration is disabled.

The PR also separates CPP-enabled speculative-decoding E2E cases from the base MTP/DSpark tests so failures are isolated and both configurations retain independent coverage.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Speculative decoding with CPP no longer enables profiling chunk on the draft model, avoiding unsupported draft-model scheduling while preserving CPP on the target model.

title: [Feature][Sample] Add Triton apply_top_k_top_p fused op for sampling
body:
## What

A Triton implementation of top-k/top-p filtering for the sampler, opt-in via `VLLM_ASCEND_USE_TRITON_APPLY_TOPK_TOPP=1` (default off). Two entry points:

- `apply_top_k_top_p` — masked logits, bit-exact with `torch_npu.npu_top_k_top_p` (`torch.equal` on fp32/bf16/fp16)
- `fused_topk_topp_softmax` — same filtering with the final softmax folded into the kernel, returns fp32 probs directly; this is the branch the sampler uses when logprobs are not requested

Both take the per-request `[B]` k/p tensors from `_get_topk_topp_constraints()` as-is. The CANN op forces a `.item()` on that tensor (host sync on every decode step); this op doesn't.

## How it works

The host does the sort once (`torch.sort`, ascending, stable) and the kernel only works on the sorted row. Because the input is ascending, both the top-k mask (`s >= topk_value`) and the top-p mask (`cumsum > 1 - p`) are suffix-monotone, so the kept set collapses to a single scalar boundary `m = max(m_p, m_k)` per row. The kernel then only scatters the surviving suffix (~k elements) into a pre-filled output — the non-surviving positions are one contiguous block write instead of V random stores.

I used a scalar boundary rather than a cumsum-derived boolean vector as the scatter mask on purpose: triton-ascend 3.2.2 miscompiles that pattern (the store collapses to a few elements). The `v >= m` comparison mask sidesteps it.

![kernel flow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/kernel_flow.png)

Two kernel paths: V ≤ 4096 loads the row in one block; larger vocabularies go tiled — pass 1 accumulates the softmax denominator, pass 2 walks tiles until the cumulative probability crosses `1 - p` (early exit; `tl.cumsum` runs only inside the crossing tile), pass 3 only touches the kept suffix. `m_p`/`m_k` can be looser than the exact CANN cutoffs; the final `v >= m` mask restores exactness, so the output stays bit-exact.

The sampler wiring prefers logprobs-preserving paths: when `raw_logprobs` is requested it falls back to the masked-logits variant + separate softmax/log_softmax.

## Enabling it

With `VLLM_ASCEND_USE_TRITON_APPLY_TOPK_TOPP=1` the sampler logs once at startup:

![switch log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/enable_log.png)

## Performance

Test environment: single Ascend 910B3 (linux aarch64), CANN 9.0.0, torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, triton-ascend 3.2.2. Model: `Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8` (w8a8-quantized, vocab 151936). Serving benchmark command (identical for both runs):

```bash
vllm bench serve --model $MODEL_PATH --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 \
    --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 300 --request-rate 10 \
    --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --temperature 0.6 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl
```

E2E serving benchmark, stock vs this PR (300/300 successful requests, identical total input/output tokens; 存量=stock, 改造后=this PR):

![serving bench](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/serving_bench.png)

## Accuracy

![triton acc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/acc_triton.png)
![stock acc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/15625122759/vllm-ascend/pr-assets/docs/pr17211/acc_stock.png)

## Tests

- `op/test_smoke.py` + `op/op_perf_test.sh`: 10-case matrix, fp32/bf16, single-pass + tiled paths, per-row k/p tensor and scalar inputs, k<0/k=0/k>V edge cases, determinism; bit-exact (`torch.equal`) vs `torch_npu.npu_top_k_top_p` + 20 randomized stress cases (N=1…1e5)
- `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_apply_top_k_top_p.py`: 6 smoke cases incl. V=32000 tiled and per-row tensors
- ruff/mypy clean

Note on CI: `pre-commit` currently fails on `vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite.py:663` (`XModelConfig has no attribute index_full_mask`) — that's pre-existing on main since #16669; `tools/mypy.sh` type-checks the whole package so it fires on any PR. Nothing in this PR's files is flagged.

## Known limitations

- `tl.cumsum` lowers to an element-serial runtime call on triton-ascend 3.2.2 (~29.7us per 2048-wide tile vs ~0.2us for `tl.sum`, measured). The tiled kernel only runs it inside the single threshold-crossing tile, so the impact is small, but it would be nice to have a tree-scan lowering in the backend.
- The host-side `torch.sort` (~100-470us depending on B/V) stays. Callers that already hold sorted logits can use the `*_with_sorted` variants and skip it.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c
