title: [Feature][Attention] Add A5 FlashMLA BF16 and C8 model execution
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add the A5 FlashMLA BF16/C8 reader and its real dense-MLA model execution path. **Depends on #17198 (shared A5/C8 headers and FlashAttn prefill), #17297 (DCP exchange/combine helpers), and #17298 (output gate/masking).** Those implementations are deliberately not copied here; this PR is a separate review unit and is not independently mergeable before its dependencies. #17190 is an optional MLAPO preprocessing optimization, selected only when its operators are available.

The implementation includes:

- Native BF16/C8 paged reader, AICPU schedule producer, compressed-cache gather and BF16 prefill preparation, with PrivateUse1/Meta bindings and A5 build entries. C8 reuses the shared pipeline in #17198.
- Actual `AscendMLAImpl.forward` routing through BF16 decode, C8 quantized history, BF16 current chunks, DCP output merge, bounded expanded prefill and mixed decode/prefill. C8 query/KV scales come from the existing quantization contract. Optional MLAPO operator bodies are not part of this PR.
- Isolated Flash metadata helpers, graph-stable buffers populated from device lengths, and MRv1/MRv2 cache/spec/metadata/zeroing integration. FP8 latent and BF16 positional planes preserve manager page padding and neighboring storage.
- Kimi replicated-Q projection wiring and dense-MLA draft capture/replay integration. GQA and recurrent-state cache layouts retain their existing paths. No Conv1d, EPLB, KDA, PP scheduling or output-projection operator changes are included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The opt-in `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASH_MLA=1` enables the backend for dense MLA; default is `0`. The supported model contract is BF16 activations, latent width 512, positional width 64, one KV head, BF16 or calibrated FP8 E4M3 cache, and PCP1. Kernel pages are 128 tokens. Kimi TP8/DCP8 selects replicated Q before weight loading.

The normal projection/quantization C8 path remains usable without the optional MLAPO package. No end-to-end throughput or native accuracy result is claimed from CPU validation.

CPU coverage executes production Python methods with emulated collectives/native operators, checks quantization and history/current orchestration, cache planes/offsets/zeroing boundaries, metadata ownership, mixed batches and ordinary projection when MLAPO is unavailable. It does not validate device kernel arithmetic.

title: [KV Pool][BugFix] Synchronize MemCache initialization across DP workers
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

When MemCache workers initialize at different speeds, an early DP rank can proceed to NPU work while peers are still establishing their MemCache channels. Add a CPU process-group barrier after successful MemCache store initialization so workers in the same DP group finish that step before proceeding.

Read the option with the other connector settings in `AscendStoreConnector`, pass it through `KVPoolWorker`, and perform the synchronization in `MemcacheBackend._setup_store()`. Skip the barrier for DP size 1, metadata-only scheduler clients, and actual lazy initialization. Lazy initialization is request-driven and DP ranks may enter it independently; a collective there could block a rank waiting for idle peers. When a backend ignores a lazy initialization request and initializes eagerly, keep the startup barrier. Cover initialization ordering, configuration propagation, opt-out, invalid values, initialization failure, and lazy initialization without a barrier and eager fallback synchronization in unit tests.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `kv_connector_extra_config.memcache_dp_init_barrier` is a boolean that defaults to `true` for the MemCache backend. Set it to `false` to disable the synchronization. With `MultiConnector`, configure it on the `AscendStoreConnector` child. For eager initialization, all ranks in a DP group must use the same value and reach initialization. Stores using lazy initialization skip the barrier even when the option is enabled.

### How was this patch tested?

Ran the following tests inside a newly created Linux container based on `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-releases-v0.27.1rc-a5-openeuler`, using the modified Ascend source and the vLLM revision recorded in `.github/vllm-main-verified.commit`:

```bash
python3 -m pytest \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_backend.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_ascend_store_connector.py \
  tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py -q
```

Result: **232 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, with 14 PyTorch deprecation warnings. The image's original vLLM revision was incompatible with the current Ascend test setup; the test container used the pinned vLLM source below instead.

Changed-file Ruff lint/format checks, Markdownlint 0.45.0, and `git diff --cached --check` passed. GitHub CI passed the pre-commit hooks and Gitleaks scan on the previous revision. Its separate mypy step exposed six Python 3.10 incompatibilities in the new tests (`TestCase.enterContext`). The tests now use `ExitStack.enter_context` with `addCleanup(stack.close)` instead, and all 232 container unit tests pass again. The updated CI type-check result is pending.

These are mocked unit tests. End-to-end model serving and actual multi-rank MemCache synchronization have not been validated for this config-based patch.


- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

title: [Feature][Attention] MRV2 external FlashMLA on strided BBND cache with MLA DSpark
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This draft wires external FlashMLA metadata generation and attention execution into MRV2 target inference and MLA DSpark draft inference, while retaining the token-fused, non-contiguous BBND KV cache from #16456. Eager and FULL_DECODE_ONLY use the same operator path. This is a candidate for NPU integration testing, not a validated NPU implementation.

**Dependency: #16456 must land first.** Its source branch is in another fork, so this draft targets `main` and temporarily includes its cache changes. After that PR lands, rebase this PR to leave only the operator integration and rerun validation. MRV2 DSpark #16347 is already present and is not merged again.

This continues the public [historical handoff Draft](https://github.com/Henry-Avery/vllm-ascend/pull/2) on a newer main/cache baseline. Current main's DSpark post-load weight alignment and graph APIs are retained; historical load-time rotation is not reapplied.

Candidate commit: `2ec47279b60f674d4dcd43a7b8becd190434b8bd`.

Pinned inputs:

- Ascend main: `fde460648b159410eac68f4d32fec97587cc8f3d`.
- #16456: `4839002d74a5cac8965a5dfee11c627442bdaa79`.
- Combined baseline: `c8ca7b135f4cd989dd4367ac81919c7759be5514`.
- Paired vLLM: `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`.
- At publication, main has one later CI/bisect revert (`79eeed81c`); this candidate retains the pinned runtime baseline.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Opt in with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` and `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASH_MLA=1` (FlashMLA is off by default).

- Both stages import `flash_mla_with_kvcache_metadata` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` from **`cann_ops_transformer.ops`**. The adapter does not call the in-tree `_C_ascend.flash_mla*` bindings or fall back to FIA when the external package is absent. Other Ascend operators may still use the in-tree extension.
- Both stages pass `max_seqlen_q=-1,max_seqlen_kv=-1`. The main operator uses `TND / PA_BBND / NTD`, actual TP-local Q heads in `{8,12,64,96}`, and QK/V dimensions 576/512.
- Preserve #16456 cache strides, storage offsets, page tables, slots, allocation, COW and zeroing. Write into original 512/64 component views without repacking persistent KV.
- Target and draft own separate schedules/buffers; device lengths and padding are refreshed outside graph capture/replay, with producer waits and consumer reuse fences. Keep V-up, gate, O-proj and non-MLA backends.
- Initial scope: A5, MRV2 dense MLA, BF16 KV, PCP/DCP=1, PP=1, no PD/KVPP. DCP helpers are preparatory only. TP4 requires both actual checkpoints' head geometry and memory capacity to fit; there is no replicated-head workaround.

The Chinese runbook is in `docs/flash_mla_mrv2.md`. The reference launcher is `examples/flash_mla_dspark.py`: target-only / DSpark, eager / graph, `--dry-run`, and `--preflight-only`. Preflight prints installed module/function paths and versions and probes the external Meta implementation; it does not certify NPU kernel dispatch or numerical correctness. No operator wheel is bundled.

Example (replace paths and the draft token count with checkpoint-specific values):

```bash
python examples/flash_mla_dspark.py \
  --target-model /path/to/target --draft-model /path/to/mla-draft \
  --num-speculative-tokens 5 --mode graph \
  --devices 0,1,2,3 --tp 4 --draft-tp 4 --dry-run
```

On the NPU host: inspect package/schema with `--preflight-only`, then test target eager, target + MLA draft eager, and the same inputs in graph mode. Checkpoints may require additional weight-quantization arguments; KV remains BF16.

### How was this patch tested?

Local host: macOS arm64, Python 3.12, CPU torch 2.8.0.

```bash
python -m unittest \
  tests.ut.attention.test_flash_mla_host_contract \
  tests.ut.spec_decode.test_flash_mla_dspark_host_contract \
  tests.ut.worker.test_flash_mla_integration_host_contract -v
```

- 40 CPU/mock tests passed. Coverage includes device length correction, context KV writes, padding/masks, target/draft ownership, stable buffers, executor fences, graph refresh/replay routing and single post-load alignment.
- An added test supplies in-tree FlashMLA bindings that fail if called: metadata and attention still use the external package; missing external entries raise rather than falling back.
- 4 #16456 lifecycle cases passed in an isolated CPU harness with actual worker methods/test bodies. Fix only the fixture's byte-count/BF16-element-count mismatch and per-subpage COW expectation; production allocator/COW/zeroing code is unchanged.
- Four launcher dry-run combinations and eight invalid-input cases passed; no NPU package was loaded and no service was started for these checks.
- Scoped lint/format, compile checks, whitespace checks and applicable pre-commit checks (including staged gitleaks) passed locally.

**Still unvalidated:** the installed external operator package on NPU, real scatter/RoPE/Triton execution, full vLLM import/build, checkpoint loading, numerical correctness, DSpark acceptance/rejection, graph capture/replay, collectives, four-card K3 service, and performance. CPU zeroer checks validate metadata only. A listening server or an importable package is not acceptance evidence.

title: [Feature][KV offload] Add fused lightning indexer manage and fused scatter copy sparse flash attention operators for sparse KV cache offloading.
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds two standalone AscendC custom operators for large-sequence sparse
KV cache offloading scenarios:

- `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`
- `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`

Together, the two operators cover the operator-level workflow from Lightning
Indexer TopK selection and sparse-cache management to missing-KV scatter copy
and sparse flash attention.

#### `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`

This operator performs the following operations in a single NPU invocation:

- Lightning Indexer TopK retrieval;
- initialization and steady-state eviction of the HBM sparse KV cache;
- TopK union management for multiple MTP query routes;
- cache-hit and cache-miss classification;
- generation of cache-miss source IDs and destination HBM slots.

A single batch may contain mixed request states:

- non-offload requests (`request_state = -3`);
- first-offload requests (`request_state = -2`);
- steady-state offload requests (`request_state = -1`).

Each request supports 1 to 14 query routes. The operator maintains the
persistent mapping from source token IDs to HBM logical slots through
`cache_slots_pool`.

The current implementation supports:

- FLOAT16 and BFLOAT16;
- 32 and 64 index heads;
- a fixed index head dimension of 128;
- a fixed TopK size of 2048;
- a cache block size of 128;
- source capacity up to `2^21`;
- Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products.

`query_dequant_scale` and `index_key_dequant_scale` are reserved inputs in the
current implementation and are not consumed yet. Quantized Query and Index Key
dequantization will be supported in a follow-up change.

#### `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`

This operator combines missing-KV scatter copy and causal sparse flash
attention in a single public PyTorch custom-op call. It performs the following
operations:

- initialize the HBM sparse KV cache for first-fill requests;
- identify source-aware TopK cache misses during steady-state execution;
- scatter-copy missing KPE and CKV entries from DRAM to HBM;
- execute causal sparse flash attention over the requested TopK KV entries;
- support variable numbers of MTP query routes in the TND layout.

A single batch may contain:

- first-fill requests;
- steady-state requests containing cache hits and misses;
- requests with heterogeneous MTP query counts.

Each request supports 1 to 16 query routes, corresponding to MTP0 through
MTP15. The operator consumes the TopK slot and miss metadata produced by the
cache-management stage.

The current implementation supports:

- FLOAT16 and BFLOAT16;
- 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads;
- a fixed TopK size of 2048;
- a cache block size of 128;
- a 512-dimensional compressed KV representation;
- a 64-dimensional RoPE key representation;
- Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products.

The operator uses two execution paths selected from device-side metadata:

- first-fill path: an internal helper fills the HBM sparse cache before the
  attention kernel accesses it;
- steady-state path: missing KV entries are copied while sparse attention is
  executed.

The first-fill helper and the main fused kernel are launched on the same NPU
stream. The helper becomes a device-side no-op for steady-state requests. Path
selection does not read CPU data and supports ACLGraph Capture and Replay.

#### Main changes

- add the two fused AscendC operator implementations;
- add the conditional first-fill scatter-copy helper;
- add operator definitions, tiling implementations and inference functions;
- add shape, dtype, device, contiguity and dynamic-input validation;
- add ACLNN interfaces and PyTorch custom-op registration;
- add Meta implementations;
- enable the operators for Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products;
- add operator documentation and representative latency results;
- add standalone correctness and ACLGraph replay tests.

This PR only introduces the standalone operators and their operator-level
tests. Framework-side metadata construction, cache-manager integration and
model execution integration are not included and will be submitted separately.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

Two new PyTorch custom operators are exposed:

```python
torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_fused_lightning_indexer_manage(...)
torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention(...)
```

No existing API, model execution path or default behavior is changed. The new
operators are not connected to the vLLM model execution path in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

The operators were built and tested on an Ascend NPU environment.

Test environment:

- Device: Ascend 910_93
- CANN: 9.1.0
- npu-smi: 25.2.1
- OS: Linux
- Python: 3.12.13
- pytest: 8.3.2
- vLLM: `0.1.dev21135+g84030bbe3`

#### Lightning Indexer and cache-management tests

Test command:

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_lightning_indexer_manage.py
```

Test result:

```text
collected 105 items
105 passed, 14 warnings in 27.91s
```

The tests use `torch_npu.npu_lightning_indexer` as the TopK reference
implementation and cover:

- FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 and 32/64 index heads;
- all query route counts from Q1 to Q14;
- non-offload, first-offload and steady-state requests;
- mixed request states and lifecycle transitions;
- cache initialization, eviction, hit/miss classification and miss union;
- repeated invocation and all-hit convergence;
- miss-occurrence boundaries around 2048 and 4096;
- long source IDs from `2^17` to near the `2^21` upper limit;
- representative invalid shape, dtype, contiguity and query-count inputs.

All 105 correctness cases passed, including the Q14 state matrix, mixed-state
batch cases and long-sequence cases.

#### Scatter-copy sparse flash attention tests

Test command:

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention.py
```

The tests cover:

- FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 and 8/16/32/64/128 query heads;
- MTP0 and heterogeneous MTP2/MTP3/MTP8/MTP15 TND batches;
- steady-state fused scatter copy;
- first-fill requests and mixed-request batches;
- `attention_out` precision against a CPU reference;
- HBM KPE and CKV cache update correctness;
- ACLGraph Capture and Replay;
- switching from the captured steady-state path to the first-fill path through
  device-side metadata.

Representative latency results for both operators are included in their
respective README files. They are provided as reference data only and are not
used as test thresholds.

### End-to-end inference results

The operators were also evaluated end-to-end with GLM-5.2-w4a8 on Ascend 910C,
using TP16/EP16 and a 64K sequence length.

With the same batch size of 5, enabling KV cache offloading increases ITL only
from 73.56 ms to 78.42 ms, corresponding to a 6.6% degradation.

With KV cache offloading enabled, the batch size can be increased from 5 to 16.
In this configuration, ITL increases from 73.56 ms to 109.54 ms, while
throughput increases from 188 TPS to 406 TPS, corresponding to a 115%
throughput improvement.

The operator-level contributions are as follows:

* `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`: at batch size 5 without offloading, the
  total latency of the Lightning Indexer operators across all layers is
  2.89 ms. At batch size 5 with offloading, the total latency of the LIM
  operators across all layers is 6.83 ms, resulting in only a 3.94 ms
  increase in ITL.

* `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`: at batch size 16, with separate
  scatter-copy and sparse flash attention operators, the total scatter-copy
  latency across all layers is 11.75 ms and the total sparse flash attention
  latency is 18.81 ms. With the fused CopySFA operator, the total latency
  across all layers is 23.90 ms. Therefore, the fused operator reduces ITL by
  `11.75 + 18.81 - 23.90 = 6.66 ms`.

Compared with the first version of the fused operators, evaluated with 4
machines, 1P1D, 32 concurrent requests and a 29K sequence length, ITL is
reduced from 80 ms in the first version
([https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14278)) to 77.7 ms with the
current implementation, corresponding to a 2.3 ms ITL reduction. There is
still room for further optimization on the framework side.

Split the MiniMax-M3 A5 mixed KV-cache policy out of #16904 so it can land independently of the pending CANN operators.

Yes. MiniMax-M3 deployments on Ascend A5 that request FP8 KV cache will use BF16 KV cache for GQA layers. Other models, non-FP8 KV-cache configurations, and non-A5 devices are unchanged.

title: [MRV2][BugFix][Kernel] Fix and optimize sampling mask packing on Ascend
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is a backport of #17193 for the v0.28.0 release branch.

The sampling-mask kernel can overflow UB on Triton-Ascend when
`logits.stride(1) > 1`. For a batch-32, vocabulary-151936, stride-2
input, the original BLOCK_SIZE=8192 kernel fails compilation with:

`ub overflow, requires 12583424 bits while 1572864 bits available`

The implementation also has two Ascend-specific lowering issues:

- reducing the boolean keep mask does not produce the required finite-logit
  count;
- per-element variable shifts and the `[512, 8]` axis-1 reduction lower to
  scalar-heavy execution.

This PR adds an Ascend implementation for the sampling-mask API. It:

- makes only strided vocabulary inputs contiguous, without modifying the
  caller's tensor;
- casts the keep mask to int32 before reduction;
- uses BLOCK_SIZE=4096 to remain within the NPU UB limit;
- transposes the packing layout from `[512, 8]` to `[8, 512]`, multiplies by
  compile-time bit weights, and reduces axis 0;
- replaces `SamplingMaskTensors.from_logits` with the Ascend implementation;
- adds operator documentation and registers the NPU regression test in the
  A2 single-card nightly matrix.

The following msprof results use an Ascend 910, `npu:0`, 10 profiling
rounds, and `MemoryDetail,Occupancy,PipeUtilization,Roofline`. Values are
selected kernel task durations and exclude Python wrapper time and the
preceding contiguous copy.

| Case | Baseline | Optimized | Speedup | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `b1_v17_active1_colstride1` | 123.330 us | 5.640 us | 21.87x | 95.43% |
| `b8_v8191_active1_colstride1` | 244.573 us | 6.960 us | 35.14x | 97.15% |
| `b8_v8192_active1_colstride1` | 244.327 us | 6.680 us | 36.58x | 97.27% |
| `b8_v8193_active1_colstride1` | 365.349 us | 8.940 us | 40.87x | 97.55% |
| `b8_v8193_active0_colstride1` | 365.357 us | 8.780 us | 41.61x | 97.60% |
| `b32_v151936_active1_colstride2` | 4604.258 us | 84.758 us | 54.32x | 98.16% |
| `b128_v151936_active1_colstride1` | 18403.968 us | 327.093 us | 56.27x | 98.22% |

The original stride-2 BLOCK_SIZE=8192 implementation has no runtime
duration because it fails compilation with UB overflow. The table uses
the first compilable correctness-fixed implementation with the original
variable-shift packing as the performance baseline.

TTIR/NPU IR inspection confirms that the optimized packing lowers to
vector transpose, multiply, and reduction operations; the previous
tensor-wide scalar shift loop is absent.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

Correctness validation environment:

- Ascend 910
- Python 3.12.13
- Torch 2.10.0
- torch-npu 2.10.0.post4
- Triton-Ascend 3.2.2
- CANN 9.1.0

The NPU regression test passed against the vLLM v0.28.0 three-field
sampling-mask interface.

The regression test verifies:

- finite support sizes 0, 1, 7, 511, 512, 513, 2048, 2053, and the full vocabulary;
- random sparse token positions and a vocabulary size not divisible by eight;
- active and inactive rows, including `num_sampled_tokens > 1`;
- NaN and positive/negative infinity exclusion;
- non-contiguous `logits` with `stride(1) == 2` and an unmodified caller view;
- exact packed masks, counts, and decoded token IDs.

The regression is registered as the A2 single-card nightly case
`sampling-mask`.

The following repository checks passed:

- `bash format.sh`
- `python -m compileall`
- `git diff --check`
- `SHELLCHECK_OPTS="--exclude=SC2046,SC2006,SC2086" pre-commit run
  --all-files --hook-stage manual --show-diff-on-failure`

title: [BugFix] Fix SFA output projection TP for idle DP ranks
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix output-projection tensor parallelism (OTP) in the shared SFA path. When one DP rank has no requests, it must still contribute its projection weight shard to active ranks. Previously, the idle SFA path skipped those collectives; unequal decode graph buckets also produced incompatible exchange shapes.

- Keep idle SFA ranks in OTP collectives with empty local inputs.
- Exchange full DP inputs without sharding them twice, and use fixed-capacity communication buffers across graph capture/replay and uneven batches.
- Allow oversized profiling-only batches to participate with empty inputs while preserving their output shape.
- Preserve aliased SFA/Mamba cache pages and Conv-history offsets in PreemptOffloadConnector, which is required by the tested OTP deployment. This fixes GLM-5.3-Flash cache registration with the mandatory offload connector.

Refs #15665

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. SFA decode deployments using `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` can handle idle DP ranks and uneven batches, including GLM-5.3-Flash P/D serving. Existing configuration constraints remain in effect; no new option is added.

The shared SFA/OTP fix is also expected to apply to GLM-5.2 on the same execution path, but GLM-5.2 model-level validation is not claimed here.

### How was this patch tested?

- **296 unit tests passed** across the following commands, including regressions for idle ranks, uneven batches, stable collective buffers, profiling, and both shared-cache registration orders:

  ```bash
  python -m pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_linear.py tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2 tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_cache_config.py tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kv_cache.py tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kpool_model_backend.py
  python -m pytest -q tests/ut/kv_offload/test_preempt_offload_connector.py
  ```

- Real Ascend 910 NPU check: aliased-cache registration and selective Conv-history restore passed; unrelated state and padding were preserved.
- GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 on 16 Ascend A3 NPUs: **P TP8+EP8 → D TP1+DP8+EP8+OTP8**, MRV1, MooncakeConnectorV2 transfer, and MultiConnector with PreemptOffloadConnector on D. D used `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with capture sizes `[1,2,4,8,16]`, `max_num_seqs=16`, and `max_model_len=16384`. Five structured smoke requests passed, covering low concurrency, mixed-length concurrent requests, and resume after idle.
- Full **8-shot GSM8K: 1280/1319 (97.04%)**, temperature 0, 32 client workers, 10,240 generated-token cap, strict final `####` integer extraction. No HTTP or other client errors. Two length-limited incorrect answers are included in the score. The run had no preemptions; full-model preemption stress was not tested.
- Ruff check/format and `git diff --check` passed for the six changed files. No nightly case was added.

title: [Performance][Ops] Use fused rotary embedding for Gemma 4 global attention
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Gemma 4 global (full) attention RoPE currently falls back to native PyTorch on Ascend. vLLM's OOT registry dispatches by exact class name (`cls.__name__`), and `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding` (the `proportional` rope type) is not registered, so these layers never reach the Ascend fused rotary forward that sliding-attention layers already use.

This PR registers an adapter, `AscendGemma4RotaryEmbedding(Gemma4RotaryEmbedding, AscendRotaryEmbedding)`. Gemma4's constructor runs first and keeps its proportional frequencies (head-size exponents, zero-padded non-rotated pairs, `rotary_dim = head_size`), then the existing Ascend fused forward is reused unchanged. Non-rotated pairs have cos=1/sin=0 in the cache, so the full-head fused rotation is exact for them. Compatibility (310P) devices keep their current path.

Relation to #15332: that PR fuses split-QKV + RMSNorm + RoPE + V-norm for Gemma 4, but intentionally keeps the unfused chain on 950 (no A5 variant) and for KV-shared layers. Those paths still call `rotary_emb`, so this change is complementary.

Operator measurements on one Ascend 950PR, BF16, gemma-4-31B global-attention geometry (32 Q / 4 KV heads, head 512, `partial_rotary_factor=0.25`, 262144 positions), NPU graph replay with identical input clones in both paths:

| Tokens | Q+K native → fused (µs) | Query-only (KV-shared) native → fused (µs) |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 33.2 → 13.8 (2.41×) | 20.4 → 13.8 (1.48×) |
| 4 | 35.9 → 14.1 (2.55×) | 22.1 → 13.4 (1.64×) |
| 32 | 47.6 → 13.8 (3.45×) | 30.3 → 16.2 (1.88×) |
| 256 | 87.9 → 33.0 (2.67×) | 61.6 → 29.5 (2.09×) |
| 1024 | 278.8 → 83.2 (3.35×) | 226.8 → 77.2 (2.94×) |

These are operator measurements, not end-to-end throughput; only global-attention layers (about one in six in gemma-4-31B) use this rope type.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Gemma 4 global-attention layers use the existing Ascend fused RoPE. The cos/sin cache is bit-identical to upstream. The fused kernel uses FP32 intermediate arithmetic, so outputs are not bitwise equal to the native BF16 fallback; against an FP32 reference with the same cache, query relative L2 error is ~0.083% fused vs ~0.119% native. No additional cache memory: the module-level cache recorders keep the first (sliding-layer) cache.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests (`tests/ut/ops/test_rotary_embedding.py`, `tests/ut/test_utils.py`): constructor/frequency cases for partial (512/128) and full (256/256) rotary, cache recording, unchanged-signature check, and registration of `Gemma4RotaryEmbedding`. 18 passed against vLLM `84030bbe` (the verified main commit) on CPU.
- NPU test (`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_gemma4_rope.py`): 16 cases — BF16/FP16, 1/4/32/1024 tokens, Q+K and query-only, noncontiguous merged-QKV views, positions up to the cache end; checks the cache matches upstream exactly, outputs match an FP32 reference, and the 384 non-rotated dims pass through bit-exactly. All pass on 950PR.
- ruff check/format pass.

NPU runs used current-main `rotary_embedding.py`, `triton/rope.py`, `triton/triton_utils.py` and `envs.py` overlaid on an installed vllm-ascend 0.26.0rc1 / vLLM 0.26.0 stack (torch 2.10, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, CANN 9.1.0); the full current-main engine was not run.

`tests/ut/test_utils.py` touches the same registration test as #17374 (Llama 3 RoPE); whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

Developed with Claude Code assistance; reviewed and submitted by the author.

title: [Performance] Optimize DeepSeek-V4 VL embed_input_ids to remove per-step copies
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Profiling the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp deployment (`dsv4-vision-exp`) showed ~4ms of copy operations inside `embed_input_ids` on every scheduler step. The cause was that the sentinel-replacement path re-executed avoidable copies per forward: 1. `torch.stack([...]).to(inputs_embeds.dtype)` — the four `image_*` parameters are float32 while embeddings are bf16, so every step re-stacked and re-cast the sentinel vectors. 2. `sentinel_mask & ~is_multimodal.to(input_ids.device)` — `is_multimodal` lives on CPU in this stack, so every step performed an H2D copy of the mask plus a device AND. This exclusion is unnecessary: positions flagged `is_multimodal` are always overwritten afterwards by `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, so the table value written there is dead anyway. 3. `torch.where(...)` allocated a fresh full `seq_len x hidden` tensor per step on top of the `table[idx]` gather. Changes: - Cache the stacked sentinel table in the embedding dtype (`_get_sentinel_table`), built once per model instance and reused for the process lifetime. - Drop the redundant `& ~is_multimodal` exclusion and its per-step H2D copy (safe because `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` overwrites those positions afterwards). - Write the sentinel replacement in place via `torch.where(..., out=inputs_embeds)`, removing one full-sequence allocation per step.
